methods.title: Accounts Snapshot
methods.description: Return provider account posture.

methods.title: List Installed Third-Party Coding Agents
methods.description: READ-ONLY discovery of installed ACP-capable third-party coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, opencode): existence checks over $PATH and known install directories, no process is ever executed, no registration ceremony. Returns only what is present (id, title, resolved binary path, ACP launch args); absence is a quiet empty list, never a nag.

methods.title: Spawn a Third-Party Coding Agent Session
methods.description: Spawn a discovered third-party agent into a working directory as a hosted daemon session in ONE act: the binary is launched in ACP stdio mode, the handshake and session creation run under a bound timeout, and the result is the hosted record, which appears as a steerable/stoppable fleet row (kind acp-agent). Its permission asks are decided by the autonomous admission of the daemon against the current policy, never by a person, so a row is never waiting on a human; an ask that times out or cannot be decided is refused and shown as `lastRefusal`. A binary that fails the handshake returns the SAME record with state "failed" and a structured error (which binary, which stage, what happened), an honest outcome, never a hung row and never a bare string. An optional initial prompt starts the first turn.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Approve Approval
methods.description: Approve a pending approval. Optionally pass selectedHunks (edit-tool approvals only): the daemon filters the approval's own edit list to those hunk indices server-side, so every surface produces identical modified-edit args. Omitting selectedHunks approves the whole request (back-compat). An out-of-range index or a non-edit approval is rejected with a 400. rememberTier generalizes the decision (a generalizing tier persists a durable rule and sweeps queued asks it covers); modifiedArgs carries an argument-modifying approval, e.g. the typed answer to a command's terminal prompt, to the waiting call (selectedHunks supersedes it when both are present). The response's recorded block reports what the broker actually recorded. Every action sends `expectedRevision`, the `revision` of the approval it showed or read; without it the call is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. The answer is 200 with `applied`, the record and its `reading` for the caller as they are now; when `applied` is false, `refusal.code` says why: APPROVAL_SETTLED (it already ended; the first decision stands), APPROVAL_CHANGED (it moved since that revision: show the returned reading again and act on its revision), APPROVAL_EXPIRED (its deadline passed first; it is now expired), OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED (only the paired-owner decision on the device that raised it can approve it). Malformed `disposition`, `selectedHunks`, `rememberTier`, `reason` or `modifiedArgs`, a hunk index out of range and `remember` with an amendment are 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field; an unknown id is 404 APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND. Answering is your own act, from any of your credentials: the Agent's credential is refused 403 OWNER_ONLY (a model is acting with it), and so is a device whose stored scope list does not hold the right to answer.

errorCodes.meaning: A field is missing or not in its documented shape (the body names it in `field`); nothing was changed.
No approval has that id; nothing was answered.

Only you answer this approval, from any of your credentials: the Agent's credential never does (a model is acting with it), and a device whose stored scope list does not hold the right to answer does not. Nothing was answered.

methods.title: Cancel Approval
methods.description: Cancel a pending approval; send `expectedRevision`, the `revision` you read. An approval that already ended is answered `applied: false` with `refusal.code` APPROVAL_SETTLED, one that moved since with APPROVAL_CHANGED, each with the record and its current `reading`. A surface that raised the ask through approvals.raise gives up its hold with `release: true` and the `holdId` approvals.raise returned (no revision needed): while the ask waits, that means it left, and the ask is cancelled (`cancelled-requester-left`) only when no other surface that raised it still holds it; once it is decided, that means the surface received the decision, and the reading's `receipt` reads `delivered` once every hold is released. A repeated release gives up nothing more and is answered `applied: false`.

replay.name: holdId
replay.behavior: A surface releasing an ask it raised (`release: true`) passes the `holdId` approvals.raise returned: a repeat of that release gives up nothing more, even when another surface holds the same ask. A plain cancel of an ended approval is answered `applied: false`.

errorCodes.meaning: No approval has that id; nothing was answered.

methods.title: Claim Approval
methods.description: Claim a pending approval for operator handling. A claim is advisory: it shows who is handling the ask and does not stop another participant from deciding it; a later claim replaces it. Every action sends `expectedRevision`, the `revision` of the approval it showed or read; without it the call is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. The answer is 200 with `applied`, the record and its `reading` for the caller as they are now; when `applied` is false, `refusal.code` says why: APPROVAL_SETTLED (it already ended; the first decision stands), APPROVAL_CHANGED (it moved since that revision: show the returned reading again and act on its revision), APPROVAL_EXPIRED (its deadline passed first; it is now expired), OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED (only the paired-owner decision on the device that raised it can approve it).

errorCodes.meaning: No approval has that id; nothing was answered.

methods.title: Deny Approval
methods.description: Deny a pending approval. rememberTier generalizes the denial (a generalizing tier persists a durable deny rule and sweeps queued asks it covers); reason is the user's free-text feedback, which rides the structured declined result so the model adapts instead of guessing. The response's recorded block reports what the broker actually recorded. Every action sends `expectedRevision`, the `revision` of the approval it showed or read; without it the call is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. The answer is 200 with `applied`, the record and its `reading` for the caller as they are now; when `applied` is false, `refusal.code` says why: APPROVAL_SETTLED (it already ended; the first decision stands), APPROVAL_CHANGED (it moved since that revision: show the returned reading again and act on its revision), APPROVAL_EXPIRED (its deadline passed first; it is now expired), OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED (only the paired-owner decision on the device that raised it can approve it). `disposition` is `denied` or `amended` (an amendment cannot be remembered). Malformed `disposition`, `rememberTier` or `reason` is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field; an unknown id is 404 APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND. methods.title: List Approvals
methods.description: Return pending and historical approval records, newest 50. Pass `approvalId` to read one record by id wherever it ranks; `approvals` then holds that record, or is empty when the id is unknown. Each record carries `revision` (send it as `expectedRevision` on an action), `homeNode` and `requester`, and `reading`, computed for the caller: `phase` (waiting, decided, ended), a stable `reason` (waiting-for-owner, claimed-by-other, approved, cancelled-requester-left, expired-while-down and so on), `waitingOn`, `deadline`, `allowedActions` (what this caller may do now; an agent never gets approve or deny), `decision` (who decided, from which surface and node, when), `receipt` (whether the asker received the decision: delivered, waiting, requester-reads-record, not-applicable), `work` (whether the approved work ran is not reported here) and `next` (the lawful next moves). On a stream gap or reconnect, read this list once instead of trusting the events.

methods.title: Raise Approval
methods.description: Raise a permission ask INTO the shared broker from a surface that is not in the daemon's process, the write counterpart to approvals.list/claim/approve/deny/cancel, which could only ever act on asks the daemon's own in-process callers had created. The ask becomes a record every surface can see and decide, and the daemon's attention machinery (web push, blocked-on-user) fans it out. Returns the PENDING record immediately and does NOT block waiting for an answer: the decision arrives on the control.approval_update event (SSE/WS, `gate` domain), which is the channel to watch using the returned id. An identical ask already in flight from the same caller (same authenticated principal, session, tool and args) coalesces onto the existing record, one prompt, one decision, `coalesced: true`, and the returned record is that earlier one; another caller's identical ask is raised as its own. Who raised the ask is recorded by the daemon (metadata `raisedByPrincipal`); a caller's own `raisedBy*` or `raisedVia` metadata is dropped. `approvalId` is always returned; `approval`, the record, is returned only to a caller holding read:approvals. Optional timeoutMs expires the ask if nobody answers (clamped to 12h); optional waitMs waits inline for a decision for callers that want one round trip (clamped to 60s) and reports `decided: false` with the record still pending when it runs out, never a decision that was not made. The response carries `holdId`: release it with approvals.cancel `{ release: true, holdId }` when you leave without a decision, AND once you have received the decision; that release is the evidence the approval's reading shows as `receipt: delivered`. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: Answer Owner Inbox Item
methods.description: Answer one open inbox item with one of its `options`, or with `text` when it has none (text may also accompany an option). An approval answered approve or deny is decided through the approval broker exactly as approvals.approve/deny would, and needs `expectedRevision`, the approval item's `revision`: a stale one returns `applied: false` with refusal APPROVAL_CHANGED and the item as it is now. The first answer wins, and an answer after the item's deadline changes nothing: a later one, or an answer to a withdrawn or expired item, returns `applied: false` with a `refusal` naming who answered and from where (still 200, so a raced answer does not fail). For a question an agent or session asked, `delivery` says whether the answer reached it now, waits for its session to be opened again, or cannot reach it and why; the answer is kept either way. A decision item's choice is carried out first by the app whose gate decided (undo restores the files the call changed, never/always/ask save a standing rule for calls like it); the recorded answer's text says what was done, and a choice that could not be done, or a decision another app made, returns `applied: false` with the reason and leaves it open. The choice is claimed before it is carried out: while it is being carried out, a second choice and a withdrawal return DECISION_IN_PROGRESS, and the deadline does not close it. Who answered is taken from the authenticated caller. Answering is the owner's own act: an agent is refused, and a purchase window is answered only with the authority payments.purchase.approve takes (an app on the daemon's own machine or a paired device, admin, with write:payments), else 403. An approval that puts a change to the owner (metadata `ownerAct`) is not answered with a token minted for automation: 403 OWNER_ONLY.

methods.title: Report Owner Answer Delivery
methods.description: The asking session reports what became of the answer to a question it posted: `delivered` once the answer is in its conversation, `undeliverable` (with `reason`) when its session was deleted. Only the principal that posted the question may report, only on an answered question a session asked, and only once: a second report returns `applied: false` with a `refusal`, so exactly one terminal puts the answer in its conversation.

methods.title: List Owner Inbox
methods.description: Everything waiting on the owner in one list, newest first: permission asks (kind approval), questions agents left, channel claims, purchase windows and queued actions. Calls Jev decided for the owner at the permission gate are kind decision: open while the owner can still act on one (undo, never, always, ask, keep), and listed only when `kinds` names decision or the status is closed or all. `status` is open (default), closed or all; pass `itemId` to read one item wherever it ranks. One page holds `limit` items (default 100, at most 500); while `hasMore` is true, pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the older page, so every item is reachable (a cursor the list did not return is 400 INVALID_CURSOR). An answered question carries `delivery`: delivered to the agent or session that asked, waiting for that session to be opened again, or undeliverable with the reason. `revision` moves on every change, so a surface can tell whether its copy is current by comparing one number. An approval item carries the approval's own `revision` and its `reading` for the caller (approvals.list describes it), and its `options` are what this caller may answer: an agent reading the inbox is offered none. Every item carries its `presentation`: the question in a sentence, what it will do (`consequence`, tone `cannot-undo` only for what cannot be undone), its `choices` with their keys, whether an answer can be remembered, why the owner is asked and the rest as `details`, worded once by the daemon so every surface shows the same words; an approval item's `title` is its presentation's. A delivered answer was put on a model request the provider accepted; one put on a request by a process that then died is handed to its asker again.

methods.title: Post to Owner Inbox
methods.description: Leave the owner a question or a queued action from a process that is not the daemon (an agent in a terminal app). Returns at once; the asker carries on and reads the answer later with inbox.list (`itemId`). A post under a `key` that already has an open item this same caller posted returns that item with `created: false`, so a retried post never asks twice; an item another principal posted under the same key is never returned, and this post becomes its own item. Permission asks are raised with approvals.raise; claims and purchase windows are posted by the daemon itself.

replay.name: key
replay.behavior: A post by the same caller under a `key` that already has an open item it posted returns that item instead of posting a second one, so a repeat asks the owner once.

methods.title: Withdraw Owner Inbox Item
methods.description: Take back an open item this caller posted, because the answer is no longer needed. Only the principal that posted an item may withdraw it. An item that is no longer open returns `applied: false` with a `refusal`.

methods.title: Authority Record Status
methods.description: Return the head of this daemon's authority record: the record every machine of a group answers "is this device token, user, grant or peer token current" from. revision and digest are equal on every machine that holds the same record; behind is true when another group member has gossiped a newer one, and behindOn names the members whose record differs. kinds counts the live and revoked entries of each kind. userConflicts names each username held by separate accounts made on different machines before they joined one group: neither is overwritten, each machine keeps its own, and changes to it stay on that machine. Never returns a credential or a hash. readable false means the record file exists and cannot be read: nothing authenticates from it until it can.

methods.title: Cancel Batch Job
methods.description: Cancel a queued job. A job already in a terminal state is returned unchanged; a job already submitted to the provider is refused with 409 BATCH_JOB_ALREADY_SUBMITTED, because provider batches cancel as a whole: the refusal names the provider batch and `next` points at batch.providerBatches.cancel. Needs an admin.

methods.title: Create Batch Job
methods.description: Queue one chat request to run later as part of a provider batch, answered 202 with the queued job. A message or tool the provider could never accept is refused here with INVALID_BATCH_REQUEST rather than accepted with a job id. `flush: true` submits it right away instead of waiting for the next pass, and the response then carries the job as that pass left it. When the provider cannot batch (no batch API, or not configured for it) and `batch.fallback` is `live`, the request runs at once on the live path and the job comes back finished: `completed` with its result, or `failed` with code LIVE_FALLBACK_FAILED, marked `metadata["goodvibes.execution"] = "live-fallback"`; with `fallback: fail` it is refused with BATCH_PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED or BATCH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED (409). Refused with BATCH_DISABLED (409) while the mode is `off`, LIVE_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED (400) for `executionMode: "live"`, and BATCH_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE (413) above the request size limit. Spends provider budget, so it needs an admin.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Get Batch Job
methods.description: One batch job with its status and, once finished, its result or error. An unknown id is a 404 with code BATCH_JOB_NOT_FOUND.

methods.title: List Batch Jobs
methods.description: Batch jobs, newest first. `limit` defaults to 100 and is capped at 1000.

methods.title: Cancel Provider Batch
methods.description: Cancel a whole provider batch at the provider (the `providerBatchId` shown on a submitted job) and mark its jobs. `providerStatus` is what the provider answered: `cancelled` when it stopped, `running` while it is still winding down, in which case requests it finished before the cancel are collected by the next pass and the rest are marked cancelled when it ends. `jobs` is every job of that batch as the cancel left it. A batch whose jobs are all finished is returned unchanged. Refused with BATCH_PROVIDER_BATCH_NOT_FOUND (404) when no job belongs to the id and BATCH_PROVIDER_CANCEL_UNSUPPORTED (409) when the provider has no cancel call. Needs an admin.

methods.title: Run Batch Pass
methods.description: Run one submit-and-poll pass over the queue now instead of waiting for the timer. `force: true` submits queued jobs even before their delay has elapsed. Returns the counts for this pass, all zero when the mode is `off`. Spends provider budget, so it needs an admin.

methods.title: Batch Runtime
methods.description: The batch queue's current mode (`off`: nothing is queued; `explicit`: the job API is open and a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat completion is queued when it sends `x-goodvibes-execution: batch`; `eligible-by-default`: every such completion whose provider can batch is queued unless it sends `x-goodvibes-execution: live`, and one whose provider cannot runs live as usual), what happens to a job whose provider cannot batch (`fallback`: `live` runs it at once on the live path and answers it finished, `fail` refuses it), which queue backend holds jobs, the Cloudflare settings it would use, its limits, and the providers that can batch. `GET /api/batch` and `GET /api/batch/config` return the same document.

methods.title: Create Calendar Event

methods.title: Delete Calendar Event
methods.description: Remove an event from the configured calendar (Google or CalDAV). Requires explicit confirmation (confirm: true). `deleted: false` means the calendar no longer held it. A whole recurring series is refused with 409 CALENDAR_SERIES_NOT_SUPPORTED (on Google, one occurrence is removed by the id calendar.events.list gives it); an event that changed after it was read is refused with 409 CALENDAR_EVENT_CHANGED. A backend that cannot delete events answers 501 CALENDAR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

methods.title: Get Calendar Event
methods.description: Return the full event object including attendees, recurrence, raw iCalendar UID and revision (the calendar's version of it, to send back as expectedRevision on calendar.events.update). An occurrence id from calendar.events.list returns that occurrence (its own start, end and any change made to it), not the first of its series. On Google Calendar an event deleted from the calendar is still returned by its id, with cancelled: true; it is not on the calendar.

methods.title: List Calendar Events
methods.description: Return event summaries from the configured calendar (a CalDAV server, or the connected Google account) within an optional time window. With no from or to, lists from 24 hours ago to 30 days ahead; a recurring event is listed at each occurrence in the window, each with its own id (on CalDAV, the resource href plus `#` and the occurrence's RECURRENCE-ID instant) and the `seriesId` every occurrence of its series shares (on Google, its recurringEventId), so a list can count the series once.

methods.title: Update Calendar Event
methods.description: Change an event on the configured calendar (Google or CalDAV): only the fields sent change (attendees replaces the guest list; start and end are both dates for an all-day event or both date-times). Requires explicit confirmation (confirm: true). An unknown eventId is a 404; an id that names a whole recurring series is refused with 409 CALENDAR_SERIES_NOT_SUPPORTED (on Google, one occurrence is changed by the id calendar.events.list gives it); an event that changed on the calendar after it was read is refused with 409 CALENDAR_EVENT_CHANGED and nothing is written. Send expectedRevision (the revision calendar.events.get returned when the event was shown) so a change made elsewhere after it was shown is refused the same way; read the event again and repeat the change. A backend that cannot change events answers 501 CALENDAR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

methods.title: Find A Capability
methods.description: What the caller needs, in words, in; three to five capabilities out, never the whole list. Step one picks the function group (the decision model when one is usable, keyword ranking otherwise); step two ranks the capabilities of that group, and of the nearest group when the best match is weak. Each comes with its id, one line on what it does, where it runs (daemon: here; session: in the program holding a conversation; terminal: only inside a terminal program for now), what a repeat does, its inputs (name, kind, required, choices, default) and its risk. Nothing runs.

methods.title: List Capabilities
methods.description: The capabilities this daemon knows, as a screen draws them: each one's id, group, where it runs (daemon: here; session: in the program holding a conversation; terminal: only inside a terminal program for now), what a repeat does, its words (label, the sentence that says what it will do, the line said when it is done), its risk, what it touches and how long it lasts, its inputs as described (kind, required or its usual value, fixed choices or the live list they are read from), and what undoes it. ids narrows the answer to those capabilities, group to one function group; with neither, every capability. Nothing runs.

methods.title: Run A Capability
methods.description: Runs one capability by id with its inputs (names and values as capabilities.find lists them), as the same act would run from any other source: the inputs are checked against its definition, its effects are admitted for the caller, and then your own call (a sign-in, a paired device, the machine's token, a typed `goodvibes do`, the MCP set-up) is your own act and runs at once in every permission mode; only a model's call (the program's model after its own capability gate judged it, or the model of another program) is decided under the owner's permission mode: YOLO runs it when its scopes and reach allow it, Jev decides gives it to Jev's permission decision, Ask me raises the one approval card and this call waits on the owner's answer (the caller closing its connection withdraws the question; nothing of it is kept). A capability with its own method runs through that method. workingDirectory is the caller's project (a hooks file, a project secret store); program is the terminal program asking (tui or agent); model is the model that program's conversation uses (provider:model), which a capability on that conversation's model (its context window size) acts on unless its inputs name another. The answer is the text a person reads (detail: the capability's own words without its done line), the facts a script reads (never a secret value), the risk and what a repeat of this capability does; reveal is a value the person must see once (a new device's token, a join key), returned only to the person who asked. A call not allowed is refused, 403 CAPABILITY_NOT_APPROVED with the reason. A refusal is never a 500: it keeps the code of what refused it and the status that code stands for (404 NOT_FOUND for what is not held, 422 only for inputs that do not fit, 503 UNAVAILABLE for what this daemon was started without, 409 for any other refusal of the state found, with the capability's own code); a refusal from a method or an outside program the daemon ran for the capability keeps that method's status and code (424 CI_SOURCE_REFUSED for GitHub); 500 is the daemon's own fault. A capability that acts in a project folder is refused at once, 422 CAPABILITY_CALLER_CONTEXT_MISSING, when the call names no workingDirectory: nothing is decided about a call that would then be refused. Under Ask me the owner's yes stands as the person's request for that call's own nested method that needs one (confirmation owner-request), for that one call only; whatever can refuse it without the owner (its inputs, its preview) is checked before the owner is asked. A capability that is the owner's own act is made by you from any of your credentials; a model asking for one is decided under the owner's mode, and a model never makes the acts that grant or withdraw access, sign anyone in, change a credential or the permission rules. A yes that waited is judged again against the mode and the deny rules as they are when the owner answers: plan mode switched on, or a rule that now refuses it, refuses it with that reason. A remembered answer to a model's call is kept for that caller only. Folder trust is not asked for a daemon capability: it acts on what the daemon keeps, not in a project folder.

errorCodes.meaning: No capability has this id; capabilities.find names the ones that do what is needed.
An input is unknown, missing or not one of its choices; the message names it and nothing ran.
The capability acts on a conversation (it runs in the program holding it), or it has not moved to the daemon yet and runs only in a terminal program; the message says where, and nothing ran.

The capability ran and did not do what was asked, for the state it found (nothing to store, a plugin that would not switch); the message says what is true and what to do. Any other code of the capability's own (NOT_DONE, TARGET_EXISTS, TURN_RUNNING, a missing sign-in such as GOOGLE_NOT_CONNECTED) answers 409 the same way, with that code.
What the inputs name is not held (a card, a pool, a job by that id); as the method underneath said it, any code ending _NOT_FOUND too. Nothing ran.
An input is of the right kind and does not fit what the capability found (a date in the past, a name already taken); any code ending _INVALID too. Nothing ran.
This daemon was started without what the capability needs (its knowledge store, its notifier), or cannot read it (a code ending _UNAVAILABLE or _UNREADABLE). Nothing ran.
The capability acts in a project folder (or for a program) the call did not name: workingDirectory (or program) is missing. Refused before anything was asked of the owner; nothing ran.

Decided under the owner's mode and not allowed (refused by a rule, by Jev, by "When the decision model is missing or fails" set to Decision Model Only, or by the owner's No on their card); the message says why, and nothing ran.

methods.title: Count Every Place
methods.description: What waits or is wrong in every place (Waiting for you, Automation, Work, ...), in one call, as a menu of places shows it when it opens: for each place with something to count, the count, its words ("2 waiting", "1 failed") and its tone (waiting: something waits on you; wrong: something needs a look). Each count is the place's own, made from its own lists read from their daemon sources, so it agrees with the place when opened; a list a terminal program keeps (its conversation, its key table) is not read here, and unread names a list whose read was refused (the count is made without it). program (tui, agent or web) counts that program's view: a list declared for other programs only is not read. workingDirectory is the caller's project, sent with each project-bound read. A place with nothing to count has no count. Nothing changes.

methods.title: Query Channel Directory
methods.description: Query a channel directory surface for users, groups, threads, or services.

methods.title: Get Channel Doctor Report
methods.description: Return doctor checks and repair posture for a channel surface.

methods.title: Delete Channel Draft
methods.description: Remove a channel draft from the daemon-side store.

methods.title: Get Channel Draft
methods.description: Return one channel draft by id: the owner (admin) receives its text, so a draft written on one device can be finished and sent on another; any other caller receives the redacted record. Webhook values stay redacted. An id that names no draft returns a notFound marker.

methods.title: List Channel Drafts
methods.description: Return channel drafts for cross-device sync, metadata only: each message reads as a redacted marker and webhook values are redacted. The daemon is the store of record; the text is served by channels.drafts.get.

methods.title: Save Channel Draft
methods.description: Mirror a channel draft to the daemon-side store. Webhook values must be redacted before transmission; raw webhook tokens are rejected. Requires explicit confirmation; a call made with the Agent's credential (the Agent acting on the owner's behalf) instead takes fresh recorded native admission.

methods.title: Apply Inbox Labels
methods.description: Write triage labels to inbox messages at their provider: an IMAP keyword on mail, a reaction on Slack, a reaction or forum tag on Discord. `itemIds` are ids from channels.inbox.list (up to 100); `labels` are GoodVibes/Spam, GoodVibes/Priority or GoodVibes/Normal (writing one takes the other two off), or a custom label name. Writes only for accounts whose owner switch is on (surfaces.slack.inboxTagging, surfaces.discord.inboxTagging, surfaces.email.inboxTagging). Returns one result per message: `applied` (every label is on it now), `refused` (nothing was written, with the reason and what to do) or `failed` (the provider did not take a label; `effects` says which mark was written or not).

methods.title: List Channel Inbox
methods.description: Return the merged inbound message feed (Slack DMs, Discord messages, email threads) from the host's synced provider mirror, newest first. Read-only; no provider write. Every known provider reports its own state in `providers`, including the unconfigured and the failing ones, so a short list is never ambiguous, and `partial` is true whenever a configured provider's items are missing because its last sync failed. Page with ?limit and ?cursor (opaque, from nextCursor); ?since=<cursor> returns only items committed after a previous answer's `cursor` watermark (the store's commit sequence, not a time); ?provider=<id> narrows to one provider; `uids` (a list of mail UIDs) returns only those messages of the live mailbox, matched by the email provider's current account and mailbox generation, so a client can look up a listed page without reading the feed. Each provider with triage says in `triage` whether new messages are being labelled and, when not, why and what turns it on; channels.inbox.triage labels a page now. An email item says in `screening` whether privacy screening read its text: `not-screened` (with `screeningReason`) when only code checked it for credential and card text; its subject is always the sender's own.

methods.title: Triage Inbox Now
methods.description: Score a page of one provider's stored inbox now: each message gets a spam / priority / normal label from the decision model on the account's privacy-screening route (labels otherwise come after each poll, so this is for a backlog or a re-check). `provider` is required (slack, discord or email); page with `limit` (at most 100) and `cursor` (nextCursor from channels.inbox.list or an earlier answer). `dryRun: true` returns the readings without storing them. Returns one receipt per message: `settled` with its label and score, or `held` / `unavailable` / `withheld` with why nothing was settled. When triage is off for the account the call is refused with the reason and what turns it on; channels.inbox.list reports the same state on each provider as `triage`.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Get Channel Lifecycle State
methods.description: Return lifecycle version posture for a channel surface.

methods.title: List Channel Policy Audit
methods.description: Return channel ingress policy audit records.

methods.title: List Channel Policies
methods.description: Return ingress policy configuration for channels.

methods.title: Update Channel Policy
methods.description: Update ingress policy configuration for a channel surface. `open` makes it a shared channel: while every allowlist is empty, every sender is admitted and no owner claim is raised (off by default, so the first unknown sender raises a claim the owner accepts or declines). Anyone admitted who is not the channel's owner talks as a guest: their turn may read and answer, and every change it asks for is put to the owner.

methods.title: Unbind Channel Profile
methods.description: Remove a channel profile binding. Returns { deleted: false } when no binding for that key existed, an honest boolean, never a phantom removal. Removing a binding whose permission mode is tighter than the one its channel's sessions would fall back to (the surface-wide binding's, else the host's) loosens it, which every credential of the user does at once (a device holding a narrow scope list is refused by its scopes).

methods.title: Get Channel Profile Binding
methods.description: Return the profile binding for a channel (surfaceKind plus optional channelId) and `effective`: what a session that channel originates gets, each field merged from this binding and the surface-wide one, with `sources` naming the binding id that supplied each field. Returns 404 when no binding for that exact key exists. A listed or returned binding with `invalid` holds a value this build cannot use; that field is left out until the binding is set again or deleted.

methods.title: List Channel Profile Bindings
methods.description: Return every per-channel profile binding: the model, provider and permission-mode defaults the daemon applies to the sessions each channel originates. These are the values that apply; a channels.routing assignment for the same channel names a profile that only the surface owning it resolves.

methods.title: Bind Channel Profile
methods.description: Bind (upsert) the model/provider and permission-mode defaults for a channel. Keyed on (surfaceKind, channelId?): field by field, a channelId-scoped binding wins over the surface-wide default; setting the same key again replaces it. A session the daemon originates from the channel uses these values whatever a channels.routing assignment names. A set that loosens the permission mode the channel's sessions run under (against the mode they get now, the host's when no binding sets one; leaving permissionMode out of a set removes the key's own mode) is made at once by every credential of the user, as sessions.permissionMode.set is (a device holding a narrow scope list is refused by its scopes).

methods.title: List Channel Repair Actions
methods.description: Return repair actions exposed by a channel surface.

methods.title: Assign Channel Routing Rule
methods.description: Create or update a channel-to-profile routing rule in the daemon-persisted routing table. The daemon applies it on every channel surface (slack, discord, telegram, msteams and the rest) and to slack, discord and email inbox items: an agent started for a message from the channel takes the profile's model and reasoning effort when neither the request nor the channel profile chose a model. routeId is the conversation (a chat, channel or room id); without it the rule covers the whole surface, and surfaceKind any covers every channel. tui, web and service are refused with 400 ROUTING_SURFACE_NOT_ROUTED, because their model is chosen in the surface itself. Requires explicit confirmation; a call made with the Agent's credential (the Agent acting on the owner's behalf) instead takes fresh recorded native admission.

methods.title: Delete Channel Routing Rule
methods.description: Remove a channel-to-profile routing rule from the daemon-persisted routing table.

methods.title: List Channel Routing Rules
methods.description: Return the daemon-persisted channel-to-profile routing table. The profileId a rule names is stamped on inbox items from that channel (their routeId) so the surface owning the profile picks them up; it sets no model, provider or permission mode. Those come from channels.profiles.*, the one table the daemon applies to sessions a channel originates.

methods.title: Get Channel Setup Schema
methods.description: Return the versioned setup schema, secret targets, and external steps for a channel surface.

methods.title: Channel Status
methods.description: Return status for channel plugins and provider-backed channels.

methods.title: Resolve Channel Target
methods.description: Resolve a typed channel target for outbound delivery or routing. A plain name resolves only when it names exactly one conversation; a name several conversations share (a person and a channel both called ops) returns the unresolved fallback target with metadata.ambiguous listing each candidate's id, kind and label, so the caller passes #name, @name or a typed id.

methods.title: Send Channel Test Message
methods.description: Send a real test message through a configured channel surface and report the actual delivery outcome. delivered:true means the daemon's delivery router accepted and sent it (with the surface's responseId when it returns one); a failed send is delivered:false with the real error (unconfigured/unsupported surface, provider/transport error), never a fabricated success. Provide address to target a specific recipient/channel, or omit it to use the surface's configured default.

methods.title: Cancel Home Assistant Conversation Turn
methods.description: Stop the running turn of a Home Assistant chat session, named by sessionId or by a known messageId. The session stays open. A session that is not a Home Assistant chat session answers 404.

methods.title: Home Assistant Conversation Health
methods.description: Report whether the Home Assistant surface is enabled and the conversation endpoints it serves.

methods.title: Stream Home Assistant Conversation Message
methods.description: Post one utterance and stream the reply as server-sent events: delta frames, then one final or error frame. A providerId or modelId of the caller's choosing needs an admin token.

replay.name: messageId
replay.behavior: A repeat that names the same `messageId` in the same conversation posts nothing again and starts no second turn: while the first turn runs the repeat waits for it and streams its outcome as the final or error frame; after it ended the outcome is read from the transcript. A stream the client drops cancels its own turn, so a repeat after a drop reports it cancelled. The daemon keeps the messageId while it runs (a restart forgets it). Without a messageId each call posts the utterance and starts a turn.

methods.title: Submit Home Assistant Conversation Message
methods.description: Post one utterance to the isolated chat session of a Home Assistant conversation and wait for the reply (or return at once with wait false). A providerId or modelId of the caller's choosing needs an admin token. A tools list is refused.

methods.title: Get Check-in Config
methods.description: Return the proactive check-in configuration (enabled, cadence (cron), delivery channel, quiet hours) and `schedule`: whether the scheduler really holds the check-in job (scheduled), none is needed (not-needed: check-ins are off), or it could not be installed (failed, with the reason; for example the automation subsystem is off). Enabled with a failed schedule means no check-in will arrive.

methods.title: Update Check-in Config
methods.description: Update the proactive check-in configuration. Absent fields are left unchanged. Enabling syncs the kind:checkin automation job onto the scheduler; disabling stops it. The answer carries `schedule` (scheduled, not-needed, or failed with the reason), because the config is stored even when the scheduler could not install the job.

methods.title: List Check-in Receipts
methods.description: Return the visible receipts of past check-in runs (newest first): each run records whether it stayed quiet, delivered a message (and what), or was skipped.

methods.title: Run Check-in Now
methods.description: Trigger one check-in evaluation immediately (a manual run): assemble the briefing, judge whether to contact the user, deliver if so, and record a receipt.

methods.title: Create Workspace Checkpoint
methods.description: Create a new workspace checkpoint. Returns checkpoint:null, noop:true (not an error) when the workspace tree is identical to the most recent checkpoint, no commit, ref, or manifest entry is created in that case.

methods.title: Diff Workspace Checkpoints
methods.description: Diff two checkpoints, or one checkpoint against the live working tree when `b` is omitted. An unknown/gc'd checkpoint id is an honest 404, not a silent empty diff.

methods.title: List Workspace Checkpoints
methods.description: Return workspace checkpoints (whole-workspace filesystem snapshots), newest first, optionally filtered by kind/since and capped by limit.

methods.title: Restore Workspace Checkpoint
methods.description: DESTRUCTIVE: restore the workspace to the state captured by a checkpoint (git-backed workspace rewrite). Refuses to run unconfirmed: pass confirm:true to execute immediately, OR a confirmToken from checkpoints.restorePreview (bound to the checkpoint, its workspace and the other sessions' changes it showed; another one, or another session's change made since, is refused with TARGET_CHANGED). A restore that would take back changes other sessions made after the checkpoint runs with confirm:true only when takeBack names each of those sessions; otherwise it is refused (refusal.otherSessions names them and their files) and nothing changes. Those sessions are told in their conversations. An unconfirmed call returns a structured refusal (result:null, refused:true, refusal naming the options), not an error. An unknown/gc'd checkpoint id (once confirmed) is an honest 404, not a silent no-op.

methods.title: Preview Workspace Checkpoint Restore
methods.description: Read-only: preview what a checkpoints.restore of this checkpoint would change (label, affected-path count + sample, diffstat, and otherSessions: the other sessions whose changes it takes back, with their files) and mint a short-lived (~2 min), single-use confirmToken that authorizes the matching restore, those sessions' changes included. No workspace mutation. An unknown/gc'd checkpoint id is an honest 404.

methods.title: Revert a Single Hunk
methods.description: DESTRUCTIVE: reverse-apply ONE unified-diff hunk to its file in the live working tree, undoing exactly that hunk and nothing else. The hunk must still apply cleanly in reverse, a stale/drifted hunk is an honest 409 conflict, never a partial write. Refuses to run unconfirmed: pass confirm:true to execute immediately, OR a confirmToken from checkpoints.revertHunkPreview. A token binds the workspace, the hunk and the file as the preview read it: the revert runs in that workspace whatever sessionId the call names, and a file changed since the preview is refused with TARGET_CHANGED naming it. An unconfirmed call returns a structured refusal (receipt:null, refused:true, refusal naming both options), not an error. Snapshots the whole tree (a manual checkpoint) before writing, so the revert is itself reversible; returns a receipt whose undo block carries that checkpoint id. Emits a HUNK_REVERTED receipt event.

methods.title: Preview a Single-Hunk Revert
methods.description: Read-only: check whether reverse-applying ONE unified-diff hunk (copied from a checkpoints.diff / sessions.changes.get diff) to its file in the live working tree would apply cleanly right now, and mint a short-lived (~2 min), single-use confirmToken authorizing the matching checkpoints.revertHunk. A stale/drifted hunk returns applies:false with a human-readable conflict and a null token, an honest "this hunk no longer applies", not an error. No workspace mutation.

methods.title: CI Per-Job Status
methods.description: Poll GitHub for a repo/ref/PR and return EVERY job with its conclusion. The overall verdict is derived from the per-job conclusions (never a rollup); continue-on-error jobs are surfaced as violations and force the verdict off "passed".

errorCodes.meaning: GitHub could not be read through gh (not signed in, unreachable, or gh is missing); the message carries gh's own words, and nothing was read or changed.
GitHub has no such repository, branch or pull request that this login can read, so no verdict will come.

methods.title: Create CI Watch
methods.description: Create a standing watch on a repo/ref or PR. On a terminal verdict it notifies the channel. Failed jobs request a fresh recorded repair decision from the original source owner; the compatibility flag is not authorization.

methods.title: Delete CI Watch
methods.description: Remove a standing CI watch. Returns { deleted: false } when no watch with that id existed.

methods.title: List CI Watches

Stored flags are not repair authority; production repair requires current original-source ownership and Jev admission.

methods.title: Check CI Watch Now
methods.description: Poll a standing watch immediately: returns the per-job report, whether a completion notification fired, and whether an admitted fix-session started, or an honest refusal/error. When the check ended the watch without a verdict or a repair, `retired` is true and `endedReason` says why.

methods.title: Validate Cloudflare Credentials
methods.description: Check that the API token (inline, by reference, or the stored one) is valid and return the account it belongs to. A missing token is refused with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_REQUIRED (400), a stored one this computer's secret store could not read with CLOUDFLARE_CREDENTIALS_UNREADABLE (412, the cause named, nothing asked for again), and a token Cloudflare rejects fails the call with Cloudflare's error. Changes nothing.

methods.title: Disable Cloudflare Worker
methods.description: Switch the Cloudflare integration off. Always disables it locally (`cloudflare.enabled` false and the batch queue back to `local`; `persistConfig` defaults to true) and stops this daemon's tunnel connector, so the daemon stops using the worker. When an API token and account are available it also removes the worker's daemon credential (the script secret and its Secrets Store copy), its cron trigger (`disableCron`, default true) and its workers.dev route (`disableWorkerSubdomain`, default true; pass false to keep the route). `remote` is `disabled` only when every Cloudflare step succeeded; otherwise it is `not-disabled`, the deployed worker may keep calling the daemon until it is disabled in the Cloudflare dashboard, and `steps` says which. The worker and the account's other resources stay in place; each one still deployed is listed as a `still-deployed` step. With `bootstrapToken` (a token allowed to edit API tokens) it also revokes the operational token this daemon created; without it a `revoke-operational-token` step says that token is still live.

methods.title: Provision Cloudflare Platform
methods.description: Create or update the selected Cloudflare resources (worker, queues and dead-letter queue, tunnel and its connector on this daemon, Access application and service token, DNS records, KV for queued-job state, Durable Objects for the daily queue budget, R2 for job bodies, Secrets Store for the worker's credentials), answered 202 with one step per resource: `ok`, `skipped` or `warning`; `warnings` repeats the message of every warning step. Generated secrets are stored as `goodvibes://` secrets when asked and returned only when `returnGeneratedSecrets` is true. With Workers selected and a worker URL known it then runs the `cloudflare.worker.verify` check unless `verify` is false. `ok` is true, and `cloudflare.enabled` and the Cloudflare batch queue are switched on, only when that check passed (or was turned off) and Access, when asked for, protects the daemon hostname; otherwise a `switch-on` warning step says why nothing was switched. Creates and changes billable resources in the Cloudflare account.

methods.title: Discover Cloudflare Resources
methods.description: List what the account already has for the selected components: accounts, zones, the workers.dev subdomain and, with `includeResources`, existing queues, KV namespaces, Durable Object namespaces, R2 buckets, Secrets Stores, tunnels and Access applications. Read-only against Cloudflare; sent as a POST so credentials and the component selection travel in the body.

methods.title: Cloudflare Status
methods.description: Whether the Cloudflare control plane is enabled and ready, which of its settings and credentials are configured (booleans only, never values), the stored non-secret configuration, and the warnings that explain anything missing. A resource (worker, queues, tunnel, Access, KV, Durable Objects, R2, Secrets Store) reads as configured only when a provision created or confirmed it at Cloudflare. Where this daemon runs the Cloudflare Tunnel connector, `tunnelConnector` says whether it is connected and what to do when it is not; `ready` requires it. `GET /api/cloudflare` returns the same document.

methods.title: Create Cloudflare Operational Token
methods.description: Use a temporary bootstrap token (required, used once, never stored) to create a narrower operational token with the permissions `cloudflare.token.requirements.get` lists. With `storeApiToken` the operational token is saved as a `goodvibes://` secret and its reference is returned; the plaintext token comes back only when `returnGeneratedToken` is true. When this daemon already holds the operational token it made for the same account, zone and components, that token is returned with `reused` true and nothing is created (`reuse: false` makes a new one). A new token revokes the one it replaces; `replaced` says whether that worked. Creates run one at a time. Each create is recorded in the daemon's operation log before it is sent, and the new token's name ends in that operation's id: a create whose answer was lost fails with CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (the token may exist), and the next create first finds such tokens (by the id noted, or by name) and revokes them, since their values were never stored; any it cannot find or revoke are listed in `residual`. Answered 201. Creates a credential in the Cloudflare account unless one is reused.

methods.title: Cloudflare Token Requirements
methods.description: The Cloudflare API permissions each selected component needs, and how to create the one-off bootstrap token that `cloudflare.token.create` uses. Components default to Workers and Queues. Reads nothing from Cloudflare and changes nothing. Sent as a POST so the component selection travels in the body.

methods.title: Verify Cloudflare Worker
methods.description: Check the deployed worker: its `/batch/health` route (`workerHealth`) and its `/api/batch/config` proxy to this daemon (`daemonBatchProxy`), each with `ok`, the HTTP status and any error; `ok` is true only when both pass. A stored worker client token is sent only to the configured `cloudflare.workerBaseUrl`; for any other URL pass `workerClientToken` in the request or the proxy check reports why it was not authenticated. The URL must be https and is required (CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL_REQUIRED, 400). Changes nothing.

methods.title: Remove a File From a Sent Companion Chat Message
methods.description: Remove a file attached to a sent companion-chat message, for good: the file is deleted from the artifact store and cannot be put back. Every message of the chat that carried it keeps a line in its place (`removedAttachments`: `artifactId`, `name`, `removedAt`; clients show "<name> was removed"), and the model no longer receives the file on later turns (it is told the file's name and that it was removed). Works on a closed chat too. Repeating it answers the same way with `alreadyRemoved: true`. An unknown chat is 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, an unknown message 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND, a file the message never carried 404 ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND; while a reply is streaming, a message is being prepared or sends are queued it is refused with 409 CHAT_TURN_BUSY and nothing changes (stop the reply or let it finish, then remove); a daemon with no file store is 501 ATTACHMENTS_UNAVAILABLE.

methods.title: Switch Companion Chat Branch
methods.description: Put another version of a turn on the conversation. A turn has versions when a user message was edited (the message and its edits, linked by `revisionOf`) or a reply was regenerated (the replies to one user message, linked by `inReplyTo`); each version heads the run of messages one fork marked superseded. `messageId` is the first message of the version wanted. The version on the conversation now (that turn's active message and everything after it, except a reply to an earlier message) is marked superseded, kept as history, and the chosen version is active again, so the chat shows it on every device and the model continues from it; nothing is deleted and no turn starts. Switching back is the same call with the other version's first message. A `messageId` already on the conversation answers `switched: false` and changes nothing. Works on a closed chat. An unknown chat is 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, an unknown message 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND; a message that does not start a version, or whose turn is not on the conversation now, is 409 NOT_A_BRANCH; while a reply is streaming, a message is being prepared or sends are queued it is 409 CHAT_TURN_BUSY and nothing changes.

methods.title: Stream Companion Chat Events
methods.description: Server-Sent Events stream of turn and agent events scoped to a single companion-chat session. Besides the turn frames (`companion-chat.turn.*`), `companion-chat.transcript.changed` (`{ type: "transcript.changed", sessionId, change: "attachment-removed" | "branch-switched", messageIds }`) says the transcript changed outside a turn (companion.chat.attachments.remove, companion.chat.branches.switch): read the messages again. Needs read:transcripts; the chat's own maker follows it under read:sessions or write:sessions as well.

methods.title: Send Companion Chat Message
methods.description: Post a user message to a companion-chat session. Accepts either `body` or `content` in the payload; `body` wins when both are provided. Attachments reference artifacts created through `artifacts.create`. A message queued behind a running turn whose turn can never run (the chat closed, the service shut down or the daemon restarted first) ends as `deliveryState: "unanswered"`. Optional `clientMessageId` (1 to 255 letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") makes the send safe to repeat: a second send with the same id returns the first message's id and starts no second turn, so a client whose response was lost can resend. The id is remembered while the session stays loaded in the daemon; a daemon restart forgets it.

replay.name: clientMessageId
replay.behavior: A second send with the same `clientMessageId` returns the first message's id and starts no second turn, while the session stays loaded in the daemon (a daemon restart forgets the id).

methods.title: Edit Companion Chat Message And Branch
methods.description: Edit a user message and branch the conversation from it. `messageId` (required) is the user message to edit; the edited text is passed as `body` or `content` (as message create accepts), with optional `attachments` referencing artifacts. The original message and everything after it are SUPERSEDED, retained as history, never deleted, a new user message carrying `revisionOf` back to the original is appended, and a fresh turn answers it. Returns the new message id and the superseded ids for honest lineage. Same closed/unknown-session refusals as companion.chat.messages.retry, and the same 409 CHAT_TURN_BUSY while a reply, a message being prepared, or queued sends are in flight (nothing is superseded).

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: List Companion Chat Messages
methods.description: Return the messages of a companion-chat session, oldest first. With neither `limit` nor `before` the whole transcript is returned. With `limit` (1-1000, default 100 when only `before` is given) and/or `before` (a message id) one page is returned: the messages just before `before`, or the newest ones. Every answer carries `total` and `more`; while `more` is true, pass `nextBefore` back as `before` to read the page before it. A `before` that names no message in the chat is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. Needs read:transcripts; the chat's own maker reads it under read:sessions or write:sessions as well.

methods.title: Regenerate Companion Chat Response
methods.description: Regenerate an assistant response. Omitted `messageId`: the latest answered user message is answered again; whatever followed it in its exchange (its reply, a failed reply, or nothing) is SUPERSEDED, while a reply to an earlier message that was stored after it stays active, so retrying a failed regenerate repeats the same exchange. With `messageId` (an active assistant message): that response and every message after it are superseded, and the turn re-runs from the user message it answered. Superseded messages are kept in the message list and on disk, flagged as retained history, never deleted. Returns the superseded message ids so the caller can render the honest lineage. Rejected on a closed session (409 SESSION_CLOSED) or unknown session (404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND); a `messageId` that is unknown is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND, already superseded 409 MESSAGE_SUPERSEDED, not an assistant message 400 NOT_AN_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE; with no user message to answer again it is 409 NO_ANCHOR_MESSAGE. While a reply is streaming, a message is being prepared, or sends are queued it is refused with 409 CHAT_TURN_BUSY and nothing changes: stop the reply (or let it and the queue finish), then retry.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Search Companion Chat Messages
methods.description: Find companion-chat messages whose text contains `query` (case-insensitive) across every chat, newest first. Each item names the chat (`sessionId`, `sessionTitle`), the message (`messageId`, `role`), a snippet around the match and `createdAt`. History retained behind a regenerate or edit is not searched. Closed chats are searched only with `includeClosed`. Paged: `limit` 1-100 (default 25); pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` while `hasMore` is true. A blank query is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT; a cursor this search did not return is 400 INVALID_CURSOR. A caller below admin searches only the chats it made (under read:transcripts, read:sessions or write:sessions).

methods.title: Steer Companion Chat (Interrupt And Send)
methods.description: Send a message that runs IMMEDIATELY, interrupting the in-flight turn if one is running. The message jumps to the front of the pending-turn queue; the active turn is cancelled through the same finalization path as companion.chat.turns.cancel (any non-empty partial reply is persisted with `deliveryState: "cancelled"` and the terminal `turn.cancelled` event reaches every subscriber), then the steered message's turn starts. Messages queued behind an active turn keep their places behind the steer. With no turn running this behaves as an ordinary send. Accepts the same payload as companion.chat.messages.create (`body`/`content`, `attachments`, `metadata`). Returns the new message id, `steered: true`, and `cancelledTurnId` when a turn was interrupted. Ordinary sends posted while a turn is running are QUEUED (transcript-visible immediately with `deliveryState: "queued"`, answered in order), steer is the explicit jump-the-line verb. A queued message whose turn can never run (the chat closed, the service shut down or the daemon restarted first) ends as `deliveryState: "unanswered"`, never silently dropped.

replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Remove a Queued Companion Chat Message
methods.description: Take a companion chat message out of the queue before its turn starts, so it is never answered. The transcript keeps it, marked `deliveryState: "unanswered"`, and leaves it out of what the model sees. A message whose turn has started (or that was already removed) is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_QUEUED.

methods.title: Edit a Queued Companion Chat Message
methods.description: Replace the text of a companion chat message still waiting for its turn; its attachments stay. The transcript shows the new text. A message whose turn has started (or that was removed) is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_QUEUED.

methods.title: List Queued Companion Chat Messages
methods.description: The messages of a companion chat waiting behind the running reply (sent while it was still being written), in the order they will be answered. Each stays editable and removable until its turn starts; a message whose turn has started no longer appears. An unknown chat is 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND. Needs read:transcripts; the chat's own maker reads it under read:sessions or write:sessions as well.

methods.title: Close Companion Chat Session
methods.description: Close a companion-chat session (soft close). The session record and its messages are preserved in closed state and remain listable with includeClosed. Distinct from companion.chat.sessions.delete, which permanently removes the record.

methods.title: Create Companion Chat Session
methods.description: Create a new companion-chat session. Optional `provider` / `model` override the registry default. The session retains its requested `reasoningEffort`; null restores provider defaults. Title and system prompt are stored on the session record. `workingDirectory` (absolute; else the `x-goodvibes-project` header) is the project the chat works in: its tools, tool servers, hooks, checkpoints and rules are that project's; without one the chat works in the daemon's own folder.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Delete Companion Chat Session
methods.description: Permanently remove a companion-chat session: the on-disk record file is deleted and the session is dropped from the shared session store, this does NOT merely close it (use companion.chat.sessions.close for a soft close). Requires the session to already be closed: deleting a still-active session is rejected with 409 SESSION_ACTIVE (close it, then delete). An unknown or already-deleted id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop.

methods.title: Get Companion Chat Session
methods.description: Return a companion-chat session record together with its full message history. Needs read:transcripts; the chat's own maker reads it under read:sessions or write:sessions as well.

methods.title: List Companion Chat Sessions
methods.description: List active companion-chat sessions, newest first, one page of `limit` (default 100). Pass `includeClosed` to include closed sessions. While `hasMore` is true, pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the page of older chats; a cursor this list did not return is 400 INVALID_CURSOR. Each record carries its title and system prompt, so it needs read:transcripts; a caller below admin is listed only the chats it made, under read:sessions or write:sessions as well.

methods.title: Reopen Companion Chat Session
methods.description: Open a closed companion-chat session again so it accepts messages. The model history is rebuilt from the saved transcript on the next send. A chat that is already open answers `reopened: false` with its current status; an unknown id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND.

methods.title: Update Companion Chat Session
methods.description: Update companion-chat session metadata, including session-local provider, model and requested reasoning effort, without changing the daemon/TUI current model. Routing changes are refused while a reply is active; null effort restores provider defaults.

methods.title: Cancel Companion Chat Turn
methods.description: Stop the in-flight turn for a companion chat session, a true server-side stop: the provider stream is aborted, any non-empty partial reply is persisted to the transcript with an explicit `deliveryState: "cancelled"` marker (an honest partial, never disguised as a complete reply) AND committed to the model-facing conversation history with an explicit interruption note, later turns can reason about what the user saw and stopped, which is usually what a follow-up or steer refers to, and the terminal `turn.cancelled` event is published to every subscriber of the session stream so a stop from one client converges on all others. Any announced tool call without a result is closed with a synthetic error `turn.tool_result` before the terminal event. Optional `turnId` guards against cancelling a newer turn a stale stop raced against (409 TURN_MISMATCH). A stop without `turnId` that lands before the next turn starts (a message still being saved, or one queued to start) cancels that turn: the answer is `cancelled: true` with `stoppedBeforeStart: true` (and `messageIds` when a queued message was named), no `turnId`, and the message stays in the transcript as `unanswered`. No turn in flight and none on its way is the benign 404 NO_ACTIVE_TURN (the turn finished before the stop landed). When the turn has not stopped within 3 seconds (a tool call or the provider has not ended yet) the stop is still accepted and the answer is 409 TURN_STOPPING with `state: "stopping"`: treat the turn as stopping, not failed; the terminal `turn.cancelled` event follows when it stops. Repeat cancels are idempotent successes. The session stays open; the next message starts a fresh turn normally.

methods.title: Get Config
methods.description: Return the resolved GoodVibes config snapshot.

methods.title: Reset Config Value
methods.description: Remove the explicit value of one config key through the daemon API so it reads as its default again, in every settings file that holds it. The response reports the value the host now holds and which file and tier it came from. Refuses a key that holds a credential (use credentials.delete), a key the host does not know, a key locked by managed policy, and runtime.workingDir (no caller moves the daemon). A change that loosens a security, permission, judgment or payment setting is made at once by every credential of the user (a sign-in under any name, a device paired with full scopes, the operator token); the permission mode in force decides one sent without the person's claim, as for any call. A device holding a narrow scope list reaches only what its list names (this method needs write:config and an admin: it is refused 403).

replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. methods.title: Set Config Value
methods.description: Write one config value on the daemon: `{ key, value }`, where value is any JSON the key accepts. The response reports the value the host now holds and which file and tier it is in; a value that did not take is refused with what the host holds instead. A key that holds a credential takes only a goodvibes://secrets/ reference (store the secret with credentials.set); runtime.workingDir is refused (409 WORKSPACE_CHANGE_UNAVAILABLE): the daemon serves every project at once and no caller moves it, so a call names its project itself. The same route also serves the settings clients' lane, which answers with its own object: `{ settingsPrecondition }` takes action `capture` (read the facts a change would act on) or `write` (make it, optionally only while `ifServing` and `ifIncarnation` still hold; a repeated `requestId` returns the first answer). methods.title: Set Several Config Values
methods.description: Write several config values on the daemon as one update: `{ entries: [{ key, value }] }`. Every entry is admitted before anything is written, each settings file is written once and the configuration revision moves once, so a pair of settings that only make sense together never lands half-applied. A refusal names the setting, the reason and the next step, and says what was saved (nothing, unless a later settings file could not be written after an earlier one was). The answer lists, per key, the value the host now holds and which file and tier it is in; when a key does not hold the value asked for (a higher tier overrides it, or it was coerced), the answer is 409 CONFIG_SET_NOT_APPLIED naming those keys in `notApplied`, with the revision written and every entry's held value. A key that holds a credential takes only a goodvibes://secrets/ reference; runtime.workingDir is refused (409 WORKSPACE_CHANGE_UNAVAILABLE), as with config.set.
