methods.title: Delete Credential
methods.description: Remove a credential: the stored secret first, then the config reference pointing at it. That order is deliberate, clearing the config first would strand a secret nothing points at and nothing reaps, while this order leaves, for an instant, a reference resolving to nothing, which every reader already treats as configured-but-broken (the honest state for a credential mid-removal). `cleared: false` means nothing was stored under that key: a miss, not an error, because asking for a credential to be gone when it already is has succeeded. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding. Mutating, so a relay call is covered by relay.requireStepUpForMutations exactly as config.set is.

methods.title: Get Credential Status
methods.description: Return secret-free credential status (configured/usable) for the shared store. Never returns raw secret bytes. Optional ?key= narrows to one credential.

methods.title: Set Credential
methods.description: Store a credential for a secret-bearing config key THROUGH the daemon, so a surface no longer has to write it into its own on-disk secret store, the write counterpart to credentials.get, and the reason a client on another machine can now finish a settings modal at all. `key` is the config path (e.g. surfaces.telegram.botToken); the secret-store name is derived from it. The value goes into the encrypted store at the scope the ownership rules resolve (a daemon-needed credential lands in the daemon tier whoever asked), is read BACK and compared, and only then does the config key take its goodvibes://secrets/goodvibes/<KEY> reference. A read-back mismatch fails the call and leaves the setting exactly as it was, because a reference resolving to nothing reads as a configured-but-broken credential. The response is secret-free: key names, the resolved scope, the reference now in config, and two plain sentences about where the setting and the credential are filed, never the value. Refuses a key that is not credential-bearing (use config.set) and refuses a value that is itself a goodvibes:// reference. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding. Mutating, so a relay call is covered by relay.requireStepUpForMutations exactly as config.set is.

methods.title: Continuity Snapshot
methods.description: Return the continuity integration snapshot.

methods.title: Set a Running Contract's Budget
methods.description: Replace a running contract's token and cost ceiling (`maxCostUsd`, `maxTokens`, or both); a limit left out keeps its current value. Each running group's remaining allowance moves by the same amount, and a unit waiting because the budget was used up starts. Returns the new `budget`, both limits as they now stand. 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when neither limit is given or one is negative; 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_ENDED once the contract has ended; 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work.

errorCodes.meaning: An input is not one the method accepts; the error names it and nothing was changed.
No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.
The contract has ended; its budget can no longer change.
Native work keeps its budget with its own execution.
This runner holds the contract only for inspection.

methods.title: Cancel a Contract
methods.description: Stop a contract and every unit agent it runs; its status line records how many files were already changed and where. `cancelled` is false when the contract had already ended. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work (stop it through its own execution, or answer its open question with `cancel`); 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING when this runner holds the contract only for inspection. A contract held because its recorded input could not be restored (status `held.code` `input-unavailable`) is cancelled here; one held because no run claim could be taken (`claim-unavailable`) is refused with 409 CONTRACT_HELD, since another process may be running it.

errorCodes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.
Native work stops through its own execution, or by answering its open question with cancel.
This runner holds the contract only for inspection.
The contract is held because no run claim could be taken; another process may run it, so it is not cancelled here. Fix the contract directory and restart, then cancel.

methods.title: Dispatch Contract Work
methods.description: Start a contract for `ask` (the person's words verbatim) in a hosted session created for it, in `workspaceRoot` (absolute, inside the daemon's working directory or a registered workspace, the folders sessions.hosted.workspaces lists) or the daemon's working directory. The contract's questions arrive as that session's replies, and the session ends when the contract passes, fails or is cancelled. Returns at once with the contract and its owner agent id; read it with `contracts.get`, stop it with `contracts.cancel`, answer it with `contracts.reply`. `idempotencyKey` returns the first dispatch's contract to a retry by the same caller, also after a daemon restart, and the session made for it still ends when it settles. 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when `ask` is empty or `workspaceRoot` is relative or outside those folders; 409 with NOT_HOSTING when this daemon hosts no sessions (use `contracts.start`).

replay.name: idempotencyKey
replay.behavior: A repeat by the same caller with the same `idempotencyKey`, `ask` and workspace returns the first dispatch's contract instead of starting a second one, and creates no second session; the same key with a different ask or workspace is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Keys are kept with the workspace's contract store per caller, as for contracts.start, so a retry after a daemon restart, or through another process on the same project, still returns the first contract. A dispatch whose key cannot be recorded is refused with CONTRACT_KEY_UNRECORDED and starts nothing; a repeat while another process is still starting the first is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT.

errorCodes.meaning: An input is not one the method accepts; the error names it and nothing was changed.
This daemon hosts no sessions, so work cannot be dispatched into a new one; use contracts.start.

methods.title: Get a Contract
methods.description: One contract with its whole tree, running or ended. The captured input's per-file list, which only contracts captured before the input was recorded as a git tree carry, is left out unless `includeInputFiles` is true. To poll for progress, use `contracts.status`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND when no runner on this daemon holds the id.

errorCodes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.

methods.title: List Contracts
methods.description: Every contract this daemon holds, newest first, each with its whole tree: the ask, the goal, the acceptance criteria with every Jev reading, the groups and units with their checks and nudges, open and answered owner escalations, decisions, usage, and the answer or status line once it ends. `sessionId` narrows the list to one session's contracts (a hosted session's, or a shared session's); ended contracts are left out unless `includeTerminal` is set. For a list view, `contracts.summaries` returns the same contracts as small summaries. A contract an identified caller started belongs to that caller (`ownerPrincipalId`) for its whole life; one a hosted session's own turn started belongs to that session's identified owners. Contracts of another caller are left out here and read as CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND everywhere else.

methods.title: Remove an Ended Contract
methods.description: Delete the record of a contract that has ended (passed, failed or cancelled): its checkpoint and summary. Its branch and worktree, if any, are left to the worktree retention rules. Ended contracts are also removed automatically 30 days after they end, and beyond the newest 100 per project. `removed` is true when it was deleted. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_ENDED while it runs (cancel it first); 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work, whose record its native execution keeps.

errorCodes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.
The contract is still running or settling; cancel it, then remove it once it has stopped.
Native work keeps its record with its native execution.

methods.title: Reply to a Contract Escalation
methods.description: The owner's free-text reply to an open escalation of a contract, read by Jev as approve, reject, amend or unclear. Returns how it was read and what the runner did: approved, amended, stopped, asked again (with the new escalation id), or refused when the escalation is no longer open. Approval never passes a criterion Jev read as unmet; the requirement changes only through an amendment. A failed-work question (a native work contract's failed turn, a failed unit, a result that could not be published) is not read by Jev: it accepts exactly `retry` or `cancel`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_NOT_RUNNING when this runner holds the contract only for inspection, 409 with CONTRACT_ENDED when the contract has ended, 409 with ESCALATION_NOT_OPEN when the escalation is already answered or another reply to it is being read, 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when the text is not an answer the question accepts.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

errorCodes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.
This runner holds the contract only for inspection.
The contract has ended.
The escalation is already answered, or another reply to it is being read.
An input is not one the method accepts; the error names it and nothing was changed.

methods.title: Run One Contract Unit Again
methods.description: Run one unit of a running contract again: a unit that is working gets a fresh agent with its brief and previous checks, a unit that failed (the contract waits on its retry-or-cancel question, the units depending on it held) runs again with a fresh agent, the same as replying `retry`, and a passed unit whose commit failed has its changes committed again. `outcome` is `restarted`, `committed`, or `refused` with `reason` naming why and what to do instead (a unit that has not started, is being fixed, or ended with its contract). 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; 409 with CONTRACT_ENDED once the contract has ended; 409 with CONTRACT_NATIVE for native work.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

errorCodes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.
The contract has ended; start a new one for the remaining work.
Native work runs its units through its own execution.
This runner holds the contract only for inspection.

methods.title: Start a Contract
methods.description: Start a contract for `ask`, the person's words verbatim, which every stated acceptance criterion must trace to. Returns at once with the new contract and its owner agent id; the contract shapes, plans and runs on its own, and its progress arrives on the `contracts` event domain. When `sessionId` names a live session this daemon hosts, the contract starts in that session (origin `hosted`): its turns receive the contract's questions and a following turn answers them. Otherwise it starts on the daemon's own runner (origin `external`) under `sessionId`, or the `operator` session when none is given, in `workspaceRoot` (absolute), or the daemon's working directory. `isolation` overrides `contract.isolation` for this contract. 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when `ask` is empty, `workspaceRoot` is relative or outside the daemon's workspace, or differs from the hosted session's; 403 with SESSION_NOT_OWNED when the session belongs to another caller; 409 with SESSION_NOT_LIVE when `sessionId` names a hosted session that is no longer live.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: A retry with the same key and the same body returns the first contract (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true response header) instead of starting a second one; the same key with a different body is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Keys are kept with the contract store per caller, so a retry after a daemon restart, or through another process on the same project, still returns the first contract; the body is compared field by field, in any order. A start whose key cannot be recorded is refused with CONTRACT_KEY_UNRECORDED and starts nothing; a repeat while another process is still starting the first is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again in a few seconds). The key may also be sent as `idempotencyKey` in the body; the header wins when both are given. A replayed result carries `replayed: true`.

errorCodes.meaning: An input is not one the method accepts; the error names it and nothing was changed.
The session belongs to another caller.
sessionId names a hosted session that is no longer live.
This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request; use a new key.
Another process is still starting a contract with this key; send the same request again in a few seconds.
The key could not be recorded in the project's contract directory, so nothing was started; make the directory writable and retry.

methods.title: Get a Contract's Status
methods.description: One contract's summary (as `contracts.summaries` gives it), for polling. Pass the `revision` of the last answer as `ifRevision`: when nothing changed the answer is only `{ id, revision, notModified: true }`. A stored contract this daemon holds without running carries `held` with `code` (`input-unavailable`: its recorded input could not be restored, and `contracts.cancel` ends it; `claim-unavailable`: no run claim could be taken) and the `reason`. 404 with CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND when no runner on this daemon holds the id.

errorCodes.meaning: No runner on this daemon holds that contract id.

methods.title: List Contract Summaries
methods.description: The contracts `contracts.list` returns (same `sessionId` and `includeTerminal`), newest first, each as a small summary: id, session, owner agent, origin, ask, goal, status and status line, failure, group and unit counts, open owner question ids and the newest open question, usage, created, ended and last-changed times, and a `revision` that changes whenever any of these does. Nothing of the evidence, readings or history is sent; read one contract's tree with `contracts.get`.

methods.title: Current Auth Context
methods.description: Return the current control-plane principal, granted scopes, and authentication mode.

methods.title: Login
methods.description: Authenticate a local control-plane user and create a session token. The first sign-in with the generated first-run password (the owner account, `auth-bootstrap.txt`) also sets the owner's own password: send it as newPassword; without it the answer is 409 FIRST_SIGN_IN_SETS_PASSWORD and no session is made. Setting it removes the first-run file, and the generated password no longer signs in.

methods.title: Logout
methods.description: End the sign-in session that authenticates this request (its bearer or session cookie) and expire the session cookie. Any signed-in user may end their own session; ending another session is local_auth.sessions.delete (admin). A credential that is not a live sign-in session is answered 401 SESSION_UNKNOWN.

methods.title: List Control-Plane Clients
methods.description: Return authenticated and recently connected control-plane clients.

methods.title: Operator Contract
methods.description: Return the operator-facing control-plane contract manifest, including auth, transport, method, and event metadata.

methods.title: List Gateway Events
methods.description: Return the event catalog for SSE and WebSocket control-plane subscriptions.

methods.title: Open Control-Plane Event Stream
methods.description: Open the SSE control-plane event stream.

methods.title: List Control-Plane Messages
methods.description: Return recent surface messages published through the control plane.

methods.title: Get Gateway Method
methods.description: Return a single gateway method descriptor.

methods.title: List Gateway Methods
methods.description: Return the gateway method catalog.

methods.title: Control-Plane Snapshot
methods.description: Return the current control-plane gateway snapshot.

methods.title: Daemon Status
methods.description: Return daemon status and version. THREE version fields, because there are two versions and they are not the same number: `buildVersion` is the running artifact's own release version, what a person installed, and what the auto-update loop compares against release tags, and `platformVersion` is the platform build it is composed from. `version` carries the build version and exists because every client already reads it; on an embedded daemon that ships no artifact of its own, all three are the platform build. Pass receipts=peek to also receive undelivered daemon receipts (update/crash/migration notices) without consuming them, then receipts=ack&ids=<id>,<id> once they are shown, so a response lost in transit is offered again. Without the flag no receipts are returned or marked, so identity probes and keepalives never take them.

receipts.description: Omit for a read that never touches receipts. "peek" returns undelivered daemon receipts without marking them; "ack" (with ids) marks exactly those delivered, once the reader has shown them.

ids.description: With receipts=ack: comma-separated receipt ids to mark delivered, as receipts=peek returned them (at most 200 per call).

methods.title: Open the Web App
methods.description: Open the web app on the approval (`approval`) or session (`session`) the link names: a 302 redirect to the web app when the daemon serves it (controlPlane.webui.serve) or knows where it runs (a user-set web.publicBaseUrl, or web.enabled with web.host/web.port). With no web app known, returns the control plane's built-in HTML page. Answered before authentication; the page signs in on its own.

methods.title: List Relay Codes
methods.description: List the relay codes this daemon issued, one per device paired through the relay (relay.pairing.mint), as redacted views: id, name, created time and, when the device has used it, the last time a relayed request presented it. The code itself is never stored in listable form and is never returned.

methods.title: Revoke Relay Code
methods.description: Revoke one device's relay code. Revocation is immediate: every relay connection the code opened is closed at once (each open stream gets a stream-close with reason relay-code-revoked, its in-flight requests are aborted; `closedConnections` counts them), the device's next request through the relay is refused with 401 RELAY_CODE_REVOKED, and every other device keeps working. The device reaches the daemon through the relay again only after pairing again on the home network. An unknown id is a 404 RELAY_CODE_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop.

errorCodes.meaning: No relay code has that id; list the codes with relay.codes.list and revoke an id it shows.
The revocation could not be written to the authority record, so nothing was revoked and the device keeps relay access; try again.
The code is revoked and refused, and its connections were closed, but it could not be removed from the relay codes file; revoke the same id again to retry the removal.

methods.title: Mint A Relay Pairing Payload
methods.description: Return the pairing payload one device scans to reach this daemon through the relay: the relay URL to dial, the rendezvous id the daemon registered under, the daemon's static public key, and a relay code issued for this device alone (returned once; only its hash is kept). Every request the device tunnels through the relay presents that code, and the daemon refuses one whose code it did not issue or has revoked (401 RELAY_CODE_REVOKED), so one phone is cut off with relay.codes.revoke while every other keeps working. `name` labels the code in relay.codes.list (default: "Relay device" and the time). `codeId` and `codeName` name the code minted. `turnOn: true` is the owner's yes to letting devices reach this machine through the relay, asked by the caller first (the ask opens on No): when the relay is off, the daemon sets `relay.enabled` (which also backs the relay-connect capability) and `relay.url` from `url` (the relay's wss:// address; needed only when none is set), and the registration starts without a restart. A registration that is on its way (`idle`, `connecting`, `reconnecting`) is waited for in the same call, with no timer, until the host's own answer: `registered` mints the pairing, `refused` or `failed` answers with `pairing` null and that status (relay.reachability.get then says why). The wait ends with the caller. While it waits, every status change is announced as LIST_CHANGED with `list: "relay"`, and relay.reachability.get answers `words`, the status in plain words with the relay's address (`The relay at <url> is not answering yet; GoodVibes keeps trying.`), for the waiting screen. `words` is on this answer too. `pairing` is null, not an error, and no code is kept, when there is no live registration to mint against: the relay is off and `turnOn` was not sent, or the relay refused it. Minting does not create a second identity or a second registration; it describes the one that exists. 400 RELAY_URL_REQUIRED when `turnOn` is sent, no relay address is set and `url` is empty. 409 RELAY_CODE_LIMIT when 64 codes are held.

errorCodes.meaning: The daemon already holds 64 relay codes, so no new device can pair; revoke the ones no device uses (relay.codes.list, relay.codes.revoke), then pair again.
The authority record could not be read, so no relay code was issued and nothing was paired; check the record file, then pair again.
turnOn was sent, but no relay address is set on the daemon and none was given; send the relay's wss:// address as url.

methods.title: Relay Reachability
methods.description: Whether this daemon is registered with the relay, and what state its registration is in. `disabled` is a distinct answer from every other one and the distinction is the point: it means a gate is off, `relay.enabled`, the relay-connect capability, or an empty `relay.url`, rather than that a connection is failing. `idle` means the gates are open and nothing has started; `connecting`, `registered` and `reconnecting` are the live registration; `refused` means the relay refused the registration for a reason another attempt cannot clear, and the daemon stops dialling until the relay settings or identity change; `stopped` is a controller that was told to stop. `configured` says whether all three gates are open, so a caller can render "turn it on" instead of "it is broken". `rendezvousId`, present while a registration is running, is the id the daemon is registered under, derived from its relay identity key; it is the id a pairing payload carries and a step-up challenge is bound to. `refusal`, present after the relay refused the registration, says why (`state`), what to do (`next`) and whether the daemon keeps trying (`retryable`). ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: Check For An Update Now
methods.description: Run one update check immediately instead of waiting for the next interval, and return the status afterwards. This is the same tick the schedule runs, so an on-demand check and the hourly one cannot reach different conclusions. It never forces an install: a found release still waits for a moment when no work is in flight, which the returned `pendingVersion` reports. A check that fails is reported in `failedCheckCount` and `lastCheckFailure` rather than refused, the caller asked what the state is, and "the check failed" is the answer. `check` says what the call did: `ran` (a check ran now), `already-in-flight` (another check was still running, none was started, and the rest of the answer is as of now) or `loop-off` (no loop is armed, `offReason` says why, and nothing ran) or `installing` (a check ran now, found `pendingVersion`, and the daemon is installing it and will restart into it; this answer is sent before the install starts, so the daemon stops answering shortly after it).

methods.title: Self-Update Status
methods.description: Whether this daemon is keeping itself current, and, when it is not, the reason in one line. `armed` is false whenever no loop is running and `offReason` says which gate stopped it: update.auto not set, no artifact identity (a host that manages its own updates), or no release URL to resolve tags from. `failedCheckCount` with `lastCheckFailure` is the case that used to be invisible: checks running on schedule and failing every time, which looks exactly like having nothing to update to. `pendingVersion` is a release that was found and waits for a moment when no work is in flight before it is downloaded and installed; `installing` is a release being downloaded and installed now, with `receivedBytes` (bytes of release files received so far), `file` (the release file that last received bytes), `fileReceivedBytes` and `fileTotalBytes` (how much of that file has arrived, and its size, null when the server did not send one), `fileNumber` and `fileCount` (which of the release's files that is, counting from 1 in download order, and how many it downloads; null when not known) and `since` (when the install began, epoch ms), and is null when none runs (no clock ends a download: it runs until it finishes, the connection fails, or the daemon stops); `pendingSince` says since when a release has waited and `pendingBlockedBy` names the fleet ids of the work it waits behind (the owner is told once after 24 hours). `rejectedVersion` is a release that was installed here, failed to start, and was rolled back, it is deliberately not reinstalled. `recoveryRequired` (true) and `transactionRecovery` appear only while an interrupted update or rollback fences the loop: `transactionRecovery.recoveryPaths` lists the retained files to inspect, `recoveryErrors` what went wrong, and the loop stays off until they are dealt with.

methods.title: Get Cost Attribution
methods.description: Return windowed (24h/7d) cost attribution over observed LLM usage, grouped by a dimension (agent, tool, hook, mcp, model, provider, session, or source: what it was for, a schedule, a piece of work, a web chat, a shared session or a conversation), each row naming the models that spent it and whether each has a price, with cache-aware pricing (fresh input vs cache-read vs cache-write). Honest-unpriced: an unknown model contributes to unpricedRecordCount with a null cost, never a fabricated amount; costState is priced, unpriced, or estimated (a mix). totalCostUsd is null when every contributor is unpriced.

methods.title: Get Delivery
methods.description: Return a single delivery record. It names its recipient (address and label), so it needs read:automation-content.

methods.title: List Deliveries
methods.description: Return delivery records and integration snapshot data. Each attempt names its recipient (address and label), so it needs read:automation-content.

methods.title: List Failed Notifications
methods.description: Outbound notifications (Slack, Discord, webhooks) that failed every attempt, oldest first. They are kept across restarts until resent. Each entry gives the channel, the event, what it said in metadata-only form, when it failed, the attempt count and the last error (HTTP status when there was one). Pass `channel` (slack, discord or webhook) to list one. Resend with notifications.deadLetters.replay.

methods.title: Resend Failed Notifications
methods.description: Send failed notifications again: those named in `ids`, or all of them when `ids` is absent. Each is queued with a fresh retry budget; the result per id is delivered, retrying (still queued), dead_letter (failed again and back in the list), not-found, or destination-changed: the Slack or Discord channel now posts somewhere other than where the notification failed (another webhook, another default channel, or none), so it was not sent and stays in the list, with `reason` and `changes` naming the old and new destination. Pass toCurrent: true to send those to the destination configured now. A webhook notification is not sent to a URL that was removed since it failed. A queued retry is likewise never sent to a destination that changed while it waited: it ends in the list with the reason.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Send a Program Notice
methods.description: A terminal program (the terminal app, the Agent) sends a notice of its own event (a turn that ended, an approval waiting, a budget reached, an agent that failed, or the model's own words through its notify tool) to the daemon's one list of webhook addresses (notifications.webhookUrls) and, for a turn, approval or budget notice, to the Slack and Discord channels the daemon posts notifications to. Facts are worded by the daemon under "metadata only" as it is set now. A typed notice is queued and retried; one that fails every attempt is kept in the daemon's failed notifications (notifications.deadLetters.list). A text notice is one attempt, reported per address. No address is returned.

methods.title: Download an Email Attachment
methods.description: Return one attachment of an inbox message as base64 bytes, by UID and its position (from 0) in the attachments list email.inbox.read returns. uidValidity is required: the mailbox generation email.inbox.read returned with the message, so a reset mailbox refuses with nothing downloaded instead of handing over an attachment of whichever message now holds that UID. Read-only (BODY.PEEK). Meant to be saved as a file, never rendered: the bytes are whatever the sender attached. Attachments over 25 MB are refused with the reason.

methods.title: Create Email Draft
methods.description: Append a draft message to the configured IMAP Drafts folder. Distinct from the local channel draft store. A draft is never sent by this verb and takes no confirmation field. To change a saved draft, use email.draft.update with its uid and uidValidity: a second create leaves two drafts. A save the mail server refused is reported as not saved, with the cause from its response code (mailbox full, Drafts folder missing, draft too large, or refused). A save whose answer from the mail server was lost is reported as one that may have been saved, never as not saved; creating the same draft again in this daemon run looks for it in the Drafts folder first (by the Message-ID it was saved under) and returns it instead of saving a second copy.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Replace an Email Draft
methods.description: Replace one saved draft in the IMAP Drafts folder with an edited one, so the folder keeps one copy: the edited message is appended, then the draft named by `uid` is removed. `uid` and `uidValidity` are what email.drafts.list (or email.draft.create) returned; a reset Drafts folder or a draft that is gone is refused with nothing changed, and a server that cannot remove one message by UID (no UIDPLUS) is refused before anything is written. A save whose answer was lost is reported as one that may have been saved; replacing the same draft with the same edit again in this daemon run looks for the edited copy first and does not save it twice. A draft is never sent by this verb. Answers the new draft's { draftId, uid?, uidValidity?, mailbox } and `replaced`, the UID removed.

methods.title: List Email Drafts
methods.description: Return the newest drafts (default 25, at most 100) in the account's Drafts folder, newest first, each with its recipient, subject, date, the Message-ID it replies to and up to 64 KB of body text, so a draft can be reopened in a composer; `uidValidity` is the Drafts folder generation the UIDs belong to, which email.draft.update needs to replace one. `before` (a UID) reads the page of drafts older than it: pass the smallest UID of a page to read the one before, until `total` drafts are read. Read-only.

methods.title: Cancel Verification Expectation
methods.description: Close an expectation the workstream abandoned. A signup dropped before submission otherwise leaves a live correlation key for an address nobody is waiting on, occupying one of the bounded open slots until its window elapses. Cancelling an id that is not open is an answer, not a failure.

methods.title: List Verification Expectations
methods.description: Return every open verification expectation with its recipient, service domain, purpose and remaining window. Disclosure: an expectation is a live correlation key, and the owner is entitled to see which ones exist.

methods.title: Open Verification Expectation
methods.description: Register, in advance, that a verification message is expected at one address from one service domain, within a bounded window. Called by the workstream that already holds authority BEFORE it submits the signup or checkout form. Grants evidence-only authority: a matching message proves control of the address and can never start work, widen the expectation or extend its window. The answer carries `watching`: whether a mailbox is being read right now and, when not, why. Opening is not refused while nothing watches (a cluster standby legitimately does not), but a message cannot arrive then.

methods.title: Wait For Verification Message
methods.description: Where one expectation stands, waiting up to timeoutMs (default 0, at most 60000) for it to change. state "arrived" carries the verification link or code the daemon took from the matching message (token); "waiting" lists matching messages that held none (arrivals); "expired", "capability-lost" and "cancelled" say how it ended, with detail; "replaced" means a later email.expectation.open for the same address replaced it, and replacedBy is the id to wait on instead; "unknown" means no expectation with that id is open or remembered. watching says whether a mailbox is being read right now, so "nothing yet" is never confused with "nobody is looking". Call it again while the state is "waiting".

methods.title: Inbound Mail Status
methods.description: Disclose the inbound-mail watcher: whether it is running and why, which source is reading the mailbox and the delay that source actually costs, the current capability verdict, every persisted cursor with its position and age, every open verification expectation with its remaining window, whether each store could be read, whether arriving mail is actually being announced to the owner, and what each store retains before it is reaped. Read-only.

methods.title: List Email Inbox
methods.description: Return inbox message summaries fetched live from the configured IMAP account, newest first (ordered by server-assigned UID, never by the sender-written Date header). Read-only (EXAMINE / BODY.PEEK); never marks messages read. `before` pages backwards: pass the smallest UID of the page you have to get the next older page; `total` counts every match. When the server answered for a message and the daemon could not read the answer, the page is short and `unreadable` says so, an omitted message is not by itself evidence that it was deleted. A message the daemon's inbox mirror has labelled carries `triageLabel` (spam, priority or normal); one not labelled yet has none. A message the mirror holds carries `screening`: `screened`, or `not-screened` when only code checked it for credential and card text, with `screeningReason`. `uidValidity` is the mailbox generation the page's UIDs belong to (absent only when the server reports none); email.inbox.update needs it.

methods.title: Read Email Message
methods.description: Return the full body and attachment metadata for a single inbox message by IMAP UID, with `uidValidity`, the mailbox generation it was read under (email.inbox.update needs it). Read-only (BODY.PEEK; does not mark as read).

methods.title: Mark, Archive or Delete an Email
methods.description: Change one inbox message by IMAP UID: action seen or unseen sets or clears its read flag; archive moves it to the folder the server marks Archive (or All Mail); delete moves it to the folder the server marks Trash, so it can be recovered there. A server with no such folder is refused and nothing changes; nothing here expunges permanently. uidValidity is required: the mailbox generation email.inbox.list or email.inbox.read returned with the uid, so a reset mailbox refuses instead of changing whichever message now holds that UID. Answers { uid, action, movedTo? }.

methods.title: Send Email
methods.description: Send a composed email via the configured SMTP account. Irreversible external send; requires confirm: true and explicit user review of recipients and body. Pass a clientSendId (8-128 letters, digits, - or _) chosen when the message was composed: a repeat with the same id and the same message within ten minutes returns the first answer, marked repeated: true, instead of sending again (the id also becomes the Message-ID), and the same id with a different message is refused (409 CLIENT_SEND_ID_REUSED). A send whose final server reply was lost fails with EMAIL_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED: it may have gone, and repeating it with the same id will not send it twice.

replay.name: clientSendId
replay.behavior: A repeat with the same `clientSendId` and the same message within ten minutes returns the first answer instead of sending again; the same id with a different message is 409 CLIENT_SEND_ID_REUSED.

methods.title: Feature Defaults Report
methods.description: Return the feature defaults report: every platform capability with its current default, default-disposition state (dark = default-off with no evidence, soaking = accumulating evidence, graduate-candidate = judged ready and awaiting a release decision, graduated = default on, blocked = held off with a dated reason), and its validation evidence. The daemon collects no validation readings, so every entry's evidence says "no evidence collected"; the only instrumentation, the permissions divergence simulation, runs with "See what the candidate policy changes" (the capability security.simulate-policy) and reports there. releaseBlockers lists every graduate-candidate entry: capabilities judged ready that are neither on by default nor held with a dated reason.

methods.title: Feature Restart Status
methods.description: Return the features whose saved setting the running daemon has not applied yet. A feature that only changes at daemon start keeps its running state when its setting is saved; each entry names the feature id (the id settings surfaces render), the state it is running in and the saved state that takes effect at the next daemon restart. An empty list means every feature runs as saved. config.get returns saved values only; read this beside it to learn what is running.

methods.title: Archive Finished Fleet Subtree
methods.description: Move one FINISHED process subtree (root id + all descendants, every node terminal) out of the live fleet view into the session archive. Honest refusal (archived:false + reason) for an unknown id or a subtree with live members. Archived nodes stay inspectable via fleet.archived.list.

methods.title: List Archived Fleet Processes
methods.description: Return the session-archived process nodes (same node shape as fleet.snapshot; still live-derived from the source managers, so usage/cost stay current).

methods.title: Archive All Finished Fleet Subtrees
methods.description: Archive every root subtree whose nodes are all terminal (done/failed/killed/interrupted). A finished member of a still-running swarm stays with its parent. Returns the number of nodes archived.

methods.title: Propose a Best-of-N Winner (Model Judgment)
methods.description: Run the optional judge model over a best-of-N group's candidates (a paid model call that also records the proposal on the group) and PROPOSE a winner, with reasons. The output is explicitly model judgment (scoredBy:"model"), it never auto-picks unless the source item opted into auto-accept; a human still confirms via fleet.attempts.pick. An engine with no judge configured returns an honest 501.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: List Best-of-N Held-Merge Groups
methods.description: Return the best-of-N attempt groups whose siblings ran in isolated worktrees and are HELD for a winner pick instead of auto-merging (optionally filtered to one workstream). Each group lists its candidates with their per-attempt diff, usage, and outcome, plus any prior judge proposal. Read-only.

methods.title: Pick a Best-of-N Winner
methods.description: Accept one attempt as the winner of its best-of-N group. Without `confirm: true` nothing is merged or cleaned: the call returns `applied: false` and `requiresConfirm: true` with the group's candidates as a preview, so check `applied` before reporting a winner as picked. With `confirm: true` its worktree branch is merged through the existing sequential integration lane and every losing sibling's worktree is cleaned; `losers` reports each clean-up as observed: `done` (worktree seen gone), `pending` (still cleaning after ten seconds; `check` names what to run), or `failed` (kept or not cleaned, with its refusal). The winner must be a held (passed) candidate of a group whose siblings are all terminal, an unknown/not-ready group or an invalid winner is an honest 409, never a partial merge.

methods.title: List Merge-Conflict Rows
methods.description: Return every work item whose integration merge CONFLICTED and is waiting on a human: the kept worktree path, item branch, the STRUCTURED conflicting-file list, and the resolution session id once one was spawned. Optionally filtered to one workstream. Read-only.

methods.title: Spawn a Conflict-Resolution Session
methods.description: The conflict row's one action: spawn a resolution session INSIDE the kept worktree, seeded with the structured conflict list and tree path (the same seeded-session machinery as the CI fix flow), and stamp the REAL session id back onto the item. When the resolution session ends with success, the merge is retried automatically (also after a daemon restart) and a clean merge reclaims the kept tree; otherwise fleet.conflicts.retry retries it. An item with no unresolved conflict is an honest 409, as is an item whose merge is being retried. When the conflict ends while the session starts (its merge landed meanwhile), the session is stopped and the call is refused with 409 CONFLICT_RESOLVED_ELSEWHERE.

replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. methods.title: Retry a Conflicted Merge
methods.description: Attempt the integration merge of a conflicted item again, for a conflict resolved by hand in the kept worktree or by a resolution session that ended without a clean re-merge. Answers outcome merged (the kept tree is reclaimed), conflict (still conflicted; the row stays) or not-conflicted (nothing to retry). Refused with 409 while that item's resolution session is still running or being started, or while another retry of it runs.

methods.title: Get Workstream Task Graph
methods.description: The dependency-graph view of one workstream: nodes (id, title, state, cluster, files, merge state, blocked reason, orphaned flag, deepest-remaining-path depth, stalled tell, agent), edges (from depends on to), and the elastic-pool state (ready/running counts, at-cap, cap key + size, any spawn refusal). Surfaces render the task graph under the chain from this, the fleet/observability idiom. 404 when the workstream is unknown to this daemon.

methods.title: Interrupt a Fleet Node
methods.description: Gracefully interrupt one fleet node: an agent ends its current turn, a trigger or schedule is paused. Answers the node ids acted on. A node whose capabilities do not include interruptible is refused with FLEET_ACTION_UNAVAILABLE; an unknown id with FLEET_NODE_NOT_FOUND.

methods.title: List Fleet Processes
methods.description: Paginated, filtered (kinds/states) query over the live process registry. Cursor pagination returns disjoint pages that union to the full matching set at query time.

methods.title: Steer an Observed Foreign Agent
methods.description: Type text into an externally-launched coding-agent session goodvibes only OBSERVES (a Claude Code / Codex process it did not spawn or host), over the session's own control channel (a tmux pane). That agent runs with its own permissions, so every steer is first put to the owner through the approval broker, naming the session, its directory, the exact text and whether it is submitted; "always" for that session holds until the daemon stops, for that exact process only (pid with its start time, pane, kind, directory and command line), so a new process that reuses the pid is asked about again, and it is not offered when the start time is unknown. The text is typed only; it is submitted with Enter only when submit is true. queued:false with an honest reason when the owner declines, the row exposes no channel, or the first send fails; nothing was sent then. queued:"partial" when the text (and maybe one Enter) reached the pane and a later send failed: `sent` lists the steps that went out, `failed` the one that did not; do not send the same steer again, finish it in the pane. STOP is never offered on an observed row.

methods.title: Resume a Fleet Node
methods.description: Re-arm one paused trigger or schedule (for a trigger with an open breaker, this is the reset the breaker waits for). Answers the node ids acted on. A node whose capabilities do not include resumable is refused with FLEET_ACTION_UNAVAILABLE; an unknown id with FLEET_NODE_NOT_FOUND.

methods.title: Fleet Snapshot
methods.description: Return a point-in-time capture of every live/completed runtime process (agents, contracts with their groups and units, workflow FSMs/triggers/schedules, watchers, background processes) as a flat, parentId-linked node list. Capped at 2000 nodes (truncated:true + totalCount when the live fleet exceeds the cap), use fleet.list to page through a larger fleet.

methods.title: Stop a Fleet Node
methods.description: Hard-stop one fleet node through its owning manager (agent cancel, background process stop, watcher stop, workflow cancel, trigger or schedule remove, contract cancel, hosted ACP agent stop). `cascade: true` stops its descendants first. Answers the node ids actually acted on. A node whose capabilities do not include killable is refused with FLEET_ACTION_UNAVAILABLE; an unknown id with FLEET_NODE_NOT_FOUND.

methods.title: Restore Archived Fleet Subtree
methods.description: Return an archived subtree to the live fleet view. Returns the number of nodes restored (0 when nothing under the id was archived).

methods.title: Health Snapshot
methods.description: Return the health integration snapshot.

methods.title: Diagnose a Symptom
methods.description: Find the runbook for a symptom in plain words (for example "stuck turn", "mcp keeps disconnecting", "approval never answered", "compaction failed") and run its checks against the daemon's live state. Each check is pass, fail or unknown (it could not look), with a one-line summary; each runbook lists the next steps as real commands. Read-only, no model request. An empty `playbooks` means nothing matched; `available` lists what can be diagnosed.

methods.title: Get Memory Governance State
methods.description: The MemoryGovernor snapshot: the current memory-pressure tier and budget, resident set size and heap, the tier thresholds and hard limit in force, per-cache footprints the governor can shrink, which deferrable background jobs are paused, and the leak-tripwire state. When memory.budgetMb, memory.tier.* or memory.hardLimitPct were refused, `configFallback` names the settings and why; the shipped values shown are in force until the setting is fixed and the daemon restarts. Read-only observability so operators can see the daemon shedding memory before it approaches OOM.

methods.title: Set the Owner Keep-Awake Toggle
methods.description: Turn the owner keep-awake toggle on or off: a daemon-held sleep inhibitor INDEPENDENT of work state, surviving surface closes, persisted as power.keepAwake. Covers idle + sleep + lid-switch classes where grantable; the returned state names any refused class honestly. No timers, no AC-only sub-options, the always-visible chip is the safety mechanism. Emits runtime.ops OPS_POWER_STATE_CHANGED so every attached surface updates its chip.

methods.title: Get Sleep-Ownership State
methods.description: The host sleep-ownership state: whether the automatic work inhibitor is held (and the live "held because X" reasons, cap, and expiry), and the owner keep-awake toggle with the classes the OS actually granted vs refused, a refused lid-switch block is stated honestly ("idle sleep blocked; lid-close suspend is controlled by your OS here"), never papered over. sleepEdge says whether work is checkpointed before sleep and caught up on wake, and its note says why not when it cannot be. Surfaces render the always-visible "sleep disabled" chip from this state and the runtime.ops OPS_POWER_STATE_CHANGED event.

methods.title: Read the Runtime State
methods.description: What the daemon's runtime store holds now, by domain (session, conversation, agents, tasks, permissions and the rest), for debugging. domains names the ones to read, comma-separated; without it every domain is read, and available lists them all. The data is made safe on the way out: dates are ISO text, errors { name, message }, binary data "<N bytes>"; credential fields read [REDACTED] and owner-profile fields [REDACTED_PROFILE], and credential-shaped text is masked; nesting and total size are bounded, a cut value reads "[Truncated]" and truncated is true. unknown lists asked-for domains the store does not hold. Read-only.

methods.title: Install the Managed Local-Voice Runtime
methods.description: Starts the one-act setup and answers at once with the run it started (or the run already in progress it joined); the install runs on in the daemon, voice.local.status serves its live progress as installInProgress and, when it ends, its receipt as lastInstall. The setup: download + checksum-verify the piper TTS engine, a default voice, and (where a pinned goodvibes-built bundle exists) the whisper.cpp STT engine with its default model into the goodvibes-managed directory, then point the voice.local.* config keys at the managed install, never overwriting a key you already set to a custom value (skipped keys are reported). The install ends by speaking a test phrase and reading it back: the transcript is compared word by word in code, allowing one differing word, and the receipt carries the transcript and the comparison. Downloads only when you ask; a failed or checksum-mismatched download keeps nothing.

methods.title: Get Managed Local-Voice Runtime State
methods.description: Whether the managed local voice runtime (piper TTS + a default voice) is installed: not-provisioned (with a size-labeled offer), partial, provisioned, or unsupported-platform. STT (whisper.cpp) reports its own managed state: goodvibes builds and pins the whisper.cpp bundle per platform (no official prebuilt exists; provisioning never compiles on your machine), so where a pinned bundle exists STT provisions like TTS, and elsewhere it reports unsupported honestly. While a voice.local.install run is active, the response also carries installInProgress, the live per-component progress (phase, byte sizes where known) of that run, so surfaces poll this read during the install to render real progress; the section is absent when no install is running. Once a run ends, lastInstall carries its receipt (or the reason it stopped without one) with the run's start and finish times; a surface that started an install reads its result here. Read-only.

methods.title: Set Up Voice
methods.description: Sets voice up for what was asked: intent wake (this surface listens for the wake word; implies speech-to-text), stt, tts or voice (all of it), for the surface named (tui, agent, webui, app), which is the one that ends up listening. The plan is decided from this host's own facts (wake rows, wake models on disk, the managed speech runtimes, the input device); steps that need no answer are done at once (the wake rows are set, missing wake models are fetched), and the answer lists each step: do (done, or why it could not be), propose (acceptProposals: true does it) and ask (ttsChoice answers the text-to-speech question: local or a cloud provider this host holds a credential for). An install the plan needs is started and not waited for: installStarted names the run, and voice.local.status serves its progress and receipt. rendered is the plan as one reply a surface prints as-is; complete is true when nothing is left to answer and every step that ran finished.

methods.title: Read Wake-Word Model Bytes
methods.description: Read one provisioned wake artifact in bounded chunks, for a surface that cannot fetch it itself, a browser tab, whose cross-origin fetch of the release asset is refused because that asset answers with no CORS header. Each chunk carries the offset, the whole artifact's size, and its PINNED sha256, so a client reassembles the file and verifies it against the pin: a truncated transfer fails at the consumer instead of loading as a model that silently never detects. Both classifier formats are served, "classifier" is the onnx build a browser tab loads, "tflite" the same classifier for a runtime that cannot, as is the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs ("vad"), and so is the attribution NOTICE of each redistributable artifact ("notice" for the classifier, "embedding-notice" for the front end, "vad-notice" for the gate), because a client that can fetch the bytes but not the NOTICE cannot satisfy the terms it received them under. Serves what is on disk and does not download; installation puts it there, and voice.wake.provision is the recovery path when it is missing.

methods.title: Download the Wake-Word Models
methods.description: Download and checksum-verify the pinned wake-word classifier in both runtime formats (onnx and tflite), the speech-embedding front end, the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs, and the attribution NOTICE of each, into the goodvibes-managed directory, about 6.1 MB. Installing goodvibes already does this, and a daemon retries at boot, so this verb is the RECOVERY path: an install that was offline, an artifact that failed verification, or a re-provision after the pinned model changes. Resumable by re-running: an artifact that already matches its pin is skipped, and one that is present but fails verification is replaced rather than used. A failed or mismatched download keeps nothing at the destination. Single-flight: two surfaces asking at once, or a boot attempt and a user asking, join one download instead of racing for the same files.

methods.title: Get Wake-Word Model State
methods.description: Whether the pinned wake-word artifacts are on disk and VERIFIED BY CONTENT: the "hey goodvibes" classifier, the tflite form of the same classifier, the speech-embedding front end the classifier sits behind, the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs, and the attribution NOTICE belonging to each of the three redistributable artifacts (the classifier's, the front end's and the gate's). Each reports verified, corrupt (present but failing its checksum, a truncated or swapped file, distinct from missing) and its byte size, with the total a fresh provision would download. Installing goodvibes provisions these, and a daemon retries at boot whatever the install could not fetch, so on a normal machine this reads ready without anyone having run a setup command; an offline install reports not-provisioned here until it is retried. The overall ready flag covers the classifier, the front end and both of THEIR NOTICEs, an artifact whose attribution is missing is not one this daemon may serve, and excludes two things: the tflite twin, which nothing here loads, so a host missing just that can still detect; and the speech gate, reported as vadReady instead, because voice.wake.vadThreshold defaults to 0 and the detector runs without it. Also restates that the model's published recall figures are measured on synthesised speech only, which any surface describing the model must carry. Never downloads. Read-only.

methods.title: Post Hook Runs
methods.description: A terminal program (the terminal app, the Agent) tells the daemon which hooks it ran: which hook, at which hook point, on what, when, and what it did (let the event go on, refused it, put it to the owner, changed its input, added context, failed). The daemon keeps one trace of every program's runs, newest first, and says the list changed (LIST_CHANGED hook-trace); the capability hooks.trace reads it. A run is kept once by its id, so a post sent again changes nothing. Up to 100 runs per post.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake cancel
methods.description: Close a review: the row leaves the queue at once, its place is freed and its original is released. Also withdraws a message still waiting for a decision.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake configure
methods.description: Select one Telegram chat (and thread) for delegated intake: its messages stop being handled normally and each one waits for the owner instead, held in memory only for pendingRetentionMs. The configuration ends after configurationLifetimeMs; the chat stays selected and held until released.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake decide
methods.description: Answer one waiting message: approve it with explicit retention choices (it enters the review queue as accepted-for-review) or deny it (its original is released). One decision per message; nothing is executed.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake list
methods.description: The review queue (accepted-for-review and reviewed rows) and the messages still waiting for the owner's decision, for the calling owner.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake read
methods.description: Read the original text of a message in the review queue while it is still in memory; the review is marked reviewed. Held with the reason when the original expired or was released.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake release
methods.description: Stop routing this chat through delegated intake and return it to normal handling. Pass the configurationId, or the chatId (and threadId) when no configuration exists.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake revoke
methods.description: End a configuration: no new message is captured. The chat stays selected and held (not answered normally) until inbound.telegram.release.

methods.title: Telegram Delegated Intake status
methods.description: Where one message stands: waiting for the owner, in the review queue (accepted-for-review or reviewed, with whether its original is still in memory), or held with the reason and next step.

methods.title: Intelligence Snapshot
methods.description: Return the intelligence integration snapshot.

methods.title: Run Browser Judgment Battery
methods.description: Run one explicitly installed, authorized browser battery. Unconfigured services and unresolved or unauthorized input remain held.

methods.title: Remove MCP Server
methods.description: Remove a project/global MCP server config and disconnect it without daemon restart.

methods.title: MCP Servers Reveal
methods.description: Return effective MCP config with environment and request-header VALUES (env, headers) and the unredacted url and args included, so an edit can resend them. Admin only, the redacted mcp.config.get view is what every other caller should use.

methods.title: Set an MCP Server's Role
methods.description: Keep a server's role (what kind of server it is) with its entry in the MCP config file that holds it and apply it at once, after a restart too; a role set for this daemon's session ends. The same as /mcp role <server> <role>.

methods.title: Block an MCP Tool
methods.description: Keep a block of one tool with its MCP server's entry in the config file that holds it (global or this project's .goodvibes/mcp.json) and apply it at once: every call to the tool is refused, whatever the server's trust level and limits allow, and a call not yet sent ends. A block replaces a kept exemption of the same tool. Refused for a server whose entry is in a file another program owns. The same as /mcp block <server> <tool> --keep.

methods.title: Let an MCP Tool Go Beyond Its Server's Limits
methods.description: Keep an exemption of one tool with its MCP server's entry in the owner's global MCP config and apply it at once: calls to the tool pass the server's folder and site limits. A blocked server, held-back tools and a block of the same tool still refuse. Loosens what the server may do, so it is the owner's own act: refused for the Agent's model and for a server kept in a project file. The same as /mcp exempt <server> <tool>.

methods.title: Stop Blocking an MCP Tool
methods.description: Drop the block kept for one tool with its MCP server's entry, and this daemon's block of it for its session, and apply it at once, so the server's trust level and limits decide the tool again. A kept exemption of the tool stays. Refused when the tool is not blocked. Loosens what the server may do, so it is the owner's own act: refused for the Agent's model. The same as /mcp unblock <server> <tool>.

methods.title: Make an MCP Tool Follow Its Server's Limits Again
methods.description: Drop the exemption kept for one tool with its MCP server's entry and apply it at once, so the server's folder and site limits hold the tool again. A kept block of the tool stays. Refused when the tool has no exemption. The same as /mcp unexempt <server> <tool>.

methods.title: Set an MCP Server's Trust Level
methods.description: Keep a server's trust level with its entry in the MCP config file that holds it and apply it at once, after a restart too; a level set for this daemon's session ends. allow-all is kept only in the owner's global file. A looser level loosens what the server may do, so it is the owner's own act: refused for the Agent's model. The same as /mcp trust <server> <mode>.

methods.title: Upsert MCP Server
methods.description: Persist a project/global MCP server config and reconnect the changed runtime server without daemon restart.

methods.title: MCP Tools List
methods.description: Return currently connected MCP tools.

methods.title: Analyze Media Artifact

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Collect Pending Media Job
methods.description: Finish a generation job an earlier media.generate answered as pending: pass the providerId, taskId and resume it named. Waits up to waitSeconds (0 checks once) and returns the outputs, or pending again when the job is still running. Nothing new is paid for.

methods.title: Generate Media Artifact
methods.description: Generate a media artifact through a registered media provider. A job the provider accepted but had not finished when the wait ended comes back with artifacts empty and pending set (providerId, taskId, resume); the job is paid for and keeps running, and media.collect finishes it. The kind asked for (the major type of outputMimeType, or image with options.image true) chooses the provider: without providerId the first configured provider that makes that kind is used, and when none does (or the named provider does not) the answer is 409 MEDIA_OUTPUT_UNAVAILABLE naming the providers that make it; nothing is sent.
