methods.title: Decide a Memory Consolidation Proposal
methods.description: Answer one pending consolidation proposal (memory.consolidation.receipts lists them with their `id`). The actions each kind accepts, `first`/`second` being the proposal's ids in order: contradiction keep-first | keep-second | both-stand; cross-scope-duplicate keep-first | keep-second | keep-both; stale-delete delete | keep. Keeping one record marks the other stale (recoverable); delete removes the record; both-stand and keep-both mark the records reviewed and record the decision, so the proposal is not raised again. Answers decided:true with the records changed and removed, or decided:false with a refusal (code, state, reason, next) and nothing changed. ws-only invoke verb.

methods.title: Memory Consolidation Receipts
methods.description: Return the retained memory-consolidation run receipts (what each idle/scheduled pass scanned, merged, archived, decayed) and the pending judgment PROPOSALS they carry (contradictions, cross-scope duplicates), the records a proposal references are already marked into the review queue, and a human resolves them through the confirmation-gated review route. A runtime without the consolidation scheduler answers an honest 501.

methods.title: Memory Doctor
methods.description: Return sqlite-vec and memory embedding-provider diagnostics.

methods.title: Set Default Memory Embedding Provider
methods.description: Set the active default memory embedding provider.

methods.title: Get Memory Projection
methods.description: Return one standing record's projection by id: its metadata entry plus the exact markdown the file projection would write (front-matter + content, with the live temporal status labelled). Returns 404 when no standing (project/team) record has that id, a session-scope or unknown id is an honest miss, never an empty projection.

methods.title: List Memory Projections
methods.description: Return the live projection of standing (project/team-scope) memory records, one metadata entry per record (id, filename, scope, class, summary, tags, confidence, review state, temporal validity + status), oldest first. This is the read view over the same standing memory the file projection writes as markdown; session-scope records are excluded (they are not standing memory). Computed live from the store, never read from disk, so it always matches the current records. An expired record is present with status:"expired" rather than silently dropped.

methods.title: Add Memory Record
methods.description: Add a memory record to the daemon-owned canonical store. The daemon is the single writer for its store; a client surface routes its writes here instead of opening the store file, so two processes never write the same sql.js file. New records default to confidence 60 (the recall floor) and reviewState fresh unless the review block overrides them. An optional caller-generated id (mem_<base36 time>_<8 hex>) makes the add safe to resend: the same id with the same record returns the stored row, the same id with a different record is refused.

replay.name: id
replay.behavior: An add that names a caller-generated `id` (mem_<base36 time>_<8 hex>) stores the memory once: a repeat with the same id and the same record returns the stored row, and the same id with a different record is refused. Without an id each call stores a new memory.

methods.title: Delete Memory Record
methods.description: Permanently delete a memory record and its links from the canonical store. Delete means delete: the record is removed from the store and the semantic index, not merely flagged. Returns { deleted: false } when no record with that id existed, an honest boolean, never a 200 that pretends a phantom row was removed.

methods.title: Export Memory Bundle
methods.description: Export a no-loss bundle (records + links) for the given filter from the canonical store. The bundle round-trips through import id-keyed, so it is the wire form of the cross-surface fold/reconcile seam. Read-only.

methods.title: Get Memory Record
methods.description: Return a single memory record by id from the canonical store, or 404 when no record with that id exists.

methods.title: Import Memory Bundle
methods.description: Import a bundle into the canonical store as an id-keyed union: an id already present is left untouched (counted skipped), a new id is added; a link is added only when both its endpoints exist. Never overwrites, never deletes, idempotent on re-run. The daemon is the single writer, so a client imports here instead of writing the store file.

methods.title: Link Memory Records
methods.description: Create a directed relation (e.g. "supersedes", "caused") from the path record to a target record. Returns 404 when either endpoint does not exist, never a 200 that pretends a link was made between records that do not both exist.

methods.title: List Memory Record Links
methods.description: Return every link where the record is the source or the target. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists, an honest not-found, distinct from a record that exists but has no links (an empty array).

methods.title: List Memory Records
methods.description: Bulk read from the canonical store: a literal (non-semantic) search returning the matching records as a plain array. A call that names a project (its call context, or project in the filter) reads that project's records and the ones that belong to no project; a call naming none reads only the records that belong to no project; everyProject (you, from any of your credentials: your place's "Every project") reads every record. This is the read a client surface uses instead of opening the store file for its browse/list and knowledge-injection paths.

methods.title: Search Memory Records
methods.description: Search the canonical store, literal or semantic. When semantic is requested but the semantic index cannot be consulted, the search falls back to a literal scan and states the reason in indexUnavailableReason rather than returning a silent empty result that reads as "nothing was ever stored". With recall=true the cross-surface recall-honesty contract is applied: flagged (stale/contradicted) records are excluded outright and records below the 60% confidence floor are dropped, each exclusion counted honestly.

methods.title: Semantic Search Memory Records
methods.description: Rank records by semantic similarity against the query, returning scored results (distance, similarity, score). When the query has no vector match the store falls back to a lexical ranking rather than a silent empty. distance is null for a fallback (non-vector) result. Read-only against the daemon's canonical index.

methods.title: Update Memory Record
methods.description: Edit a record's content fields (class, scope, summary, detail, tags) and its temporal validity window (validFrom, validUntil) in the canonical store; a changed class refiles the record in place, keeping its id. This is distinct from the review update: it changes the record itself, e.g. moving scope project→team promotes a record to the shared surface. For validFrom/validUntil a number sets the bound, null clears it, and an omitted field leaves it unchanged, so a proposal that changes only the window can be applied. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists.

methods.title: Update Memory Record Review
methods.description: Update a record's review signal (reviewState, confidence, reviewer, staleReason) in the canonical store. Marking a record stale or contradicted flags it so the recall-honesty contract will never inject it into a prompt again regardless of confidence. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists.

methods.title: Memory Review Queue
methods.description: Return memory records prioritised for review. Accepts optional limit (?limit=N) and scope filter (?scope=session|project|team). A scope query parameter that is present but not one of the three valid values returns 400.

methods.title: List Memory Copies
methods.description: The memory store's point-in-time copies, newest first: the daily copy, the copy taken before a schema migration, the copy every restore takes of the records it replaced, and the tripwire copy. Each with its name (what memory.snapshots.restore takes), why it was taken, when, its size on disk and how many records it holds (null when the copy could not be read). Only the records store is copied; the semantic index is rebuilt from the records. Empty for a store that lives in memory only.

methods.title: Restore Memory From a Copy
methods.description: Replace every memory record, link, consolidation proposal and store fact with those of one copy (its exact name from memory.snapshots.list, `latest` for the newest copy not taken by a restore, or the start of one name such as a date). `latest` names the same copy before and after a restore, so repeating the call writes the same records again. The owner's act only: its confirmation is owner-request, confirm: true from a credential that states a person asked (a sign-in, a paired device or an app on the daemon's machine), else CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; an agent is refused. A copy of the records being replaced is taken first and named in `undoSnapshot`, so restoring it undoes this restore. One SQLite write transaction: processes that share the store (terminal app, Agent, daemon) see the restored records on their next read, and a failure part way leaves the store as it was. The semantic index then re-embeds only records whose text differs from what it holds (`vectorIndex: updating`). Answers which copy, records before and after, and links after.

errorCodes.meaning: This store keeps no copies (an in-memory store), or a copy of the current records could not be taken first; nothing was changed.
No copy has that name (or there are no copies yet); nothing was changed.
More than one copy starts with that text; name one in full. Nothing was changed.
The copy cannot be read or was written by a newer version; nothing was changed.

methods.title: Rebuild Memory Vector Index
methods.description: Rebuild the sqlite-vec vector index.

methods.title: Memory Vector Stats
methods.description: Return the current sqlite-vec vector-store posture.

methods.title: Acknowledge An Occasion
methods.description: Record that the owner has one occurrence in hand, so nothing is pushed at them about it again. This is not a yes and not a no: the open item STAYS OPEN and stays enumerable, so occasions.pending still lists it, under acknowledged[] rather than in the nudge, and asking what is coming up still answers with it. Only the push stops. The record expires with its occurrence, so next year asks fresh. An occurrence already answered yes or no is left as it is: changed is false and reply says so. source names how it was recorded: conversation when the owner said so in a reply, explicit when a surface offered the action, gift-flow when the owner is already answering gift questions about it.

methods.title: Answer An Occasion Nudge
methods.description: Record yes, no, later or acknowledged for one occurrence. A no goes silent for the rest of this cycle and expires with the date, so next year asks fresh carrying no memory of the refusal. A later is NOT a decline, it comes back roughly halfway to the date. A yes on a gift-giving occasion opens the short interview and returns its first question. A yes or a no RESOLVES the open item and removes it. A later keeps the item open and moves it to its return date with its pushes available again. An answer of acknowledged leaves the item standing and quiet (the same as occasions.acknowledge); on an occurrence already answered yes or no it changes nothing and ok is false with the reason.

methods.title: Record A Confirmed Important Date
methods.description: Write the confirmed occasion as one line in the owner profile, under Important dates, carrying its provenance. self:true marks the owner's own date (written as for me), so a remember-only one is never pushed at them. This is the ONE confirmation: nothing re-confirms at nudge time, because for an annual date a silent write means the mistake surfaces up to eleven months later. Refused without a kind rather than defaulting one. Goes through the owner-profile write gate, so authority, surface and a verbatim quote of what the owner said are all required.

self.description: True when the date is the owner's own (their birthday). Written as `for me`; a remember-only date of the owner's is kept and listed but never pushed at them.

methods.title: Resolve A Date Conflict
methods.description: Apply the owner's answer to "which date is right?": keep names the date to keep, the other lines for that title are removed from the owner profile through the profile write gate (so authority is required with keep), answers and gift history stay, and the conflict is not raised again. Without keep nothing changes and dates lists what is recorded, to put to the owner. A conflict is never resolved automatically: only the owner knows which date was right. Two lines for one occasion are a conflict even when they name the same date (their kind, person or lead time can differ); then keep may be left out, and every line but the first is removed. When the file already holds one line (the owner fixed it by hand) the reminder is closed and resolved is true.

keep.description: The date to keep, as recorded (MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to get the recorded dates back without changing anything.

methods.title: List Gift History
methods.description: Return what the owner landed on for one occasion in previous years, newest first. Kept beyond the answers deliberately: the answers expire with their date so next year asks fresh, the history does not.

methods.title: Answer A Gift Interview Question
methods.description: Record one answer and return the next question, if there is one. The interview guides the owner to their own idea and never recommends a gift, that judgement is the owner's, which is also why the outcome recorded is what the owner landed on rather than what was suggested.

methods.title: Get Gift Interview
methods.description: Return one gift interview and the question that has not been answered yet. A thread the owner walked away from resumes here rather than restarting: the next step is the one the owner did not get to. Over a channel the steps are asked one at a time; in the agent they can be one exchange.

methods.title: Record What The Owner Landed On
methods.description: Close the interview with what the owner settled on and write it to the gift history. Recording the outcome rather than merely that the owner said yes is the point: "said yes in 2026" cannot stop year three steering where year one did.

methods.title: List Important Dates
methods.description: Return every occasion declared in the owner profile, with its next occurrence, how many days away it is, the lead it uses, whether it is inside its lead window, and what was answered for that occurrence. Also returns lines under the heading that could not be typed, each with the reason, and any occasion recorded on two lines (two different dates, or the same date written twice). This carries the dates: it is the owner asking their own system what it holds, which is the explicit ask that unlocks a closed-tier read. A nudge never does.

methods.title: Pull Outstanding Occasions
methods.description: Return everything unresolved, without delivering anything: the batched nudge, any date conflict still open, and any interview left mid-thread. This is how a surface that is not a push destination receives a nudge, it pulls at the start of a turn rather than being pushed at, and a stored date is the prior scheduling that permits raising something unprompted. A nudge a push has already landed on the agent is left out while the agent is a configured push destination, so the push and the pull cannot raise the same thing twice; an item no push has ever landed there is still returned, so a missing sender or a failed send loses nothing. An occurrence inside its window is listed even before any sweep has opened it, so a machine that was just started still answers. Composed in code, the same with or without a decision model. The nudge names the occasion and the person and NEVER the date: proximity is a word, not a count of days.

methods.title: Record A Confirmed Plan
methods.description: Write the confirmed plan as one line in the owner profile, under Plans, carrying its provenance and every entry of details (a confirmation number, flights and times, who is travelling), which occasions.plans.list returns in extras. Same one-confirmation rule and the same owner-profile write gate as an occasion.

details.description: Everything else the owner gave about the plan, one detail per entry: a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling, why. Stored on the line exactly; a detail the line cannot hold unchanged refuses the write.

methods.title: List Plans
methods.description: Return every plan declared in the owner profile, a dated range with attributes, plus whichever one has the owner away today. Plans are ambient: they never prompt. They exist so the system knows not to suggest things into that window, and so a nudge that would land while the owner is abroad moves to the day before they leave.

methods.title: Propose A Plan
methods.description: Work out what would be written for a plan heard in conversation, and return the one-line confirmation. Writes nothing. Away is opt-in rather than assumed: "the kitchen is being redone, 3rd to the 10th" is a real dated range that is not the owner leaving the house.

details.description: Everything else the owner gave about the plan, one detail per entry: a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling, why. Stored on the line exactly; a detail the line cannot hold unchanged refuses the write.

methods.title: Remove A Plan
methods.description: Remove one plan from the owner profile, chosen by planId (its normalised title) and planFrom when two plans share a name. One confirmation: confirmed:false returns the sentence to put to the owner and removes nothing. Goes through the owner-profile write gate, so authority is required.

planFrom.description: The start date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the plan meant, needed only when two plans share a name.

methods.title: Change A Plan
methods.description: Change one recorded plan in place, chosen by planId (its normalised title) and planFrom when two plans share a name: any of title, from, to, away, destination and details (details replaces the list); a field left out keeps its value. With confirmed:false nothing is written and proposal carries the exact line and the sentence to put to the owner; with confirmed:true the new line is written and the old one removed, through the owner-profile write gate (authority, surface and said required).

planFrom.description: The start date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the plan meant, needed only when two plans share a name.

details.description: Everything else the owner gave about the plan, one detail per entry: a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling, why. Stored on the line exactly; a detail the line cannot hold unchanged refuses the write.

methods.title: Propose An Important Date
methods.description: Work out what would be written for a date heard in conversation, and return the one-line confirmation to put to the owner. WRITES NOTHING. When no kind was given, needsKind is true and the confirmation asks for it in the same breath, the kind is the owner's choice and is never inferred, because no rule that reads a label tells a birthday from a death anniversary. Any date already recorded for the same name that disagrees comes back in conflictsWith.

self.description: True when the date is the owner's own (their birthday). Written as `for me`; a remember-only date of the owner's is kept and listed but never pushed at them.

methods.title: Remove An Important Date
methods.description: Remove one occasion and every record the machine kept against it, answers, gift history, open items, interviews and calendar mirrors. Takes exactly one confirmation: not unquestioned, and not an argument. People divorce and people die. A confirmed:false call returns the sentence to put to the owner, naming the line (removedLine), and removes nothing. The confirmed call names the line it removes in line (that removedLine, or the occasion's text from occasions.list), and only that line goes; when other lines still declare the same occasion (stillDeclaredBy above 0) its records are kept, since the next line is now the occasion. Repeating a confirmed call changes nothing: once the named line is gone it answers ok with nothing removed.

methods.title: Occasions State Disclosure
methods.description: What the machine-owned store is holding, counts of answers, gift records, open items, interviews and calendar mirrors, plus what the last housekeeping pass removed and why, and whether the file was found unreadable. Counts and reasons only: no answer, no gift and no date is returned, which is what makes this safe in a support bundle.

methods.title: Run The Approach Sweep Now
methods.description: Run one pass immediately: reap expired and orphaned state, find the occasions entering their lead window, batch them into a single message, mirror to the calendar if that is on, and deliver. Delivery goes to every destination in occasions.nudgeChannel, a comma-separated list, so Telegram and the agent both get it, and each is attempted independently, with deliveries[] naming per destination what landed and what did not. Housekeeping runs first and unconditionally, so a machine with nudging turned off still reaps. Returns hold:"quiet-hours" or hold:"disabled" when it deliberately said nothing, nothing is dropped, it waits. It runs the same with or without a decision model; with decision models off, provenance:"classic" says who each date is about was taken from the line's own for-me marker only. A push a destination accepted is recorded as sent even if settings or the profile changed during the send, so it is not pushed again next pass.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Change An Important Date
methods.description: Change one recorded occasion in place: any of date, kind, person, recurrence, leadDays (null returns to the default) and self; a field left out keeps its value. The occasion keeps its id, so its answers, gift history and calendar mirrors stay attached. A new title is accepted only when it names the same occasion (spelling or case); a different name is refused, add it as a new occasion and remove this one. With confirmed:false nothing is written and proposal carries the exact line and the sentence to put to the owner; with confirmed:true the new line is written and the old one removed, through the owner-profile write gate (authority, surface and said required). An occasion recorded with two dates is refused until occasions.conflict.resolve settles it.

self.description: True when the date is the owner's own (their birthday). Written as `for me`; a remember-only date of the owner's is kept and listed but never pushed at them.

methods.title: Complete Pairing Hand-off
methods.description: Apply the surface's per-offer decisions in ONE pass: an accepted notifications offer registers the browser push subscription (endpoint + keys, optional deviceId), an accepted passkey offer registers the WebAuthn credential, an accepted relay offer is acknowledged. Each offer returns an honest per-offer result (completed / declined / unavailable / failed); an omitted or false offer is reported as declined, never silently half-applied. Because it can register a step-up passkey it needs what stepup.credentials.register needs (admin, write:relay, never the Agent's credential), and a passkey is accepted only when pairing.handoff.create offered one to this very pairing (the caller is the device that paired with that hand-off's token), once, within 30 minutes; otherwise the passkey offer fails and nothing is registered. A pairing minted narrower than full authority cannot complete a hand-off, so pairing.handoff.create offers it nothing to complete.

methods.title: Create Pairing Hand-off
methods.description: The owner's pairing flow. Mint a per-device token AND assemble the set-up OFFER SET this daemon can satisfy (notifications, carrying the VAPID public key; relay; passkey step-up), so a freshly-paired surface can complete them in one pass. Returns the offer set, the `#pair=<token>` deep-link fragment (the exact URL-fragment shape the web app consumes, token in `pair=`, offers in `offers=`), a full deep link when a web origin is configured, and that origin's honest TLS/capability POSTURE: the one plain-http-on-LAN notice line (stated here, never a nag) plus per-capability availability labels so surfaces render "needs https: set up a secure address in Settings, General, Secure address (...)" instead of dead buttons. The token secret is returned exactly once. When a paired device asks, the new token records that device (mintedBy) and is revoked with it; a device whose own pairing is gone is refused with 403 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND. Each offer is independently declinable at completion. A pairing minted narrower than full authority cannot complete a hand-off (pairing.handoff.complete needs what stepup.credentials.register needs), so it is offered nothing to complete and gets its token alone. The device it pairs holds full authority and is recorded with origin owner-pairing when you ask from any of your credentials (a sign-in under any name, a paired device, the operator token, a typed command, the Agent's credential) without a narrow scope list; a narrowed caller's pairing keeps its list and is recorded as automation. Both are your devices. `fromSharedToken: true` is how a client signed in with the shared operator token (the owner's own browser) moves onto its own token: it pairs itself here, exempt from device.nodes.maxPaired as pairing.tokens.migrate is, and the token it gets is a full device; only a caller on the shared token may send it (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise). No code is made that a phone could not open: when the daemon's web address is reachable only from its own machine (a loopback address, or controlPlane.enabled off without web.publicBaseUrl naming it), the call is refused with 409 PAIRING_CODE_UNREACHABLE, saying why and the command to run in a terminal on the daemon's machine (goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan); pairing.posture.get gives the same decision with numbered steps before anything is minted. `serveToNetwork: true` is the owner's yes to "Phones on your network cannot reach GoodVibes yet. Serve it to your network?", which a pairing surface asks in place of that refusal: the daemon writes what goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan writes, waits for its own listener to report it is bound again (TRANSPORT_CONNECTED; no sleep, no poll), and then mints for the address phones can open, in the same call; refused 409 PAIRING_CODE_UNREACHABLE only when it still cannot be reached. `fromSharedToken: true`, and `forThisMachine: true` (a code for a browser on the daemon's own machine), are not refused for that.

methods.title: Issue the Outside Agent Credential
methods.description: The one credential this daemon gives `goodvibes-daemon mcp serve`, asked for with the operator token: a paired-device token named "Outside agent (goodvibes-daemon mcp serve)" holding full operator authority, as the operator token does, answered once with `token` and `id`. Nothing is asked and nothing is refused: it is issued at once, and it names any project. `project` (the folder the server was started in) is accepted and not needed. A second ask while it is kept is refused 409 OUTSIDE_AGENT_ISSUED (revoke it among the paired devices to have a new one issued).

errorCodes.meaning: The outside agent already has its credential from this daemon; revoke it among the paired devices to have a new one issued.

methods.title: Get Origin TLS/Capability Posture
methods.description: The honest TLS/capability posture of a web origin, pass your surface's current origin (or omit it to read the configured web origin). Plain http on a private-network origin (LAN IP, .local, localhost) is a supported posture reported with its ONE notice line; browser-gated capabilities (service worker/PWA install, push, microphone) are each labeled available or "needs https: set up a secure address in Settings, General, Secure address (...)" so surfaces render labels instead of dead buttons. Localhost keeps all three. https on a private address that is not a tailnet name is the daemon's own LAN certificate (controlPlane.lanHttps): its capabilities are available and its notice says each phone installs the certificate once from the link for phones (the page /lan-https on the https address, which offers it only when it matches the fingerprint in the link). With no origin supplied the answer is about the address a pairing code carries and adds `reach`: whether a phone can open it (otherDevices), decided by the daemon from its settings with no request on the network, and when not, the reason, the fix (a command to run in a terminal on the daemon's machine) and the numbered steps (state done|next|then, text, detail, command). Every pairing surface asks this before minting. With controlPlane.lanHttps on (the Secure address), the address a pairing code carries is the https one the listener serves: at the certificate's own name for Let's Encrypt, a certificate you made or a group's (secureAddress.get), with no install notice; at the same host for GoodVibes' own certificate, with its install notice. Plain http keeps working as before.

methods.title: Serve The Web UI To The Network
methods.description: What goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan does, from any surface, after the owner said yes to "Phones on your network cannot reach GoodVibes yet. Serve it to your network?" (asked opening on No): the daemon writes controlPlane.hostMode and web.hostMode network and controlPlane.enabled true, and answers only once its own listener reports it is bound again (TRANSPORT_CONNECTED; no sleep, no poll). The answer is the pairing posture of the address a code would now carry (`posture`, with `reach`), so the surface can mint at once with pairing.handoff.create. The plain listener stays as it was otherwise; undo with goodvibes-daemon webui enable --loopback. Admin, like config.set.

methods.title: Mint Paired Device Token
methods.description: Mint a new named per-device operator token and return its plaintext secret EXACTLY ONCE (for a QR / pairing hand-off). Only a hash is persisted; the secret is never listed or returned again. The name is user-visible and editable. When a paired device asks, the new token records that device (mintedBy) and is revoked with it; a device whose own pairing is gone is refused with 403 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND. client "agent" mints the GoodVibes Agent's credential for the calls it makes on the owner's behalf: the daemon reports it as credential "agent" and judges every call made with it; it is listed with client "agent" and does not count toward device.nodes.maxPaired. Send an attemptId and send the same one again when a reply is lost: while the token that attempt produced is unused, the repeat returns that token (same id) under a new secret. scopes limits the device to that list of operator scopes (for example read:sessions and write:sessions for a phone that only chats: it reads the chats it made under them); left out (or `["*"]`), the device holds full operator authority, and then it is the user's device: it does what every credential of the user does. A caller grants only scopes it holds: a narrowed caller's token inherits its list when scopes is left out, and naming a scope the caller does not hold is 403 MISSING_SCOPE. A device is paired by hand-off with pairing.handoff.create.

replay.name: attemptId
replay.behavior: Sending the same attemptId again while the token that attempt produced is still unused returns that token (same id) under a new secret, and the secret of the lost reply stops working; once the token has been used, the same attemptId mints a new token.

methods.title: Revoke Paired Device Token
methods.description: Revoke (permanently delete) one paired device token. Revocation is immediate: the token fails the very next request with a 401, and every token this device minted is revoked with it (listed in alsoRevoked); every other paired device keeps working. An unknown id is a 404 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop. A token the caller minted, or the caller's own token, is revoked at once; any other token (a device paired, another principal's) is revoked at once by every credential of the user (a sign-in under any name, a device paired with full scopes, the operator token); a device holding a narrow scope list is refused 403 OWNER_ONLY.

methods.title: List Paired Device Tokens
methods.description: List the per-pairing operator tokens (paired devices/browsers, and each one made that no device has used yet and that has not expired, marked waitingForFirstUse so it can be revoked before its first use) as redacted views: id, user-visible name, created timestamp, last-seen timestamp, mintedBy (the paired device that minted it, when one did), scopes (the operator scopes it holds, when it was paired with a narrower list; absent means full operator authority) and origin: `owner-pairing` for a device paired from the pairing screen or by pairing.handoff.create with full authority, completed with the code the screen showed (or by pairing.tokens.migrate), or `automation` for every other token (pairing.tokens.create, a migration, a narrowed list, the Agent's credential, and every token minted before origin was recorded). Every paired device is you: what a device may do is limited only by its stored scope list (a device with no list does everything you do, whatever its origin), never by who paired it. Origin is recorded at the mint and never changes; to give a limited device full authority, pair it again from the pairing screen and revoke the old token. The token secret is never stored in listable form and is never returned.

methods.title: Migrate Off The Shared Token
methods.description: A client currently authenticated with the legacy single shared token mints its OWN named per-device token and receives the plaintext secret once. A token minted here is labelled automation (origin automation) and is a device of yours like any other; a browser or app can also move off the shared token with pairing.handoff.create and `fromSharedToken: true`, which labels it owner-pairing. Send an attemptId and send the same one again when a reply is lost: while the token that attempt produced is unused, the repeat returns that token (same id) under a new secret instead of minting a second one. This does NOT revoke the shared token; that is a separate explicit step (pairing.tokens.revokeShared).

replay.name: attemptId
replay.behavior: Sending the same attemptId again while the token that attempt produced is still unused returns that token (same id) under a new secret, and the secret of the lost reply stops working; once the token has been used, the same attemptId mints a new token.

methods.title: Rename Paired Device Token
methods.description: Change the user-visible name of a paired device token. An unknown id is a 404 PAIRING_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND.

methods.title: Revoke The Legacy Shared Token
methods.description: Revoke the shared operator token by replacing it: every copy handed to another device stops working immediately, and the daemon writes the new value to its operator-tokens.json, where the apps on its own machine read it, so they stay signed in. Other devices use per-device pairing tokens (or user sessions). Your own act (access.withdraw): any of your credentials with full authority makes it (the operator token, a paired device, your sign-in, a typed command), at once; a credential with a narrow scope list is refused 403 OWNER_ONLY by that list, and a model never makes it. Refused with SHARED_TOKEN_NOT_REPLACEABLE (409) when the daemon serves a token set by GOODVIBES_DAEMON_TOKEN. Not safe to repeat: each call replaces the shared token again.

methods.title: List Panels
methods.description: Return integration panel descriptors.

methods.title: Open Panel
methods.description: Open a listed panel in the terminal session this process runs. Answers opened: true only when the view appeared; an id GET /api/panels does not list is refused with 404, and a listed panel this process has no terminal screen to show is refused with 409.

methods.title: Payment Budget Status
methods.description: Today's spending pools: the daily item budget, the separate overage budget that covers only unavoidable charges (tax, mandatory fees, and the delivery option actually used), and the tolerance allowance. Each reports its limit, what today has spent, what purchases in flight are holding, and what is left. Includes the calendar day and the timezone it was computed in, the day resets at midnight in daemon.timezone, UTC when unset, and whether this node is the one currently allowed to spend. Each spend keeps the day it was made on, in the zone then in force, and counts until that day is over, so changing the timezone cannot hand back a spent budget. The pools are in `currency` and count only what was spent in it: changing payments.currency starts a new pool for the rest of the day, and what was spent earlier that day in the old currency is listed in earlierSpend, in its own currency, never converted.

message.description: Which store stopped, why, that nothing recorded was lost, and the step: restart the daemon.

methods.title: Add a Payment Card
methods.description: Store a card. The number, expiry, CVV and cardholder name go to the daemon secret store, encrypted at rest, under keys derived from the config path; only the label, brand, last four digits, kind and declared issuer cap are kept as config. The response carries the metadata record and never echoes what was submitted, because an echo would be a read path and no read path exists. Sending the same card again (the same label, number and expiry, for example after an answer that was lost) returns the card already stored and stores nothing new; no Idempotency-Key is taken, because a kept request would be a hash of the card on disk. A virtual card with a hard issuer cap is the recommended configuration: it bounds what any leak could cost to one killable number, which a real card number does not.

methods.title: Remove a Payment Card
methods.description: Delete a card: its config metadata and every secret derived from its config path, reporting how many secret entries were cleared so a partial deletion is visible rather than silent. An id the daemon holds no card for, and no material under, answers 404 NOT_FOUND with nothing removed (so a delete sent again after it went through says the card is no longer there); an id with no card left but material a crashed add stranded answers deleted: false with the entries it cleared. payments.defaultCardId is not cleared by a delete; payments.cards.list shows a stale id as empty, and every purchase must name its card anyway.

methods.title: List Payment Cards
methods.description: Configured cards, as METADATA ONLY: id, label, brand, last four digits, whether it is a virtual or a real card, expiry month and year, and the issuer spend cap the owner declared for a virtual card (declared, unverifiable by us, and never treated as an enforcement layer of ours). materialComplete reports whether every required secret field is present without revealing any of them. The card number, expiry, CVV and cardholder name live in the daemon secret store and there is no method that returns them.

methods.title: Approve One Purchase
methods.description: The owner approves one purchase in advance, out of band from the conversation that will run it: the merchant's registrable domain, the item, and the most it may cost. Optional unless payments.confirmEveryPurchase is on. The amount is read in the budget currency, payments.currency ("25" and "25.00" are the same amount), and an amount no purchase could match is refused before anything is recorded. Mints a persisted, single-use approval bound to those fields and that currency (returned as currency), expiring in five minutes; a begin after payments.currency changed is a different purchase and does not spend it; a matching payments.checkout.begin spends it, and it answers that purchase's approval window for a total up to its amount. Its confirmation is owner-request: confirm: true from a credential that states a person asked (a sign-in, a paired device or an app on the daemon's machine), else 403 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED (400 when confirm is missing); the Money place (payments.approve) and the web UI send both. The response never carries card material; this verb never touches a card at all.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Buy What Is In This Checkout
methods.description: Admit one checkout against an open browser page and return a durable accepted acknowledgement before its approval/veto wait. Supply a stable requestId saved before sending; after a lost response, query payments.purchase.status with that ID. Reusing an admitted ID never starts another execution, even with changed input. Inside the owner's limits no prior approval is needed; with payments.confirmEveryPurchase on, a begin must state requestedMax and spend a matching payments.checkout.approve. cardId may be omitted to pay with payments.defaultCardId, and merchantDiscovered is read as sent. A purchase the owner asked for now carries the explicit-user-request context; one a schedule or trigger starts names standingId (payments.standing.list) instead and is bound to that entry's item, shops and maximums. The daemon parses amounts, checks cart/merchant/taint/recurrence and budget, runs the shipping ladder and owner window, fills stored addresses/card and submits once. Accepted does not mean purchased. Status retains processing, refusal, cancellation, verification and uncertain-submission outcomes. Disconnecting the caller does not cancel the operation; stopping or shutdown drains its actual work. An uncertain merchant submission is never retried automatically.

cardId.description: A card id from payments.cards.list. Omitted, the purchase is paid with payments.defaultCardId.

askedInSession.description: The session whose turn began this purchase: the agent's operator call sets it from its own turn, so the purchase window names the chat it came from. A label only; it decides nothing about the purchase.

standingId.description: For a purchase a schedule or trigger starts, with nobody asking in the moment: the id of the owner's standing authorisation from payments.standing.list. The item must be that entry's item and the merchant one of its shops; the purchase may come to at most the smaller of its per-purchase maximum and what is left of its period. Omit it for a purchase the owner asked for now.

requestedMax.description: Owner-requested maximum for the entire purchase, including tax, mandatory fees and delivery. Supply one non-negative decimal amount in the configured budget currency, such as 20.00, without grouping, currency symbols or prose. Precision must fit that currency. Exceeding it requires a new explicit approval; silence never raises it. Required while payments.confirmEveryPurchase is on: it is the amount the owner approved.

replay.name: requestId
replay.behavior: Reusing an admitted `requestId` never starts another purchase, even with changed input; after a lost response read the outcome with payments.purchase.status and that requestId.

methods.title: Approve This Purchase
methods.description: Approve an above-budget purchase or explicitly acknowledge an in-budget purchase using the exact live purchase and window references. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. The same inbox also consumes authenticated channel replies. A stale, answered or expired window refuses; this never submits directly or overrides budget, merchant, page or address checks.

methods.title: Stop This Purchase
methods.description: Stop an admitted checkout using its exact purchaseId and operationId, or object to a live window using purchaseId and windowId. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. Stopping is a request, not proof that an order was undone; inspect final status and merchant history if submission may have begun. No automatic retry.

methods.title: Deny This Purchase
methods.description: Refuse the pending purchase using the exact live purchase and window references. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. The same inbox also consumes authenticated channel replies. A stale, answered or expired window refuses; this never submits directly or overrides budget, merchant, page or address checks.

methods.title: Record the Merchant Order Finding
methods.description: After inspecting the merchant’s order history, explicitly record whether this exact uncertain or unverified checkout placed an order. Requires current paired admin authority, write:payments, confirm: true and inspectedMerchantHistory: true. The saved finding cannot be changed by a retry. Settles only original purchase/budget bookkeeping after its actual executor has drained; never submits or resumes an order. Missing local receipts never imply no charge. A no-order finding releases an original unspent hold but never credits already committed spend.

methods.title: Type the Card Security Code
methods.description: Under payments.cvvHandling prompt, hand the card security code the owner typed to the one approved purchase waiting for it, by its exact purchaseId and windowId from payments.purchase.status. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. The code is used for that purchase's card entry and kept nowhere. A closed or replaced request refuses; this never submits directly or overrides any budget, merchant, page or address check.

code.description: The three or four digits of the card security code, typed by the owner for this one purchase. Never stored.

methods.title: Purchase Operations and Windows
methods.description: Read durable checkout operation status and actual live approval/veto windows, and any approved purchase waiting for its card security code (securityCodes, under payments.cvvHandling prompt). Optionally select one purchase, including after reconnect or restart. An accepted operation is not a completed purchase; uncertain submissions must be checked with the merchant and are never automatically retried. Reading does not extend a deadline or resume execution. Complete purchase records are available through payments.purchases.list.

message.description: Which store stopped, why, that nothing recorded was lost, and the step: restart the daemon.

methods.title: List Purchases
methods.description: The purchase audit ledger: what was bought, from which merchant registrable domain, how much (item, tax, fees and delivery separately), which budget pool each part drew on, which delivery tier was requested and which was actually used, whether the shipping ladder stepped it down, which window ran and how it ended, which command-authority channel answered, and the outcome. Reconcilable against a card statement. Never contains a card number, expiry or CVV. When the shop mails that a purchase was refunded, the time is recorded as `refundedAt` on that purchase and the owner is told; check the card statement for the credit. A refund credits no pool: a refund on day five refilling day five would be permission to buy again that nobody granted.

methods.title: Authorise a Purchase in Advance
methods.description: The owner authorises, in advance, a purchase a schedule or trigger may start without asking them: the item in the owner's words, the shops, the most one purchase may come to, the most all of them may come to every periodDays days, and an optional last day. Amounts are read in the budget currency. Every other limit still applies to each purchase: the budgets, the per-purchase ceiling and the veto or approval window. Its confirmation is owner-request: confirm: true from a credential that states a person asked, else CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; the Money place (payments.repeat) sends both. The owner's own act: an agent cannot add one.

item.description: The owner's words for what may be bought; a scheduled purchase must name exactly this item.

merchants.description: The shop domains it may be bought from.

maxPerPurchase.description: The most one purchase may come to, in the budget currency, such as 60.00.

maxPerPeriod.description: The most all purchases under it may come to within periodDays, in the budget currency.

expires.description: Optional last day, such as 2027-06-30; absent, it lasts until removed.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Withdraw a Standing Authorisation
methods.description: Remove one standing purchase authorisation by its id. No new purchase can start under it, and one under it that a daemon restart interrupted is not resumed; a purchase already running keeps its window, where the owner can still stop it. Its confirmation is owner-request: confirm: true from a credential that states a person asked, else CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; the Money place (payments.stop-repeat) sends both. The owner's own act.

methods.title: Standing Purchase Authorisations
methods.description: The purchases the owner authorised in advance for runs nobody starts in the moment (a schedule or a trigger): for each, its id, the item in the owner's words, the shops it may be bought from, the most one purchase may come to, the most all of them may come to over its period, what is spent or held in the current period and what is left, and when it expires. A scheduled purchase names one of these ids as standingId on payments.checkout.begin.

methods.title: Post Decided Calls
methods.description: A terminal program (the terminal app, the Agent) tells the daemon which calls its permission gate decided: the tool, its kind, its target, how risky, and whether it was allowed. The daemon keeps them beside its own decided calls (the newest 100 in all), so reviewing a candidate policy ("See what the candidate policy changes") decides every program's calls again. A call is kept once by its id. Up to 100 calls per post.

methods.title: Delete a Durable Permission Rule
methods.description: Delete one durable user-origin permission rule by id. The matching asks prompt again afterwards, deleting a grant is how a remembered decision is revoked. deleted:false when no rule with that id exists (an honest miss, not an error).

methods.title: List Durable Permission Rules
methods.description: List the durable user-origin permission rules written by remembered approval decisions (exact command / command class / path scope / whole tool), newest first, the persistent grants and denials the permission manager consults before ever prompting. Project-scoped: with `project` (a folder), only the rules in force there, that project's own and those of every project; without it, every rule with the project it belongs to.

methods.title: Create Principal
methods.description: Create a named principal from a name, kind, and optional channel identities. Fails with a conflict when any identity is already mapped to a different principal.

methods.title: Delete Principal
methods.description: Permanently delete a principal. Returns { deleted: false } when no principal with that id existed, an honest boolean, never a 200 that pretends a phantom principal was removed.

methods.title: Get Principal
methods.description: Return one principal by id. Returns 404 when no principal with that id exists.

methods.title: List Principals
methods.description: Return every named principal in the registry with its channel identities.

methods.title: Resolve Sender Identity
methods.description: Resolve a channel-specific sender identity ({channel, value}) to the named principal it belongs to. An unmapped identity resolves to the shared unknown principal with known:false, the registry never guesses.

methods.title: Update Principal
methods.description: Update a principal's name, kind, identities, and/or metadata. Absent fields are left unchanged; supplying identities replaces the set. Fails with a conflict when an identity is already mapped to a different principal.

methods.title: Append Profile Note
methods.description: Add one prose bullet to a section, carrying its provenance suffix. Same three-layer gate as profile.set. A section that does not exist is created at the end of the document; a section the owner renamed is matched case-insensitively rather than duplicated.

methods.title: Forget Profile Line
methods.description: Delete a mechanical field and every retained history comment for it, or one prose line addressed by its section plus its exact text. Never by line position: the owner edits this file by hand, so an index taken from an earlier read may name a different line by the time the delete arrives. Text that no longer matches removes nothing and says so, rather than deleting the nearest thing. No tombstone, no deleted flag, no retention window, delete means delete. Forgetting something that was not there reports that honestly instead of returning success. Authority-gated exactly like a write: an injection that cannot add a fact must not be able to remove one.

methods.title: Get Profile Field
methods.description: Return one mechanical field by id (e.g. commerce.shippingAddress). Answers present:false for a field the owner has not recorded rather than inventing a value, and returns an invalid value verbatim with its reason instead of hiding it. A closed-tier field carries the one-line disclosure the reply should show.

methods.title: Get Person From Profile
methods.description: Return the People lines matching one name. Takes a NAME by design and has no enumerate-all counterpart: a People line may reach outbound content only when the owner named that person in this turn's instruction, and the only lookup that exists taking a name is what makes that structural rather than a matter of model judgement.

methods.title: Get Profile Provenance
methods.description: Answer "where did you get that?" for one field: the surface, the date and the owner's verbatim words, plus every superseded predecessor still retained as a history comment. A field the owner typed by hand reports handEdited:true and no provenance, rather than being dressed up as a recorded source.

methods.title: Read Owner Profile
methods.description: Return the whole owner profile, by section, with each section's tier and every mechanical field's validity. This is the answer to "what do you know about me?" and is the ONE read that returns closed-tier content in bulk. It carries its own scope, read:profile-document, so a token issued to a composition path can hold read:profile for the named lookups (get/person/provenance/status) without also being able to ask for everything. The two are unrelated names rather than a hierarchy: scope matching is exact, `*`, or a `prefix:*` wildcard, so a caller wanting both lists both.

methods.title: Set Profile Field
methods.description: Record or correct one mechanical field, moving any previous value into a retained history comment. Refused unless the caller carries owner-direct authority AND the proposed value does not overlap untrusted content read this turn AND a verbatim quote of what the owner said is supplied. A caller declaring the call was not an explicit user request is refused before any of that.

methods.title: Owner Profile Status
methods.description: Diagnostics for the profile: whether it loaded, the file path, the section names, line/field/prose counts, and every mechanical value that did not validate WITH ITS REASON. It never returns a value, that is what makes it safe in a support bundle, and it is asserted by test. An unreadable file reports unavailable with the reason rather than an empty profile.

methods.title: Undo Profile Correction
methods.description: Promote a field's most recent superseded value back to the active line, so a wrong correction is recoverable. Authority-gated like every other mutation.

methods.title: Post A Learned Context Limit
methods.description: A terminal program (the terminal app, the Agent) tells the daemon what a provider showed its own turn about a model's context window: a request of so many tokens was refused as too long, or an input of so many tokens went through. The daemon keeps it in its one context-window file (a learned limit only lowers, an accepted floor only rises, a size the person set stays), says the list changed (LIST_CHANGED context-windows), and every program reads the file again before its next turn. The capability context.window reads it; context.clear-window forgets it.

methods.title: Current Model
methods.description: The model this daemon would use for a turn right now, with whether its provider is actually configured and by which authentication route. `model` is null when nothing is selected, which is a real state, not an error, and a caller rendering a picker needs to tell it from a selection whose provider has lost its credentials. `effort` is the persisted reasoning level, null when none has been set explicitly.

methods.title: Switch the Current Model
methods.description: Switch the daemon's current model live, by the registry key `models.list` returns. The switch applies to the next turn on every surface this daemon serves and is persisted, so it survives a restart; `persisted` says whether the write to settings succeeded. An unknown key is refused with MODEL_NOT_FOUND and a provider with no usable credentials with PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED, naming the environment variables it looked for, a caller must not have to guess which of the two happened. An optional `effort` persists a reasoning level with the selection: it is validated against the known severity ladder here, and each turn maps it onto the active model's real options, snapping down and never promoting. It changes the model for every surface, so it needs an admin.

methods.title: Model Catalog
methods.description: Every provider this daemon knows about with the models it offers, whether it is configured, and how it was configured. A GET also triggers the TTL-respecting live-discovery re-check that the terminal's model picker triggers on open: a provider's list stored more than 24 hours ago is read from the provider again, and the shared model catalog checked when its last check is that old; a list that changes is announced as a providers change, so every client reads it again. Each provider carries `modelList`: where its list came from (`live` from the provider, `cache` its last stored list, `catalog` the shared model catalog), `listedAt` when it was read, and `error` when the last reading from the provider failed. `currentModel` is the daemon's current selection, or null when nothing is selected. `secretsResolutionSkipped` is true when secret-backed credentials were not resolved for this read, so a caller can tell "not configured" from "not checked". Each model that reasons carries `reasoningOptions`: the levels it actually offers and which source resolved them; a model with no entry does not reason at all. Each model carries `textWork`, what the model catalog says about holding a conversation: `text`, `other` (an image, speech or embedding model) or `unknown`. Each model carries `priceTier`, what it costs to use: `free`, `paid` (charged per token), `subscription` (served through a plan the person signed in with), `local` (a server on this computer or your own network serves it: nothing is charged per token) or `unknown`; a picker shows it beside the model, and a model the person uses that the catalog stops listing as free is announced as a PROVIDER_WARNING when the catalog is next checked. `pinned` are the registry keys of the models the person pinned and `recent` the ten used most recently, newest first: a picker lists pinned, then recent, then the rest, as the terminal's does. A connected provider's models may carry `recommended`, why the model is on that provider's short list of at most five, in catalog facts only ("newest claude-sonnet", "largest context: 1M tokens", "lowest price: $0.15 in, $0.60 out per 1M tokens"); a picker shows them after pinned and recent, and a provider the catalog gives no such facts for has none.

methods.title: Read the Model Lists Again
methods.description: Read the model lists from the providers now, past each stored list: every provider, or the one named by `providerId`; the shared model catalog is checked with them. Answers each provider that has a listing of its own: how many models it lists now, `source` (`live` when it answered; `cache` or `catalog` when it did not), the models `added` and `removed`, `listedAt`, `error` when its list could not be read, and `notAsked` when it has no key or sign-in to list with yet. A list that changed is announced as a providers change, so every client reads it again. An unknown `providerId` is refused with PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND. It sends requests to the providers with the owner's credentials, so it needs an admin.

methods.title: Store A Provider API Key
methods.description: Sign an API-key provider in from any client (the web UI's provider row): `key` is stored in the secret store under the provider's own key name (the first of its key names the credential scope registry files, such as OPENAI_API_KEY), at the scope the ownership rules resolve (a key the daemon needs lands in the daemon tier), and the provider's credentials are read again, so its row reads signed in and PROVIDERS_CHANGED is announced. Answers `provider`, `keyName`, `scope` and `signedIn`; the key is never answered or logged. A provider that takes no key (one signed in with providers.subscription.signIn.begin) or whose key name is not filed is refused 400; an unknown provider 404; a goodvibes:// reference instead of a key 400. Admin.

methods.title: Provider Snapshot
methods.description: Return runtime metadata for a single provider.

methods.title: Providers List
methods.description: Return runtime provider metadata, policy hooks, and priced model summaries.

methods.title: Begin A Subscription Sign-in
methods.description: Begin signing in to a provider through its own sign-in page, from any client (the web UI's "Sign in again"), on the same code path as the Sign in control of Models and providers (the capability provider.sign-in runs this method). Answers `authorizationUrl` (open it) and `finishes`: `on-its-own` when the provider returns to an address on the daemon's machine and a browser there completes it (the daemon then stores the sign-in and announces it with PROVIDERS_CHANGED), `paste` when the page shows a code or an address to send to providers.subscription.signIn.finish (a browser on another device always finishes this way). A new begin replaces one still waiting. Tokens are kept in the subscription store and never answered or logged. A provider with no subscription sign-in is refused 404; an API-key provider is signed in by storing its key with credentials.set. Admin, like the terminal command.

methods.title: Finish A Subscription Sign-in
methods.description: Finish a sign-in providers.subscription.signIn.begin started, with what the provider's page showed: the code, or the whole address it ended on (its state must match the begin). Stores the sign-in and announces it with PROVIDERS_CHANGED; answers the provider, `signedIn: true`, `tokenType` and `expiresAt`, never a token. A refused code is 400 with the provider's reason. Admin.

methods.title: Provider Usage
methods.description: Return usage and pricing posture for a single provider.

methods.title: Register Web Push Subscription
methods.description: Store a browser Push subscription (endpoint capability URL + p256dh/auth keys) for the authenticated operator so the daemon can deliver notifications to that device. When a stable deviceId is supplied the record reconciles on that device identity, a browser whose push endpoint rotated re-registers the same deviceId with a new endpoint and heals the one record in place rather than piling up a stale duplicate; without a deviceId it reconciles on the raw endpoint (legacy). The stored endpoint and keys are never returned over the wire; the response is the redacted subscription view.

methods.title: Delete Web Push Subscription
methods.description: Permanently remove one of the authenticated operator's push subscriptions: the stored record (endpoint + keys) is dropped and cannot be listed afterward, and the removal is a terminal entry on the authority record, so no machine of the group pushes to that device again. The removal is in force on this machine at once; when the authority record cannot be written it waits in this machine's push file and reaches the other machines with the next write that succeeds. While the authority record exists but cannot be read, the delete is refused with its error and nothing changes. An unknown id, or one owned by another principal, is a 404 SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop.

errorCodes.meaning: No push subscription of this operator has that id; list them with push.subscriptions.list and use an id it shows.

methods.title: List Web Push Subscriptions
methods.description: List the authenticated operator's registered push devices as redacted subscription views (id, deviceId when the record has one, endpoint origin, timestamps, last delivery outcome; two records on the same push service share an origin, so tell them apart by id or deviceId), plus lastRemoval: the most recent device the daemon removed and why (reason gone: the push service answered 404/410; failure-threshold: the push service rejected the endpoint push.subscriptions.failureThreshold times in a row; unusable or malformed: the stored record could never receive a push). Network errors, timeouts, rate limits and push-service outages never remove a device. The capability URL and key material are never included.

methods.title: Reconcile Web Push Subscription
methods.description: Reconcile-on-open: the client presents its device identity (deviceId) and its CURRENT endpoint + p256dh/auth keys, and the daemon heals the record for that device in place, updating a stale endpoint the daemon had been holding, then reports what drifted (created / endpoint-updated / keys-updated / unchanged) so the client learns whether the daemon was out of date. A live reconcile also clears the bounded-retry failure counter. The stored endpoint and keys are never returned; the response is the redacted subscription view plus the drift discriminant.

methods.title: Send Test Web Push
methods.description: Send a live test notification to one of the authenticated operator's subscriptions and return an honest delivery receipt (delivered / pruned / failed). A subscription whose endpoint reports 404/410 gone, or that the push service has now rejected push.subscriptions.failureThreshold times in a row, is pruned as part of the attempt and the receipt says so; a network error, timeout, 408, 413, 429 or 5xx is reported as failed and never counts against the device. An unknown id, or one owned by another principal, is a 404 SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

errorCodes.meaning: No push subscription of this operator has that id; list them with push.subscriptions.list and use an id it shows.

methods.title: Get Web Push Public Key
methods.description: Return the daemon's public VAPID key (base64url application-server key) that a browser client passes to pushManager.subscribe(). The matching private key never leaves the daemon and is never returned by any verb.

methods.title: Assess Fan-out Against Quota Window
methods.description: Assess whether spawning N agents against a provider likely exhausts its quota window right now, grounded in observed rate-limit signals (429 retry-after, and limit/remaining when headers carry them). verdict is likely-exhausts (with the evidence it rests on, an active cooldown or an observed remaining below the fan-out), unlikely (with the evidence), or unknown when no signal has been observed, never a fabricated certainty.

methods.title: Get Observed Quota Snapshot
methods.description: Return the most recent observed quota window for a provider, remaining, limit, reset, and any active cooldown, parsed from rate-limit headers carried on ordinary (successful) responses, so a consumer can render remaining quota BEFORE hitting a limit. hasSignal is false (with the observed-* fields absent) when no rate-limit signal has been seen for the provider in the lookback window: an honest "no observation", never a fabricated full quota.

methods.title: Mint Step-up Challenge
methods.description: Issue a short-lived, single-use WebAuthn challenge for one relay call. Pass the method and path of the call it is for: a challenge minted without them authorises nothing. The challenge is bound to the principal that minted it, and to the sessionId and rendezvousId when given; a relay call by another principal, or with a different method, path, session or rendezvous, is refused as challenge-unbound. A surface passes it to navigator.credentials.get and returns the assertion on the call it was minted for. Whether a relay call needs an assertion is decided by its catalog method's scopes (any scope other than read:*), not by its HTTP verb. The freshness window (ttlMs) is clamped to 5s–300s (default 120s).

errorCodes.meaning: Too many step-up challenges are open; answer one or let it expire, then ask again.

methods.title: List Step-up Credentials
methods.description: List the registered step-up passkeys: credentialId, label, creation time and signature counter. Never returns key material. Admin/local-only.

methods.title: Register Step-up Credential
methods.description: Store a WebAuthn (passkey) credential for relay step-up, its credentialId, COSE public key, and starting signature counter, and set the deployment policy (relying-party id, allowed origins, user-verification requirement). Admin/local-only: registering a step-up credential is itself a sensitive act. Self-hosted deployments register the credential directly ('none' attestation).

methods.title: Remove Step-up Credential
methods.description: Remove a registered step-up passkey so it can no longer confirm anything (a lost device). Answers 404 when no credential has that id. Admin/local-only. Mutating, so a relay call needs a step-up assertion. Removing the last passkey leaves no credential to confirm relay actions until a new one is registered.

methods.title: List Remote Backends
methods.description: Return the registered execution backends (docker, ssh, cloud terminal, local process) remote.peers.invoke runs commands on, and any stored registration that no longer reads, with the reason.

methods.title: Register Remote Backend
methods.description: Register or replace an execution backend under peerId so remote.peers.invoke runs commands on it. Credentials are goodvibes://secrets/ references only; an azure cloud-terminal credential is a JSON object {"clientId", "tenantId", "certificate"} (service principal application id, tenant id, and a PEM holding its certificate and private key), and a stored one of another shape is refused. A value docker or a cloud CLI would read as an option (starting with "-") and an id a paired peer holds are refused.

errorCodes.meaning: A paired peer already has that id; register the backend under another id.

methods.title: Remove Remote Backend
methods.description: Remove a registered execution backend; 404 when no backend has that id.

methods.title: Node Host Contract
methods.description: Return the distributed node/device host API contract.

methods.title: Approve Remote Pair Request
methods.description: Approve a pending remote pair request.

errorCodes.meaning: The request was rejected or expired, so it cannot be approved; ask the device to request pairing again.
The request names an existing peer and verifying it would replace that peer; approve again with confirmReplace: true only if it is the same device re-pairing.

methods.title: List Remote Pair Requests
methods.description: Return pending remote pair requests.

methods.title: Reject Remote Pair Request
methods.description: Reject a pending remote pair request.

methods.title: Disconnect Remote Peer
methods.description: Disconnect a remote peer.

methods.title: Get Remote Peer
methods.description: Return one remote peer by id; 404 when no peer has that id.

methods.title: Invoke Remote Peer
methods.description: Run a command on a remote peer. A paired peer gets it as queued work (answer: work, completed). A registered backend (remote.backends.register: docker, ssh, cloud terminal or local process) runs it now and answers with backend: exit code and output; on a backend, payload takes only args, stdin, env, timeoutMs and cwd, and the queue fields (priority, waitMs, sessionId, routeId, automation ids, approvalId) do not apply.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

errorCodes.meaning: The peer is revoked and cannot receive work; rotate its token or pair it again first.
The peer has not verified its pairing, so it holds no token to pull work with; ask the device to verify, then send the work again.

methods.title: List Remote Peers
methods.description: Return known remote peers: kind (node or device) keeps only that kind, and limit keeps the most recently seen that many; with no limit every peer is returned.

methods.title: Revoke Remote Peer Token
methods.description: Revoke the active token for a remote peer.

methods.title: Rotate Remote Peer Token
methods.description: Rotate the active token for a remote peer.

methods.title: Remote Runtime Snapshot
