methods.description: Return distributed node/device runtime state.

methods.title: Cancel Remote Work
methods.description: Cancel a remote work item. A caller below an admin cancels only work queued for a session or schedule of its own.

methods.title: List Remote Work
methods.description: Return queued and leased remote work items.

methods.title: Read The Secure Address
methods.description: What the Secure address screen shows: the four ways to give the daemon an https address for phones (Let's Encrypt for a domain you own, a certificate you made, Tailscale, GoodVibes' own certificate), each with what it does, what it needs from the person, what the phone gains and what is sent where; which one is in force and what the https listener serves now (address, names, end date, or why it does not serve); Let's Encrypt's last attempt, the address records written and this machine's own lookup of the name (a router that refuses local answers is named, with what to change); the own files' check; the local authority's fingerprint and the page a phone installs it from; the Tailscale address while one is served; and the group: on a lead, the machines that follow it and the line that every machine serves with the same certificate; on a node, the line that its secure address comes from the lead and what it received. On a lead the ways say what differs there (GoodVibes' own certificate covers the group's machines; a certificate you made and GoodVibes' own are sent, sealed, with their key to the group's machines). `letsEncrypt.tokenUnreadable` says, with the cause, that the secret store on this computer could not be read when no token was read (the token is then not asked for again). `notice` is a notice no owner channel carried (a node's own certificate authority set aside while it follows its lead), shown at the top of the screen; returning it here marks it given. No key or token is ever returned. Needs read:remote, an owner-private read scope: a user without the admin role is not granted it.

methods.title: Issue A New Secure Address Certificate
methods.description: The Secure address screen's "Issue a new certificate now", on the machine that set the secure address up (a group's lead, or a machine of its own): a new certificate with a new key at once, served by the https listener and sent, sealed, to the machines that follow it. With Let's Encrypt a new order is placed (an order already running finishes first); Let's Encrypt allows only five certificates for the same names a week, so a repeat spends one more of them. With GoodVibes' own certificate a new server certificate is made under the same authority, so phones that installed it need nothing. No input. The answer is ok, one line of words (issued with its end date, or the authority's refusal in plain words) and the screen as secureAddress.get returns it; never a key or a token. Refused 409 SECURE_ADDRESS_NODE on a node (its certificate comes from the lead), and 409 SECURE_ADDRESS_UNAVAILABLE with words when https is off or the certificate is one the person made (they renew it themselves); nothing changes then. A certificate is also issued again by itself when it is due and when a machine that held it leaves or is removed from the group.

errorCodes.meaning: There is no certificate GoodVibes can issue here now: the https address is off, or it serves a certificate the person made (they renew it themselves); nothing changed.
This machine is a member of a group whose lead has a secure address: it comes from the lead, and nothing is set here.

methods.title: Replace The Secure Address Authority
methods.description: The Secure address screen's "Replace the authority", where this computer serves GoodVibes' own certificate: its certificate authority is removed and a new one made, and a new server certificate signed by it is served here and sent, sealed, to the machines that follow this computer. Every phone must then remove the old GoodVibes certificate and install the new one from the page /lan-https; until it does it shows a warning for the address. It is what ends, at once, the trust a phone gives a machine that left the group or was removed and still holds a certificate the old authority signed. It cannot be undone: the screens ask first, opening on No. No input. The answer is ok, one line of words (with the new authority's fingerprint) and the screen as secureAddress.get returns it; never a key. Refused 409 SECURE_ADDRESS_NODE on a member of a group, and 409 SECURE_ADDRESS_UNAVAILABLE when https is off or the certificate in force is not GoodVibes' own.

errorCodes.meaning: There is no certificate GoodVibes can issue here now: the https address is off, or it serves a certificate the person made (they renew it themselves); nothing changed.
This machine is a member of a group whose lead has a secure address: it comes from the lead, and nothing is set here.

methods.title: Serve Other Machines For The Secure Address
methods.description: The Secure address screen's "Serve other machines", offered while other machines are not served (controlPlane.enabled off, or the daemon listening on this computer only), when a phone cannot open the https address: what goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan writes, so the daemon listens on the network and answers other machines; each still needs its own pairing or sign-in. The answer comes once the listener is bound again: ok, one line of words and the screen as secureAddress.get returns it. Refused 409 SECURE_ADDRESS_UNAVAILABLE when this daemon cannot change it from here.

errorCodes.meaning: There is no certificate GoodVibes can issue here now: the https address is off, or it serves a certificate the person made (they renew it themselves); nothing changed.

methods.title: Set Up The Secure Address
methods.description: The Secure address screen's change. certificate lets-encrypt (domain, and cloudflareToken when none is stored: a token with Zone, DNS, Edit on the zone that holds the name, stored in the secret store only once Cloudflare accepted it; never returned), own-files (certFile and keyFile, paths on the daemon's machine, checked first: the key must belong to the certificate and it must be in force), local-authority (GoodVibes' own certificate), or off (the https listener stops; plain http is unchanged). Refused 400 SECURE_ADDRESS_INVALID with words and nothing written when the input cannot work; refused 409 SECURE_ADDRESS_NODE on a node of a group, whose secure address comes from its lead. Otherwise the web UI is served to the network when it is not yet (what goodvibes-daemon webui enable --lan writes), secureAddress.* and controlPlane.lanHttps.enabled are written, and the answer (the same as secureAddress.get) comes once the https listener has synced and, for Let's Encrypt, once the order has an outcome: issued, or the authority's refusal in plain words.

errorCodes.meaning: The change could not be made as given (a name that is not a domain name, a token Cloudflare refused for the name's zone, certificate files that are not a valid pair in force); the message says what to change, and nothing was written.
This machine is a member of a group whose lead has a secure address: it comes from the lead, and nothing is set here.

methods.title: Detect Tailscale Environment
methods.description: READ-ONLY detection of a usable tailscale environment: binary present, logged-in status, MagicDNS name, and the https URL `tailscale serve` would yield. Never invokes a state-changing tailscale command. Where tailscale is absent the result says so once, surfaces offer the auto-wire affordance only when this reports a usable environment; nothing nags. Includes the most recent serve or stop receipt (lastServe), and activeServe: the serve this daemon started and has not stopped, which tailscale keeps on until tailscale.serve.stop runs.

methods.title: Set Up Tailscale Serve For The Daemon
methods.description: The one-action https affordance: run `tailscale serve --bg <port>` so tailscale fronts the web UI at its https MagicDNS URL, the port being the one the web UI is served on: the control-plane port while the daemon serves the bundle (controlPlane.webui.serve), web.port for a web UI it does not serve (web.enabled). With no web UI served it is refused with 409 WEB_UI_NOT_SERVED and nothing runs. Run only from this explicit user-initiated verb. The serve persists in tailscaled, also after the daemon stops or restarts, until tailscale.serve.stop runs. The attempt is recorded with an honest receipt either way (when tailscale prints a link to turn Serve on for the tailnet, the receipt carries it as enableUrl); on success the https address is asked once for the daemon's health (`answers`: ok and why), and only when it answers is web.publicBaseUrl updated to it, keeping the value it replaced for the stop. TLS on this route is terminated by tailscale with a certificate the phone already trusts (the other https route is the daemon's own LAN certificate, webui https).

errorCodes.meaning: No web UI is served on this machine, so tailscale serve would front nothing and nothing ran; serve it first with goodvibes-daemon webui enable --bundle-dir <dir>.

methods.title: Stop Tailscale Serve For The Daemon
methods.description: Stop publishing the daemon to the tailnet: run `tailscale serve --https=443 off`, which removes what tailscale.serve.run started. The attempt is recorded with an honest receipt either way. On success, when web.publicBaseUrl still names the tailnet URL, it is put back to the value it had before the serve (cleared when none was recorded); publicBaseUrlDetail says what happened to it.

methods.title: Review Snapshot
methods.description: Return the integration review snapshot used by external helpers.

methods.title: Apply a Unified Rewind
methods.description: Apply a unified rewind to a session turn anchor, restoring files and/or conversation. DESTRUCTIVE: requires the confirmToken minted by rewind.plan (single-use, ~2 min), which is bound to the session, turn, scope, previewed checkpoint and the conversation as it was counted (its message count and last message). Called without it, it returns a non-error refusal (refused:true) naming rewind.plan, never a silent no-op; an unknown or expired token is a 400; a token whose target changed since the plan (a message arrived, another checkpoint now resolves) is a 409 TARGET_CHANGED naming each change, and nothing is changed. Every apply records an undo point (the workspace restore takes a pre-restore safety checkpoint; the conversation store captures its pre-rewind snapshot) so the rewind is itself reversible, and returns a receipt whose `undo` block carries how to reverse it: checkpoints.restore with undo.files.restoreCheckpointId for the files, rewind.undo with undo.conversation.undoSnapshotId for the conversation. undo.conversation.expiresAfter states how long that undo point lasts, as the process holding the conversation keeps it (the newest 32 rewinds; on disk where that process keeps its sessions). The conversation is cut only at the revision the apply was confirmed against: a message that arrives while the files are restored is not cut, and the conversation half is reported skipped in a warning (plan again with scope conversation) while the receipt keeps the files undo point. Scope conversation or both is admitted only for an owner of the session (or an owner or admin credential); another caller is refused 403 NOT_YOURS, naming sessions.hosted.share. Emits a REWIND_APPLIED receipt event.

methods.title: Offer This Surface's Live Conversation for Rewind
methods.description: Register the conversation this surface is running for a session, so a conversation-scope rewind of it can actually be served. Only the process holding the messages can count or drop them: without this, rewind.plan for a session hosted anywhere but the daemon reports the conversation half unavailable, and files rewind is unaffected either way. Re-registering with the hostId returned here RENEWS the offer; registering without one claims the session and replaces whoever held it, answering that surface's outstanding requests as unavailable. The registration is a lease, not a reservation, it lapses unless the surface keeps taking its requests, and nothing about it survives a daemon restart, because a claim about a live process is worthless once the process on either end may be gone.

methods.title: Withdraw a Conversation Rewind Offer
methods.description: Withdraw this surface's offer to serve a session's conversation, when the session ends, or the surface is going away. Outstanding requests put to it are answered unavailable rather than left to time out. Only the registered host may release its own session; anyone else is refused.

methods.title: List Conversation Rewind Hosts
methods.description: Which sessions have a surface offering their live conversation right now, how each surface names itself, and when its lease runs out. This is what makes "conversation rewind is unavailable for that session" checkable rather than something a person has to take on trust.

methods.title: Answer a Conversation Rewind Request
methods.description: Report what this surface found or did. Which fields are expected follows from the REQUEST, which already says whether it was a preview, a rewind or an undo, an answer that restated that could only disagree with it, silently. For a preview: messagesToDrop and messagesRemaining. For a rewind: droppedMessages and the undoSnapshotId that restores them, optionally undoExpiresAfter saying how long this surface keeps it. For an undo: undone:true once the pre-rewind conversation is back and its save was tried, with notSaved saying why when that save failed. For any kind, a non-empty unavailableReason instead, which is the honest answer when the conversation is gone or this surface cannot serve it, and saying so beats staying silent, because silence becomes a timeout and a timed-out rewind cannot tell whether the messages were dropped; an undo refusal adds unavailableCode UNDO_POINT_GONE, CONVERSATION_CHANGED, or TARGET_CHANGED when the snapshot is of another session. A preview may add revision, the conversation's message count and last message key, which a rewind plan binds; a rewind request carries it back as expectedRevision, and a conversation whose revision differs is not cut (answer unavailableReason saying it changed after the plan). Only the surface a request was put to may answer it.

methods.title: Take Conversation Rewind Requests
methods.description: Collect the conversation questions waiting for this host, how many messages a rewind to an anchor would drop, a request to actually drop them, or a request to undo a rewind from its undoSnapshotId, and renew its lease, because a surface that is polling is a surface that is alive. With nothing waiting, pass waitMs to hold the call open until something arrives; an empty result is a normal answer, not an error. Answer each request with rewind.conversation.requests.answer before its expiresAt, or the caller waiting on it is told, honestly, that this surface did not answer in time.

methods.title: Preview a Unified Rewind
methods.description: Dry-run preview of a unified rewind to a session turn anchor: exactly what restoring files (the nearest workspace checkpoint), conversation (truncating session state to the anchor), or both would change, and a short-lived single-use confirm token authorizing the matching rewind.apply. Read-only, nothing is changed. A part with no store wired on this runtime is reported unavailable in a warning, never faked. Scope conversation or both is admitted only for an owner of the session (or an owner or admin credential), as steering it is; another caller is refused 403 NOT_YOURS, naming sessions.hosted.share. Scope files is workspace-wide, as checkpoints.restore is.

methods.title: Undo a Conversation Rewind
methods.description: Put a session's conversation back to how it was before a rewind, from the undo.conversation.undoSnapshotId of the rewind.apply receipt. The pre-rewind copy replaces the whole conversation, so the undo is refused while the conversation has newer messages than the rewind left it with. Answers undone:true, or undone:false with a refusal (code, state, reason, next) and nothing changed: the snapshot is gone (see the receipt's undo.conversation.expiresAfter), the conversation changed since, the snapshot is of another session than sessionId (TARGET_CHANGED, naming that session), or the surface holding the conversation did not answer. When the undo took effect but the conversation's store could not save it, `notSaved` says so and what to do: a restart would bring back the rewound transcript. A conversation a surface is hosting is restored by that surface, asked over its rewind.conversation.requests channel; one this daemon holds is restored here. Files are reversed separately with checkpoints.restore. Admitted only for an owner of the session (or an owner or admin credential); another caller is refused 403 NOT_YOURS, naming sessions.hosted.share.

methods.title: Create Route Binding
methods.description: Create or upsert a route binding.

methods.title: Delete Route Binding
methods.description: Delete an existing route binding.

methods.title: List Route Bindings
methods.description: Return configured route bindings.

methods.title: Update Route Binding
methods.description: Update an existing route binding. (Renamed from routes.bindings.patch in the 1.0.0 core-verb rename, canonical verb is update, not patch.)

methods.title: Route Snapshot
methods.description: Return the route and binding integration snapshot. A binding carries the chat's title and who wrote from it, so it needs read:channel-content.

methods.title: List Surfaces
methods.description: Return registered channel and control surfaces. Stay current by subscribing to the surfaces event domain: SURFACE_ENABLED and SURFACE_DISABLED when a surface is switched on or off, SURFACE_CAPABILITY_CHANGED when a capability is added or removed, SURFACE_ACCOUNT_CONNECTED and SURFACE_ACCOUNT_DEGRADED when a channel starts working or starts failing.

methods.title: Delete a Retained Device Capture
methods.description: Remove one retained camera or screen capture now, before its retention window ends: the file on the daemon host and its record. The removal is added to the housekeeping disclosure like a sweep removal, with the reason `deleted`. `deleted` is true only when the file was unlinked; a capture whose file was already gone (`file-missing`) or no longer matches what was taken (`content-mismatch`, the file is kept for inspection) loses its record and says so. An id that is not retained is a 404.

methods.title: List Retained Device Captures
methods.description: The camera and screen captures still inside their retention window, newest first, with when each was captured, when it will be deleted, and the reason the request stated. Expired captures are never listed, retention is enforced by the store, not by this verb filtering them out of a longer list.

methods.title: Read a Retained Device Capture
methods.description: Return one retained capture's bytes, base64-encoded, for a caller that is not running on the daemon host and so cannot open the file itself. The store re-hashes the bytes against the digest recorded when the capture was retained and refuses to serve a mismatch, so a torn or half-written file is never handed back as if it were the picture that was taken. A capture that is gone, expired, swept, missing, or corrupted, is an honest 404 naming which of those it was.

methods.title: Request a Capability From a Paired Device
methods.description: Ask one paired device node for one capability, a photo, a screen capture, a location fix, its clipboard, a notification, a link to open, a buzz, and return what came back. The reason is required and is shown VERBATIM on the confirmation prompt, so the person deciding sees what the caller said it was for. Every gate lives in the daemon-owned device runtime and this verb re-decides none of them: a durable grant is read from the authority record every machine of the group shares, so a grant revoked on any of them is not honoured; work waiting for the phone under a grant that is then revoked is withdrawn (refusal grant-revoked-before-claim), and work the phone had already picked up answers grant-revoked-after-claim saying what took effect; a request with no grant asks the person on whatever surface they are looking at, a capability turned off by configuration is refused with the configuration key that turned it off, and a capture is retained under the configured retention window and disclosed. A refusal is returned as ok:false with the reason and a machine-readable refusal code, it is an answer, not an error. A capability that produces a capture returns an artifact REFERENCE; fetch the bytes with devices.artifacts.read.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: List Device Capability Grants
methods.description: The durable "always allow" grants a person gave, per capability and per device, with when each was granted, when it expires, and how often it has been used, plus the ledger, newest `limit` records (default 100; a larger limit reads further back): every grant given and every one revoked or expired is kept for good, uses for 30 days (the newest 500).

methods.title: Revoke a Device Capability Grant
methods.description: Revoke durable grants by grant id, by device, by capability, or any combination. A revocation is a terminal entry on the authority record, so it holds on every machine of the group, after a restart, and on a machine that was away when it was made; the next request for that capability asks the person again, and a request still waiting for the phone under a revoked grant is withdrawn. Returns exactly what was revoked: a grant already revoked answers revoked 0, so a repeat after a lost reply succeeds. Naming nothing (no grantId, nodeId or capabilityId) is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a grantId the record never held is 404 GRANT_NOT_FOUND (read devices.grants.list for the ids); nothing is revoked either way.

methods.title: Run Device Housekeeping
methods.description: Sweep the device grants ledger and the retained captures now: expired and orphaned grants removed, captures past their retention window deleted, torn or missing capture files reaped. Returns the itemised disclosure of everything removed and why.

methods.title: List Paired Device Nodes
methods.description: Every phone paired as a device node, with the capabilities it announced, the ones it did not offer, and the ones it announced but cannot currently serve because its connection is not a secure context. Node-kind neutral: a web app node and a native app node are described identically.

methods.title: Runtime Metrics
methods.description: Return the process-wide runtime metrics snapshot: HTTP/LLM/auth/transport counters, gauges, request-duration and token histograms, and per-model tool-format telemetry (edit-tool failure classes and declared exec-expectation misses).

methods.title: Scheduler Capacity
methods.description: Return the current automation-scheduler capacity snapshot: total slots, in-use slots, queue depth, and age of the oldest queued run. Requires an admin principal.

methods.title: Install Service
methods.description: Install the GoodVibes platform service.

methods.title: Restart Service
methods.description: Restart the GoodVibes platform service.

methods.title: Start Service
methods.description: Start the GoodVibes platform service.

methods.title: Service Status
methods.description: Return platform service installation and runtime posture.

methods.title: Stop Service
methods.description: Stop the GoodVibes platform service.

methods.title: Uninstall Service
methods.description: Uninstall the GoodVibes platform service.

methods.title: Get Session Workspace Changes
methods.description: Return the aggregate workspace file changes a session made, joined over its sessionId-stamped checkpoints: the net diff (files, unified diff, --stat) from the state before the session's earliest checkpoint to its latest. A session with no stamped checkpoints returns checkpointCount:0 with an empty diff (from/to:"EMPTY"), an honest "nothing recorded", not an error.

methods.title: Announce a Session Checkpoint Change
methods.description: A terminal program that runs its own session (the terminal app, the Agent) tells the daemon it made, pruned or removed a workspace checkpoint for that session, so clients subscribed to the daemon hear of it: the daemon announces it as the runtime event LIST_CHANGED with `list: "checkpoints"`, the `change` given and `checkpointId` as its `id`. Nothing is stored and nothing is read from disk; the notice only announces. The session must be one the daemon knows (registered with sessions.register): another id is refused 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND and nothing is announced. A repeat announces again, which is harmless: a client reads the checkpoint list again.

errorCodes.meaning: No shared session has that id.

methods.title: Close Shared Session
methods.description: Mark a shared session as closed.

errorCodes.meaning: No shared session has that id.
A daemon-hosted session is still running; end it with sessions.hosted.kill, which also closes the record. Nothing was changed.

methods.title: Get Session Context Usage
methods.description: Return the live context-window usage for a session: estimatedContextTokens (the runtime's current estimate, not a fresh preflight count), a source-supported contextWindow or configured cap, and the derived contextUsagePct and contextRemainingTokens (all three null when capacity is unknown). Typed source, origin and accepted-input floor metadata remain separate from the known ceiling. `estimated` is always true, marking the token figure as an estimate rather than a fact. Answers for the daemon's own runtime session and every session it hosts; a session it runs but keeps no figure for (an active channel session) is a 409 CONTEXT_USAGE_UNAVAILABLE, and any other session id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

methods.title: Create Shared Session
methods.description: Create a shared session for a surface, route, or web client. `workingDirectory` names the project it belongs to (checked as every call's project is); the session is its caller's, kept as who made it. A caller below an admin makes one only in a project the owner gave it, or one of no project that only it and the owner reach.

methods.title: Delete Shared Session
methods.description: Permanently remove a shared session record and its queued inputs/messages from the home-scoped store. A distinct, explicit hard-delete verb, NEVER triggered by close; closed sessions stay listable (includeClosed) and deletionRetentionMs semantics for non-deleted records are untouched. Requires the session to already be closed: deleting a still-active session is rejected with 409 SESSION_ACTIVE (close it, then delete). An unknown or already-deleted id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop. Emits control.session_update (session-deleted) so subscribers drop the row live.

errorCodes.meaning: No shared session has that id.
The session is still active; close it, then delete it.

methods.title: Detach Shared Session Participant
methods.description: Remove a surface's participant and its route binding from a session so that surface stops receiving updates, WITHOUT closing or killing the session (detach != close != kill). Every participant carrying the given surfaceId is removed and any route binding they alone held is unbound; the session and all other participants keep running. Idempotent: detaching an already-detached surface, or detaching from a closed session, is a no-op success. An unknown session is a 404.

errorCodes.meaning: No shared session has that id.

methods.title: Queue Shared Session Follow-Up
methods.description: Queue a deferred follow-up for a shared session so it runs after the current agent completes, or spawn immediately when the session is idle.

replay.name: messageId
replay.behavior: Sending the same messageId again to the same session (1 to 255 letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-", chosen by the caller) returns the input already recorded (the same input id, with its current state, and mode continued-live; the reply carries no duplicate flag) instead of recording a second one; an input that failed is run again in that session. The id is scoped to the session and surface: the same id sent to another session is a new message there. Use it to resend after a lost response.

errorCodes.meaning: messageId is not 1 to 255 letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-"; nothing was changed.
No shared session has that id.
The session is closed; reopen it (sessions.reopen) before sending to it.
The input was accepted but the agent started for it could not be bound; the input was released to the queue.

methods.title: Get Shared Session
methods.description: Return a shared session record with its newest 100 messages. It returns conversation text, so it needs read:transcripts, as sessions.list and sessions.search do (titles and participants).

errorCodes.meaning: No shared session has that id.

methods.title: Attach to a Daemon-Hosted Session
methods.description: Join a hosted session and receive its transcript so far, so a client that was never connected, or one reconnecting after the daemon restarted, renders what it missed instead of an empty screen. A session restored from disk has its loop rebuilt on this call, with a system line in the transcript stating that its in-flight turn did not survive the restart. Live output continues on the `turn` and `tools` event domains, filtered on this session id. Attaching is what keeps a `kill`-policy session alive: the policy is applied when the LAST client detaches. An attachment carries a LEASE, `hostedSessions.attachmentTtlMs`, ten minutes by default, or `leaseMs` for this attachment alone, because a client that crashed or closed its tab never calls detach, and a claim nothing expires would hold a kill-policy session open forever. Calling attach again with the same `clientId` renews it, and a client whose control-plane connection is still open renews automatically, so an attached client watching a long turn in silence is never reaped. When the last attachment lapses the session is treated as detached and its policy decides. A credential below admin attaches only to a session it created or an owner shared with it (sessions.hosted.share), and needs read:transcripts as well as write:sessions because the call returns the transcript; anyone else is refused 403 NOT_YOURS naming session.share. Attaching never makes the caller an owner. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: Create a Daemon-Hosted Session
methods.description: Compose a full conversation loop INSIDE the daemon for a workspace: the same orchestrator, tool registry and permission gate a terminal runs, hosted here so the conversation does not depend on the client that started it staying open. `workspaceRoot` must be absolute, a relative path would resolve against the daemon's own directory, which is never what the caller meant, and must be the daemon's working directory or a registered workspace (or inside one); anything else is refused with the allowed folders named (sessions.hosted.workspaces lists them). `modelId` is resolved against this daemon's live model registry when given, so an unknown, ambiguous or unselectable id is refused here, 400 MODEL_NOT_FOUND, MODEL_AMBIGUOUS or MODEL_NOT_SELECTABLE, rather than at the first turn; omitted, the session follows the daemon's current selection. `detachPolicy` overrides the `hostedSessions.detachPolicy` setting for this session alone. `originSurface` names the app the session is for (`agent`, `tui`, `webui`); its client-owned settings are that app's, and with `agent` the session answers as the GoodVibes Agent: the Agent's prompt and its tools that need no terminal, the others refused and named. Its operator tools act on this daemon with full operator authority, so `agent` is refused (HOSTED_SURFACE_FORBIDDEN) for a caller that does not hold admin. `initialPrompt` is submitted as the first user message and the call does NOT wait for that turn, watch the `turn` and `tools` event domains filtered on the returned session id. Refused (429 HOSTED_SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED) with the live count and the setting named when `hostedSessions.maxSessions` is already reached. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

errorCodes.meaning: workspaceRoot is relative or outside the allowed folders, or another field is malformed (named in `field`); nothing was created.
No model in this daemon's registry answers to modelId; nothing was created. Name a model it holds, or none.
modelId is served by several providers; nothing was created. Name it provider-qualified.
The model modelId names cannot be chosen; nothing was created.
originSurface agent needs an admin credential; nothing was created.
hostedSessions.maxSessions live sessions already exist; end one or raise the setting.
The workspace's provider setup failed or the daemon is shutting down; nothing was created.

methods.title: Detach from a Daemon-Hosted Session
methods.description: Leave a hosted session. When other clients are still attached, nothing else happens. When this was the LAST client, the effective detach policy decides: `kill` (the default, and what closing a client has always done) terminates the session with the reason `detached`; `survive` leaves it idle and reattachable. The policy is the session's own override when it was created with one and the `hostedSessions.detachPolicy` setting otherwise, and the returned record says which applied and what the session now is, never a guess by the caller. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: Read a Daemon-Hosted Session's Transcript
methods.description: Return a hosted session's record and its transcript, live or ended, without attaching. An ended session (its last client detached under the kill policy, its attachment lease lapsed, it was killed, or the daemon restarted) keeps its transcript on disk until `hostedSessions.terminatedRetentionMs` (24 hours by default) retires it, so its reply stays readable here, also after a daemon restart; after that the id answers 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND. An admin credential reads any session; any other credential reads only a session its principal created or an owner shared with it (sessions.hosted.share), else 403 HOSTED_SESSION_NOT_OWNED. Reading changes nothing and does not keep a kill-policy session alive. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

errorCodes.meaning: This daemon holds no hosted session with that id, or its retention ended; nothing was read.
The session was not created by this credential or shared with it; ask an owner to share it, or read it with an admin credential.

methods.title: End a Daemon-Hosted Session
methods.description: End a hosted session regardless of who is attached or what its detach policy says: the in-flight turn is interrupted, its loop is taken apart, its workspace floor is released when it was the last session using it, and the record is kept, terminated, with the reason `killed`, until `hostedSessions.terminatedRetentionMs` retires it. Killing an already-terminated session returns that record unchanged rather than reporting an error for work that is already done. A credential below admin ends only a session it created or was shared (403 NOT_YOURS otherwise). ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: List Daemon-Hosted Sessions
methods.description: Every session this daemon hosts, most recently updated first. Terminated sessions are excluded unless `includeTerminated` is set, they are kept, with the reason they ended, until the retention window retires them, so a session that stopped can be asked about instead of having simply vanished. Each record carries the policy that would apply on the next detach, so a client can show what leaving will do before it leaves. A session's title is its first prompt unless one was given, so it needs read:transcripts, and a credential below admin is listed only the sessions it created or was shared. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: Share a Daemon-Hosted Session
methods.description: Add a principal (a user name, or `pairing:<id>` for a paired device) to a hosted session's owners, so it may attach, read the transcript and watch the session's turns live (`read:own-sessions`). Only an owner of the session or an admin shares it; anyone else is refused 403 NOT_YOURS. A principal this daemon does not know (no such user, no live pairing) is refused 404 PRINCIPAL_NOT_FOUND, naming local_auth.status and pairing.tokens.list. The owners are saved with the session and outlive its end and a restart; sharing with a principal that already owns it changes nothing (`added: false`). Attaching never adds an owner, so this is the one way another credential joins a session; sessions.hosted.unshare undoes it. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

errorCodes.meaning: This daemon holds no hosted session with that id; nothing was shared.
No user, live pairing or owner credential on this daemon has that principal id; nothing was shared.
The caller is not an owner of the session and not an admin; nothing was shared.

methods.title: Stop Sharing a Daemon-Hosted Session
methods.description: Remove a principal from a hosted session's owners: it can no longer attach, read the transcript or watch the session, and every client it attached is detached at once (the session's detach policy applies when those were the last attached). Only an owner of the session or an admin does it; anyone else is refused 403 NOT_YOURS. The last owner is never removed (409 HOSTED_SESSION_LAST_OWNER): share with another principal first, or end the session. Removing a principal that is not an owner changes nothing (`removed: false`). The change is saved with the session. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

errorCodes.meaning: This daemon holds no hosted session with that id; nothing was changed.
The caller is not an owner of the session and not an admin; nothing was changed.
That principal is the session's only owner; nothing was changed.

methods.title: Folders a Hosted Session May Use
methods.description: The folders sessions.hosted.create accepts as workspaceRoot: the daemon's working directory and every registered workspace (a path inside one is accepted too). The same list contract work dispatched into a hosted session is held to. ws-only invoke verb; no REST binding.

methods.title: Cancel Shared Session Input
methods.description: Cancel a queued shared-session input before it is delivered or spawned. An input already being answered (delivered/spawned) or already ended is refused with 409 `CANCEL_NOT_ALLOWED`, the input in its actual state, and no cancel event; an already-cancelled input answers 200.

errorCodes.meaning: Only a queued input can be cancelled; the body says whether it is running or ended.

methods.title: Mark Shared Session Input Delivered
methods.description: A live registered surface reports that it collected a queued input (moves it to `delivered`) or finished acting on it (`consumed:true` moves it to `completed`). This is how a surface-managed session, where steer/follow-up inputs queue for the surface rather than spawn a daemon executor, closes the input lifecycle honestly. Only queued/delivered inputs advance; a report on an input that already ended (cancelled, failed, answered by a daemon agent) is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_DELIVERABLE` naming its state, binds no agent and forwards no answer. One exception: an input a daemon restart cancelled while a surface in another process was answering it completes on that surface's `consumed:true` report. `agentId` names the agent the surface is running for this input: it binds the reply so a message that arrived over a channel gets its answer routed back to that conversation, the same binding the daemon makes for the executors it spawns itself. `surfaceInstance`, sent with `agentId`, names the surface process running that agent; it is kept in the input's `metadata.deliveringSurfaceInstance` (cleared by a report that names none), so a surface that restarted can fail the inputs a process that is gone was answering. `answer` (sent with `consumed:true`, optionally with `status`) is the output that agent finished with, the daemon writes it into the session and delivers it to the channel. `claim:true` is how a surface takes an input before it starts work on it: it succeeds for one caller only, for a `queued` input, or for a `delivered` one with no agent bound for at least two minutes (a claimant that died before starting it). Any other caller is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_CLAIMABLE` naming the state, and nothing changes. A granted claim is recorded as the input's `metadata.claimEpoch` (1 for the first claimant, one more for each later one): that number is the claimant's token. `claim:true` with `claimEpoch` renews the caller's own claim (restarts the two-minute lease, epoch unchanged) while no agent is bound; a surface holds its claim this way while its work waits for capacity. Every other report on a claimed input must carry the current `claimEpoch`: a report from a claimant that was superseded is refused with 409 `INPUT_NOT_CLAIMABLE` and binds nothing.

methods.title: Get Session Permission Mode
methods.description: Return the session execution mode in force (`mode`): ask-me, jev-decides, just-vibes, yolo, or the read-only plan posture, read the way the gate decides calls. `chosenMode` is the mode the session chose, or the saved one; when they differ, `reason` says why (for example jev-decides runs as ask-me while no decision model is set or while the set one is not answering). `words` says the same in plain words for a person: `chosen` (the label of the chosen mode, "Jev decides"); when the mode in force differs, `inForce` (what is in force, written to lead after "Permissions: ": "asking you, for now"), `chosenWhen` (the chosen mode and the condition it waits on: "Jev decides once a decision model is set"), `chosenShort` (the choice and its cause in a few words, for where `chosenWhen` does not fit: "Jev decides: no decision model set"), `because` ("no decision model set", "decision model unreachable") and `failure` (true when `because` reports the decision model failing or out of reach, not a choice); a surface shows `inForce · chosenWhen`, then `because` when `failure` is true. Answers for the local runtime session (addressable as `runtime`), every session the daemon hosts, a channel session with its own mode, and a web chat (companion-chat), whose turns run under the daemon-wide mode; other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL.

methods.title: Set Session Permission Mode
methods.description: Set ask-me, jev-decides, just-vibes, or yolo execution, or enter the read-only plan posture. A hosted session and a channel session with its own mode change only that session; a web chat (companion-chat) has no mode of its own, so setting it rewrites the daemon-wide permissions.mode. Emits runtime.gate (PRESET_CHANGED) so every surface stays in sync. Other session ids answer 404 SESSION_NOT_LOCAL. A looser mode is set at once by every credential of the user (a sign-in under any name, a device paired with full scopes, the operator token); a device holding a narrow scope list is refused by its scopes.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

replay.name: Idempotency-Key
replay.behavior: Send a key (1 to 255 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_", ":" or "-") chosen once per logical request, and the same key on every retry: a repeat of the same request (for a multipart or raw upload: the same fields and file content, whatever the encoding) under the same key by the same credential, within a day and across a daemon restart, returns the first answer (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true header) instead of acting again. The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Discard A Work's Kept Branch
methods.description: Throw away the branch an ended piece of work kept, with the work's own folder and whatever they hold. It cannot be undone.

methods.title: Merge A Work's Kept Branch In
methods.description: Merge the branch an ended piece of work kept (its commits are not in the project's branch) into the project's current branch, then remove that branch and the work's own folder. A merge that conflicts is undone and nothing changes.

methods.title: List Your Work
methods.description: Every piece of work of this daemon's project, read in one call: what it is, what done means, where it stands (not started, its plan waiting, starting, its start cut off, running, needs you, a step failed, done, failed, stopped), its plan as steps with their state, the questions it waits on, the step it stopped at when one failed (what failed, and whether the work can go on without it), its spending limit and its results; and each piece of work proposed with its plan (`proposed: true`, not yet asked for). What the Work place, the web Work view and an agent read. No mutation and no execution.

methods.title: Approve A Plan
methods.description: Mark the waiting plan of a piece of work approved: its next start runs with exactly these steps. A proposed piece of work (work.propose) is approved as the piece of work it was then asked for as: `as` names that work, and the plan becomes its plan.

methods.title: Throw A Plan Away
methods.description: Throw away the waiting plan of a piece of work; the work stays, not started, and its next start writes a new plan.

methods.title: Write A Plan Again
methods.description: Write the waiting plan of a piece of work again from its goal and what done means (the planning agent splits it into steps again). It waits for approval again.

methods.title: Take A Step Out Of A Plan
methods.description: Take one step out of a waiting plan (and out of what the other steps wait on); the last step stays. The plan waits for approval again.

methods.title: Change A Step Of A Plan
methods.description: Change what one step of a waiting plan does. The plan waits for approval again.

methods.title: Move A Step Of A Plan
methods.description: Move one step of a waiting plan to another place, counting from 1. The plan waits for approval again.

methods.title: Name A Piece Of Work For An Act
methods.description: Read what an act on one piece of work sends, from the work alone: `operation` "execution" answers the identity start, status, stop and resume take (its current attempt and revisions); "contract" answers the run that answering, running a step again and the spending limit act on; "own" answers only whether this caller may act on the work at all (you may from any of your credentials, a sign-in, a paired device or the machine's token; a caller that is not you acts only on work it asked for itself: WORK_NOT_YOURS otherwise). Every other field is passed through. Answers { summary, input }; nothing is kept.

methods.title: Cancel Native Work Execution
methods.description: Persist cancellation for the selected existing attempt, including a pending initial admission. A distinct prevented-before-admission result carries no receipt; admitted execution cancellation waits for actual drainage. A lost response does not establish success.

methods.title: Resume Native Work Execution
methods.description: Explicitly resume an interrupted/refused intent with a fresh evaluation or recover one prepared execution under current paired authority. Original target stays fixed. Cancelled intents require a new legitimate attempt; launch-claimed effects are never replayed.

replay.name: attemptId
replay.behavior: One attempt (workId, attemptId and expectedRevision) runs once: an exact repeat returns the same execution identity instead of starting a second run; launch-claimed effects are never replayed.

methods.title: Start Native Work Execution
methods.description: Start one existing complete native work attempt using host-owned source and paired authority. Exact replays preserve identity; interrupted or refused intents require explicit resume, and cancelled intents never restart.

replay.name: attemptId
replay.behavior: One attempt (workId, attemptId and expectedRevision) runs once: an exact repeat returns the same execution identity instead of starting a second run; launch-claimed effects are never replayed.

methods.title: Read Native Work Execution
methods.description: Inspect a bounded execution or admission-intent projection for an existing native attempt. Intent projections contain no receipt or execution progress. Returns stored revisions even if the caller revision is stale.

methods.title: Read Native Work Ledger History
methods.description: Read at most 100 events after an exclusive cursor, pinned to a history high-water mark. Advance with cursor while hasMore is true. No mutations or execution.

methods.title: Admit Native Conversation Intake
methods.description: Start the single initial semantic admission of captured conversation text. Replay joins the current operation or reports recovery required. Does not start execution.

replay.name: inputId
replay.behavior: One input id is captured and admitted once: an exact repeat returns the original source identity or joins the operation already running instead of acting again.

methods.title: Cancel Native Conversation Intake
methods.description: Persist a terminal intake cancellation before work admission. If admission already committed, return its immutable work receipt. Does not claim cancellation of admitted work or execution.

methods.title: Capture Native Conversation Intake
methods.description: Persist exact original conversation text and unsupported-source disclosures on the selected authoritative host. Exact replay preserves the original source identity. Does not route, admit work, or execute. Complete encoded input is limited to 262144 bytes without truncation.

replay.name: inputId
replay.behavior: One input id is captured and admitted once: an exact repeat returns the original source identity or joins the operation already running instead of acting again.

methods.title: Get Native Conversation Intake
methods.description: Read the current conversation intake or immutable admitted-work receipt by original input ID. Does not route, retry, resume, admit, or execute.

methods.title: Resume Native Conversation Intake
methods.description: Explicitly recover captured conversation admission with a fresh semantic operation after interruption. Preserves source identity and terminal outcomes. Does not start execution.

replay.name: inputId
replay.behavior: One input id is captured and admitted once: an exact repeat returns the original source identity or joins the operation already running instead of acting again.

methods.title: Read Native Work Project
methods.description: Read only the selected host project identity. Does not confer execution eligibility or authority.

methods.title: Read Native Work Ledger
methods.description: Read the selected host project ledger, without mutation authority or allowedActions. Requires the dedicated read scope; a caller below an admin reads only a project given to it.

methods.title: Read Native Work Submission
methods.description: Look up an immutable native submission receipt by the original request ID on the selected authoritative host. Use after a lost submit response. Does not submit, retry, resume, or start execution.

methods.title: Submit Native Work
methods.description: Persist one bounded explicit-source goal and ordered criteria on the selected authoritative host. Exact request replay returns the immutable submission receipt. Does not start execution or grant verification authority. Complete encoded input is limited to 262144 bytes without truncation.

replay.name: requestId
replay.behavior: Sending the same requestId with the same content again returns the original immutable receipt (replayed: true). After a lost response, use workLedger.submission.get with the same requestId.

methods.title: Cancel Native Hosted Turn
methods.description: Persist cancellation of the exact native hosted dispatch and drain its owned turn. Cancellation does not undo effects already performed.

methods.title: Inspect Native Hosted Session
methods.description: Read authoritative native session ownership. Only an explicit legacy result permits ordinary session ingress. Native sessions additionally require their current paired owner and native delivery scopes.

methods.title: Start Native Hosted Turn
methods.description: Deliver an already admitted native conversation input at most once through a host-owned broker identity and durable dispatch claim bound to the WebUI settings owner. An optional execution mode initializes only a new session; continuation and replay retain the current session mode. Cross-surface replay is refused. Ambiguous dispatch requires inspection and is never replayed.

replay.name: inputId
replay.behavior: An admitted input (inputId with its sourceRevision) is delivered at most once: a repeat joins or reports the first dispatch instead of starting a second turn. An ambiguous dispatch is never replayed; read it with workLedger.turn.status.

methods.title: Start Agent Native Hosted Turn
methods.description: Deliver an already admitted native conversation input at most once through a host-owned broker identity and durable dispatch claim bound to the Agent settings owner. An optional execution mode initializes only a new session; continuation and replay retain the current session mode. Cross-surface replay is refused. Ambiguous dispatch requires inspection and is never replayed.

replay.name: inputId

methods.title: Status Native Hosted Turn
methods.description: Read native hosted dispatch status. Does not admit, claim, retry or execute.

methods.title: List the Projects the Daemon Knows
methods.description: The registered workspace roots a caller with no folder of its own (the web UI, a script) can choose to act in, each once with its label. The daemon's own folder is never offered as a project. A capability bound to a project takes the chosen one as workingDirectory (capabilities.run, places.counts) or project (worktrees.snapshot); nothing picks one for the caller. Read-only.

methods.title: Register a Workspace
methods.description: Register a workspace root so the whole subtree beneath it is covered. Refuses an absurdly broad root (the home directory, the filesystem root, or the daemon state directory) with a 400, coverage flows down the entire subtree, so a root that broad would sweep far more than a project. Idempotent: re-registering the same normalized root returns alreadyRegistered:true. A root registered before native work existed has no native scope; re-registering it grants that scope and answers nativeScopeGranted:true (false otherwise), which is the step a native-work refusal asks for. Registering a root clears any remembered decline recorded at exactly that root.

methods.title: List Registered Workspaces
methods.description: Return every registered workspace root (coverage flows down each root's subtree) and every remembered subtree-scoped decline. Read-only.

methods.title: Unregister a Workspace
methods.description: Remove a registered workspace root. Returns { removed: false } when no root with that normalized path was registered, an honest boolean, never a 200 that pretends a phantom root was removed.

methods.title: Resolve Workspace Coverage
methods.description: Resolve a path against the registry: covered (by which nearest registered root), declined (at which root), or unknown. Coverage flows DOWN a registered root's subtree and is inherited through the git worktree→main-repo link, a linked worktree outside any registered root still resolves to the main repo's registration. When mainWorktreeRoot is omitted the daemon probes the link itself. Read-only.

methods.title: Discard a Worktree
methods.description: Remove a worktree per the eviction-preserving rules: any uncommitted state is first committed onto the worktree's branch (a preservation failure REFUSES the removal rather than losing work), the directory is removed, and the branch is KEPT. `project` names the project (its folder's full path, a git repository on this machine) the worktree belongs to; absent, the daemon's own working folder. Returns an honest receipt (ok, branch kept, preservation commit, detail) either way.

methods.title: Re-run Worktree Setup
methods.description: Re-run cold-start setup (worktree.setup.commands, then untracked-file carry-over from worktree.setup.carryOverGlobs; each is auto, none or a list, and auto derives from the repository) on a live worktree by path, recording the honest outcome onto the worktree record. `project` names the project (its folder's full path, a git repository on this machine) whose worktree it is and whose register records it; absent, the daemon's own working folder. Returns the setup result: state skipped (nothing to run or copy), succeeded, or failed with the failing step and error, which names a derived step as derived. A failed setup is a visible worktree state, never silent.

The same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a repeat while the first is still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT (send it again with the same key after the Retry-After header's seconds, also in the body as retryAfterMs; the SDK does this within its retries); a repeat after the daemon stopped in the middle of the first is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a repeat of a first request that failed partway is 500 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (either way: check the state, do not send again). A refusal (4xx) is not remembered, so the same key may be sent again. Over the method-invoke envelope or a WebSocket call frame the key may be sent as `idempotencyKey` beside `body`.

methods.title: Worktrees Snapshot
methods.description: Return the worktrees of a project and their ownership summary: project (a folder's full path, one workspaces.projects.list names) reads that project's register, the one its terminal programs keep; without it, the daemon's own folder. The method invoke and the GET route (`?project=`) are the same handler. A register's change is announced as LIST_CHANGED worktrees. 400 when project is not a full path, 404 when it is not a git repository this machine has.

events.description: Watcher state and heartbeat events.

events.title: Own Session Activity
events.description: What a credential without the admin role holding `read:own-sessions` receives of the sessions its own principal created or an owner shared with it (sessions.hosted.create, sessions.hosted.share): their `turn`, `tools`, `gate` and `session` runtime frames (streamed text, tool calls and results, permission decisions, turn transitions), their `approval-update` events and their `hosted-session-update` notices. Frames of every other session, and frames naming no session, are withheld; the admin-only domains stay admin-only for everything else. Open the stream with `?domains=turn,tools,gate,session` (or subscribe to those domains on the socket) and filter on the session id. Ownership is saved with the session, so it holds across a daemon restart.

events.title: Approval Record Update
events.description: Every approval record transition, pushed the moment the broker records it: an ask RAISED (status pending, this is the prompt arriving), claimed by a surface, approved, denied, cancelled, or expired. The payload is the whole `approval` record plus the `createdAt` of the notice, so a subscriber renders the prompt from the event and never needs a follow-up read to draw it. This is the channel that makes approvals.raise usable from a surface that is not in the daemon process: raise returns the pending record and the DECISION arrives here, so a client gets keystroke-fast prompt delivery instead of polling approvals.list on a timer. Domain-tagged `gate` (gateway-scope-enforcement.ts EVENT_DOMAIN), so a client that opened the stream with ?domains=… must include `gate` to receive it; a client that opted into no domain narrowing receives it as before. The record is the daemon's, not the subscriber's: several surfaces see the same transition and the daemon remains the single source of the applied result, a surface renders what the record says rather than what it locally decided. The payload also carries `reading`, the record's reading for an admin who may answer (what is waiting, on whom, the deadline, the decision and whether the asker received it), and every record carries `revision`. A subscriber applies a frame only when its revision is higher than the one it holds, so a late or repeated frame never makes a settled approval actionable again; after a gap or a reconnect it reads approvals.list once, because frames are not replayed.

events.title: Heartbeat
events.description: Keepalive event emitted by the SSE control-plane transport.

events.title: Hosted Session Lifecycle Update
events.description: Every lifecycle transition of a session whose loop runs INSIDE the daemon: created, attached, detached, turn started, turn ended, terminated, and restored after a restart, plus a contract started in the session and a line the session said for one of its contracts (a question for the owner, or the outcome). The payload carries the whole hosted-session record plus the transition name, the client it is about (attach/detach) and a short detail, so a subscriber renders the change from the event and needs no follow-up read. This channel is LIFECYCLE ONLY. The turn itself, streamed tokens, tool calls, tool results, turn transitions, is already on the `turn` and `tools` runtime domains, stamped with the hosted session id, because a hosted session runs the ordinary orchestrator; a client watches those exactly as it does for a local session and filters on the id it was handed. A second copy of that stream is not published here. Domain-tagged `session`, so a client narrowing with ?domains=… must include `session` to receive it. The record is the daemon's: `effectiveDetachPolicy` says what leaving would do right now, and `terminatedReason` says why a session ended, a hosted session never simply disappears.

events.title: Owner Inbox Update
events.description: A question, claim, purchase window or queued action in the owner inbox was posted, answered or withdrawn. The payload is the whole `item` plus the `createdAt` of the notice, so a surface renders the change and an agent waiting on its question reads the answer without a follow-up inbox.list. Approvals are not repeated here; they arrive on control.approval_update. Domain-tagged `gate`, like approvals: a client narrowing with ?domains=… must include `gate`.

events.title: Ready Handshake
events.description: Initial SSE/WebSocket handshake event emitted after a control-plane subscription is opened. `domains` is what the stream delivers; `withheldDomains` names requested domains this credential may not read; `unrecognisedDomains` names requested `?domains=` values that are not runtime event domains, so nothing will arrive for them (a request naming only unknown domains is refused with 400 UNKNOWN_EVENT_DOMAIN).

events.title: Remote Peer and Work Update
events.description: Distributed-runtime notices about paired peers and the work they run: a pair request and its approval, rejection or verification, a peer connecting, its heartbeat and disconnect, a peer token rotated or revoked, and remote work queued, claimed, settled or cancelled. The wire event name is the notice; the payload carries the sanitized peer and, for work, the work record. Requires read:remote, the scope remote.peers.list and remote.work.list require.

events.title: Session Lifecycle Update
events.description: Shared-session lifecycle broadcast. Every session created / closed / deleted / reopened / agent-bound / agent-completed / message-appended / message-forwarded / route-attached and every input & follow-up lifecycle transition is published on the single `session-update` wire event; the specific lifecycle name is the discriminated `payload.event` field. Cross-surface invalidation mapping (webui/TUI): created ⇐ session-created; updated ⇐ session-permission-mode-changed / session-message-appended / session-agent-completed / session-route-attached / session-detached / session-reopened; steered ⇐ session-input-queued-for-surface / session-input-delivered / session-message-forwarded; closed ⇐ session-closed; deleted ⇐ session-deleted. A deleted session is a hard removal: the record is gone, not merely closed. Domain-tagged `session` (gateway-scope-enforcement.ts EVENT_DOMAIN), the same tag control.hosted_session_update carries: both are session lifecycle, so a client that narrows with ?domains=… must include `session` to receive EITHER of them, and one that opted into no narrowing receives both. It is dropped entirely when the control-plane-gateway flag is turned off (no phantom buffering).

events.title: Surface Message
events.description: Out-of-band control-plane surface messages for operators and connected clients. Each carries the message text, so it needs read:transcripts, as control.messages.list does.

peer.relationship: paired device and node-host peers use a separate peer contract surface
